summary: {F-CS-10210072} Mobiile Rider:  Incorrect forward hostname
description:
Mobile Rider is reporting an issue on the account LiveBarn, Inc.

On [cdn-akamai-livebarn.akamaized.net|https://cdn-akamai-livebarn.akamaized.net/] v18, they changed the cache key hostname to incoming host header.

After activating v18, they experienced a spike in traffic to origin and SSL handshake errors.

Checking the logs, before v18 was activated, we observed [origin-i-07f3e478b1395fc3a.livebarn.com|https://origin-i-07f3e478b1395fc3a.livebarn.com/] in both ARL and forward ARL. (line 144 for a request)

[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10210072]

While during the issue, we observed [cdn-akamai-livebarn.akamaized.net|https://cdn-akamai-livebarn.akamaized.net/] (line 62 for a request) there which caused the errors as it's not in the Match CN list on the property.

[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10210072]

The forward hostname was changed from [origin-i-07f3e478b1395fc3a.livebarn.com|https://origin-i-07f3e478b1395fc3a.livebarn.com/] to [cdn-akamai-livebarn.akamaized.net|https://cdn-akamai-livebarn.akamaized.net/] after activating v18.

Customer rollback to previous version to fix the issue.  

 

However, they recreated the configuration in a test configuration and were able to replicate this behavior. 

From the test configuration we can see in Edge logs that the forward hostname is the same as the client request Host header. 

The Edge is going forward to MCH but also to Origin based on object status field.

executive_summary:
- incorrect foward hostname
From v17 to v18 they have changed the origin host from PMUSER_IP to AK_HOSTHEADER. 

If Cache Key Hostname is set to Incoming Host Header in PM, Cache Key Host Name will be taking priority while setting value for OriginServer. The Customer with single origin DNS domain name might host Virtual domains and we cache based on incoming host to avoid cache collision while maintaining forward domain same for all. If origin domain changes based on incoming thats a problem.
This needs additional review with the portal architect teams. Further tracking this under the portal dev ticket
root_cause: From v17 to v18 they have changed the origin host from PMUSER_IP to AK_HOSTHEADER. If Cache Key Hostname is set to Incoming Host Header in PM, Cache Key Host Name will be taking priority while setting value for OriginServer.
creator: Cesar Roque Quiros

longterm_mitigation: Follow-up on https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/PRTLDEVOPS-82859

description:

Account:  Fubon Multimedia Technology Co., Ltd 
PM configuration: cart.momoshop.com.tw version 10

executive_summary:
The issue is client source port is logged as 443 instead of one from an ephemeral port range between 1024 and 65535. hence the 3rd party WAF is denying the traffic on port 443, 
The issue is only reproducible on QUIC,

There were some updates to the QUIC, we are analyzing the issue, we may have to wait for a release to get this fixed hence we suggested to check with customer to disable the QUIC and they agreed to disable the Http3 and cname to akamai. We will share the ETA as soon as possible. 

Ghost release has been world deployed now.
root_cause: The issue was client source port is logged as 443 instead of one from an ephemeral port range between 1024 and 65535. Client source port being forwarded to origin server as 443 which is being extracted from the AK_CLIENT_PORT built-in Variable at the client request stage and passed over the request header as Gclientport to origin server. There were some updates to the QUIC, which caused this issue,
creator: Suman Mishra
mitigation_plan: Disabled QUIC
longterm_mitigation: Ghost release 22.2.4.1 with the proposed fix.

summary: Edgeworker component returned 403 for translate requests
description:
Followup from https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/SYSPURGSUP-301

SRE has done investigation here https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/METAOPS-9833

 
We were requested to escalate this to ERE (ghost serv perf) to identify the root cause

-----------

Account: Salesforce Inc., BT Developer (F-AC-5054360)
Impacted URLs:
[https://staging.developer.salesforce.com/quests/quests-past.json]
[https://staging.developer.salesforce.com/quests.json]
Impacted user: ssukumaran@salesforce.com

Customer is reporting they're being to invalidate the URLs inconsistently from the Control Center tool.

The customer confirmed they are on the same account when both successful and failed attempt happen.
This is replicable when internal users attempt to purge the URL as well.
The customer has given us permission to replicate this issue.

Does not match the cause of intermittent failures found on [https://community.akamai.com/customers/s/article/Fast-Purge-Intermittent-failure-with-403-Unauthorized-or-Request-not-allowed] as I do not see any recent activations for the config.

In the failed attempt, we saw the Fast Gate logs below (SCT job [https://sct-aps.akamai.com/sct/purgelogs/af4be7/):]
2025-08-05 17:12:59.294 W piup-Enhvr6vrcdies5FfMANxrP req.xlate error:"'Could not translate arl [https://staging.developer.salesforce.com/quests/quests-past.json:] No parsable X-Ak-Translate line'", type:URL, duration:151.081409ms
2025-08-05 17:12:59.294 E piup-Enhvr6vrcdies5FfMANxrP http.errorHandler workflowError:"unauthorized arl: [https://staging.developer.salesforce.com/quests/quests-past.json]"
2025-08-05 17:12:59.294 W piup-Enhvr6vrcdies5FfMANxrP resp.body
{"httpStatus":403,"detail":"https://staging.developer.salesforce.com/quests/quests-past.json","supportId":"piup-Enhvr6vrcdies5FfMANxrP","title":"unauthorized arl","describedBy":"https://developer.akamai.com/api/core_features/fast_purge/v3.html#httpcodes"}
These errors aren't observed in the succesful attempt ([https://sct-aps.akamai.com/sct/purgelogs/3ccf2b/]).

Both successful and failed attempts came from the same Edge IP, so this doesn't appear to be caused by Origin Access Control.

We had told customer to follow the mitigation steps from the following KB (they're yet to add the "Request Method IS NOT AKAMAI_PURGE" exception and confirm if they allowlisted the Purge IPs from origin). However, I couldn't find a valid reason for the response inconsistency.
[https://community.akamai.com/customers/s/article/403-Unauthorized-Purge]

This issue is impacting other users as well: [https://control.akamai.com/apps/event-viewer/#/?state=89EqMyJ9sgKMOVDg0ocJHUhzKTKvOh0QBhyAHkCIAVzLEgDvxEjpTGoGSGrKTguqR-io6YihiEhs6UmtqgGKJ-wKKImqCChhiCmpYanqbcpN7woxSg1I6WhxAgHCAmFhwqFiIeZBwcMYGEHBmAHHDuANCEZWNmMAFrb3Itcipk6jAiLDAmIYwkI5LwhH7GXKDchqROhRCkjI6iFqqGhpIAtgBQ@&clientId=6dbc7e56-850e-4507-86c0-6ddf51ced0e9]

1. Requests with 000 status code are attached local thread mtse=tl waiting for the global thread to complete -  multipurpose field with latched req ID as well ( mtse=tl|4202290206|15d2faf4 ). 
2. Forward failure happens with SSL timeouts and this closes the connection - cache.log with EOF logged and 000 with read error. 
3. Another forward request post read error initiated - logs shows same req ID with obj status F' if the request failed Sureroute parent type (from the list above) and is successful at edge. 

It looks like the behavior is due to the nature of mtse with Failaction combined together. So any requests that falls and fails between them likely get logged with 000/ERR_READ_ERROR. 

Log data in https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10202890

Questions to ERE:
1. As per log format, Multi-Threaded Store Entry debug field. The format of the field is mtse=[g|tl]|swapfilenum. Where 'g' indicates global, and 'tl' indicates thread local. Added under CR 2888067.; added in ghost 7.1.2. But few log lines have reqID mtse=[g|tl]|swapfilenum|reqID - Is this a new format added recently?
2. Becaue of mtse , there seems to a potential problem of read error for all the requests latched in. Is there a better approach or solution that can be done to avoid 000 response? 

Usually we would expect to see 0/5xx error downstream if master request fails so that fail-action kicks in(if configured). But with 000 response this won't work.
executive_summary:
The format of appending original request id in f70 after mtse=[g|tl]|swapfilenum is introduced recently, please refer https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/GREL-3842

Request ID 15d2faf4 went from edge to MCH and then to origin SS, further going forward to a260.chausf.akamai.net from edge and ultimately served 200. Hence the request flow makes sense to me while the 2nd leg of that same request ID 15d2faf4 that completes for the total object size, seems correct but just does not show fail action…. so likely something breaking with obj status logging because while walking through the request, it actually makes sense.

Additionally, to avoid 000, suggested to  try an OS failover for the original request.
root_cause: NA, it seems like the latched requests might be waiting on MTSE and got an err_read_error , client does seem to retry and succeed, here we have 000 before the client succeed only, hence we should be good here.

summary: Local Loopback address 127.0.0.1/127.0.0.2 logged for client/origin causing multiple issue behaviors
description:
Ctrip.com reported their DS2 logs contains midgress logs despite not enabled in config. Upon further checking those requests have origin IP showed as 127.0.0.2 and the Client IPs are 127.0.0.1 which seems to be unusual. The issue resolved on its own and happened only for a brief period.

There was a FF release and CDN Request Loop Protection Enforcement was stalled after phase 1 during this period.
https://release.akamai.com/ui/networks/FF/releases/18157 - world deployed on 2025-08-11
https://ac-aloha.akamai.com/home/ls/community/gs-announcements-community/post/6738924009322321
https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/CHREG-1364

It has come to our notice that other customers have been affected by different issue behaviors with such logging anomaly. I have  consolidated them under https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LDPnbPqgsn9glYlvv9TrrE5uwOa6zJa6BiAGx0bm1I0/edit?usp=sharing

Need ERE's assistance in confirming the reason behind this logging anomaly and if its related to the above release ?
resolution_description: Issue Investigated.Escalated to SR Team as there is nothing pending from ERE Side.
root_cause: All the affected customers are sharing the same SR map ID (210007109), and the origins that do not have custom map rules fall under this SR map ID range - ProxyEcorV4..
creator: Senthilkumar Rajendiran

summary: {F-CS-10246873} Duplicate headers added at the edge itself
description:
Hi Team, 

From the PM configuration Modify outgoing response header is added for the CSP, STS and other headers. 

PM config: sit-x.nab.com.au v187
Issue started since on 1st of August 
changes which were done: they migrated from ION Premier to ION Standard and changed Site-shield map and sureroute.
current SS map: s4278.akamaiedge.net
old SS map: s365.akamaiedge.net
URL to test: [https://sit-x.ewcs.extnp.nab.com.au/joinnab/ui-find-your-business/sit5/asset-manifest.json]
this is UAT site so we only have 2 IPs whitelisted and those are of LSG2 and LSG3 if needed to test (having said that we were unable to reproduce the issue)

one header metadata snippet which is added in the config to be passed over to client and xml view below for same: 
{code:java}
            <comment:note value="Start Feature modifyOutgoingResponseHeader"/>
            <match:request.type value="CLIENT_REQ">
                <edgeservices:modify-outgoing-response.remove-header name="AKA_PM_X-Frame-Options">

                    <status>on</status>
                    <edge-only>on</edge-only>

                    <name>X-Frame-Options</name>
                    <value>DENY</value>
                    <status>on</status>
                    <edge-only>on</edge-only>
                </edgeservices:modify-outgoing-response.add-header>
            </match:request.type>

Customer reported of seeing duplicate headers and first we were under the impression it is due to the header added by ICP peer https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/GREL-3963 

however investigating we could see request is not going forward to the ICP peer and from the edge directly to the origin. 

Added debug header 55, 11, 58 level 10 and GRN to capture the request id in header as customer only able to reproduce the issue.

After adding GRN we could see duplicate of the GRN header as well.

executive_summary:
Duplicate headers added at the edge itself, Customer migrated from ION premier to standard, since then they are seeing this issue,
As per the given logs, We do see that edge and parent is in a same region resulting in "ERR_DNS_IN_REGION" and it seems limited to Prefresh only. Hence we disabled the prefresh and it improved the condition, 
While further investigation, we could could it performed CLIENT_RESPONSE stage twice. Hence raised a ghost ticket https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/GHOST-6738 for long term fix. The MC with fix has been implemented https://www.nocc.akamai.com/manual_change/view.cgi?id=15281 and can see that the headers are not duplicate here. Now it will go through the usual life cycle and then will get mapped to a release.
root_cause: We identified that the issue of client-response metadata being executed twice has re-emerged.
creator: Suman Mishra
mitigation_plan: Suggested to disable prefresh as a short term mitigation
longterm_mitigation: Raised a ghost ticket to check the triggering of client response twice

summary: Peer caches incomplete gzip object when parent to origin transfer gets interrupted
description:
Customer reported partial objects being served for some users in Asia. Reviewing logs, we see the following behavior. 
* Edge gets a request from the client, goes forward to the origin through the parent, and receives it uncompressed.
* Edge receives a request from a peer for the same object, which it compresses and serves the object as it receives from the origin (through the parent).
* While it serves to peer and the original client, the transfer gets interrupted between parent and origin, so the edge stops receiving the object; however, it was able to check that the object doesn't match content-length, so it discards the object.
* In the meantime, the peer that receives the compressed object doesn't get the content length, as it was receiving it in chunks. It caches it, not knowing about the interruption.

This appears to be very similar to GHOST-5795.

Additional logs from line 208 in a separate etherpad: https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10249547-2

It's important to note that this issue so far has only being seen when there's slowness between parent and origin. We believe the slowness is due to the long distance, however this bug should be resolved to prevent this issue from happening in the future if there were to be any slowness, even from a local parent. IAT is working with the customer to move them to a US based parent map. 

Since the issue seems to be happening when the edge compresses the object when serving it to peer without CL header, we've suggested disabling compression between edge servers as recommended at the bottom of this [article|https://akamai.lightning.force.com/lightning/articles/Knowledge/Akamai-servers-are-caching-truncated-incomplete-objects-because-of-data-corruption-when-using-chunked-transfer-encoding]. 

While we're discussing these options with the customer, is there something else that we can do to mitigate the issue? Given that this is impacting Oracle Cloud, can we get the GHOST JIRA expedited, if we can confirm it's the same issue?
Let us know if you need any further information/ analysis from us. Debug logging is not possible given that the issue is hard to reproduce. To reproduce, the connection to the origin has to get interrupted and the edge has to go forward to the peer while the peer is receiving data from forward side.
executive_summary: Customer reported Asia users intermittently getting partial objects. Reviewing the logs, we see that the edge was serving incomplete bytes to the client. Further analysis showed that there was an interruption on the forward side when the edge was compressing and serving that object to the peer without CL header.

summary: {F-CS-10284284} - OPTIONS method taking higher response times than usual compared to other methods
description:
Domain: futures.mexc.com
Issue:
Customer has reported high latency on specific paths, primarily affecting HTTP OPTIONS requests, while other methods such as GET and POST are performing normally. There is no specific timeframe mentioned by customer for when the issue started but with their recent internal performance review, they found their KPI seems affected. 

With Initial findings, Akatec thought this could be related to recent platform change to prevent request smuggling via request body for OPTIONS requests, we turn PCONN Off for G2G/G2O and terminate C2G connection

_This way OPTIONS request with body is contained to not share connections, and will be contained. Since OPTIONS with body will have no pconn, they will be slower than other requests. However, OPTIONS are < 1% of all C2G requests, and OPTIONS with body is even rarer. So we do not anticipate any KPI issues
_
 
See: https://collaborate.akamai.com/confluence/spaces/MDE/pages/1197862667/Rollout+PCONN+OFF+for+OPTIONS+method+with+Body

But looks like its not the case here since OPTIONS method doesn't match the rollout criteria match of CL >0 and Transfer-Encoding : Chunked - Confirmed from logs and ACC security reports. PCONN is used in C2G and G2G.
https://control.akamai.com/apps/security-analytics?accountId=F-AC-2524708&contractTypeId=1-5G3LB&configSelector=89790&view=&hash=22e40a5b-b801-4a8e-9a10-5664fa9ec8d9



[atan@lsg-gss3 ~]$ zcat CP1289562-202508250100-23.33.25.197-775-1756089235.gz | cc_log_convert | awk '$2=="f" && $13=="OPTIONS" {print $9}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -10
  29886 0


Analysis in Etherpad: https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10284284

Need ERE's assistance in finding the root cause for higher Request End Times that causing the delay for customer's API calls and why specially OPTIONS.
executive_summary: Customer has reported high latency on specific API paths, primarily affecting HTTP OPTIONS requests, while other methods such as GET and POST are performing normally. Customer is highly sensitive to latency due to the nature of their business.
creator: Senthilkumar Rajendiran

summary: {F-CS-10264671} ghost truncates html with boomerang injection and BOTF
description:
Hi ERE Team, Property: Sky_Community (version 34 Production) When we request the following object through Akamai with mPulse injection and BOTF, ghost returns a truncated html: {code:java}  msiemczo@krk-mpb5q ~/Documents/_lsg6_backup $  curl -D - -H "User-Agent: testFBANtest" -H "Accept-encoding: gz, br" -o sky_page.br "https://community.sky.de/conversations/sky-q-sky-q-mini/sky-q-receiver-fehler-16120/6835ed72170e725f31f12533?commentId=6835fe06170e725f3127f479"   msiemczo@krk-mpb5q ~/Documents/_lsg6_backup $  brotli -d sky_page.br    msiemczo@krk-mpb5q ~/Documents/_lsg6_backup $  cat sky_page| tail -2   

Liken

Antwort

vor 6 Jahren

0

A
                                  %     {code}   (full test results in https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10264671 from line 156 onwards) I am only seeing this issue for that particular html. {*}Note that the original html is bad - it has multiple sets of and tags. Boomerang is injected multiple times - in every {*}. But that itself +does not break+ the page. It seems the issue happens only in a specific corner case - when ghost both decompresses br from origin and then compresses back to br after (multiple) injection: * BOTF is enabled and client advertises br * origin also responds br * multiple injections happen   The issue is NOT seen if: * I set my config to strip Accept-Encoding from forward and I fetch non-br from the origin. Ghost fetches non-br, makes multiple injections, compresses to br and serves - no truncation * Obviously, if client does not advertise br, then also no issue. * When I test with a _valid html_ (single tag, meaning single mPulse injection). Ghost fetches br from origin, makes one injection, serves br to client - no truncation.   *ASK:* *Can we get this checked? Or will we not support this on account of customer's html not complying with the standard?*  *Or do you think something else besides bad html syntax could be triggering this truncation?* We did ask the customer to fix their html, which they say will be difficult. We also suggested to inject boomerang at the origin, or to strip br from origin forward as mitigation. Response pending.
creator: Marta Siemczonek

summary: OPTIONS method taking higher response times than usual after Aug 5/6
description:
This issue is similar to https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/ERE-2920  - > Customer has reported high latency on specific paths, primarily affecting HTTP OPTIONS requests, while other methods such as GET and POST are performing normally. 

For this customer, we are looking non- cacheable content and customer’s only origin is in US. The workflow is from AU client -> AU edge -> US parent -> US origin, so latency is expected for such distance, however the most concern is why it suddenly increased after Aug 5/6th as it is impacting their client and current latency is a show stopper.

[~trthomas] found that The G2G SSL times are high as compared to end user SSL times and it is being reflected in the SNId component (r 88) . It isn't restricted to OPTIONS method only but not sure why the KPI degradation is specific to OPTIONS . Requested to escalate to ERE-Ghost to understand the root cause of this issue suspecting SNId issue.

summary: Increased Traffic to Origin from QMX files
description:
The customer recently experienced a service impact which was not caused by Akamai.  However, during their investigation, it was observed that there was a higher then expected number of hits and potentially bytes going back to their origin.  This concern forced them to reduce traffic on Akamai resulting in a 250K a month revenue impact.

As mentioned above, the high traffic was observed to be associated with Cache Prefresh to a specific file extension (QMX).  We believe we tracked the issue to an unexpected behavior within the AMD configuration which kept cache prefetch enabled for file extensions associated with linear streaming.

Configuration has honor origin cache control header feature enabled and has set a ttl of 2s for qmx files. 
Logs indicate we are going forward to the origin every ~1s or more. We are not sure when the issue began and has potentially have been there all along. 

For a 1 minute timeframe we can see there were a total of 84 200s, in all cases the ghost request included the HTTP If-Modified-Since to the origin.
{code:java}
[tdeary@lsg-gss7]$ zcat  CP605537-202507282000-23.33.25.197-358-1753832692.gz | grep "15803/live/WESTRPL/b1de0a346b9711f0bca2ad1f714e0ae1/index_v5.qmx" | awk '$2~/f/ && $3>1753732804 && $3<1753732865 && $19~/o/ && $15==200 {print $17}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn                                                                        
     84 i

Logs
tdeary@lsg-gss7 - CP605537-202507282000-23.33.25.197-358-1753832692.gz
[https://qssi.akamai.com/cgi-bin/qgrep_ui/qgrep.pl?screen=detail&detail=CP605537-202507282000-23.33.25.197-358-1753832692]
Etherpad
[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10197973_ERE]

IAT reviewed this with EA and we have the following feedback
 # media_amd_pearls_v2.xml  disables cache prefresh for live manifests (line 813).  The qmx extension initially doesn’t seem to be accounted for as this is part of a legacy ABR technology associated with Move Networks.  In general, it seems to make sense to disable prefresh for this file.  *Need to confirm if AMD should recognize this as part of live manifest workflow as it is generally a ABR technology that is proprietary now to SlingTV (Dish).*
 # Another observation is that cache prefresh doesn’t effectively work with honor origin cache-control and expire headers.  *As this is set in the Caching property manager module, should AMD account for this as it is selectively updating cache prefresh logic.*  This caching behavior is currently set on the Dish (SlingTV) configurations.  However, we are still executing cache prefresh.  Details of the issue is outlined in the tech docs.
 [https://techdocs.akamai.com/property-mgr/docs/cache-prefresh-refresh]

We have deployed a fix on Akamai staging to address this issue which is the following metadata tags in advanced override.  *Is this a reasonable approach?* *Or is there something else recommended with the interactions of the AMD optimizations?*

 
{code:java}
<cache:prefresh
<status>off</status>
</cache:prefresh>
{code}
 

Currently there is a delay for the customer deployment.  They are currently under an infrastructure moratorium at this point. However, the IAT wants to confirm we are safe to move forward with the fix when they finish their origin upgrades which is slated to complete mid-September. 

This was also escalated to Alex Balford in Products and it was suggested to have ERE/SRE engagement on this revenue impacting issue. The request is to have a ERE/SRE case to stay open until we can confirm reduction of traffic to origin as well as keep Product engaged regarding the issue as there is revenue impact to the business.
executive_summary:
The high traffic was observed to be associated with Cache Prefresh to a specific file extension (QMX).
Configuration has honor origin cache control header feature enabled.
Disabling prefresh via metadata can be done, but disabling it via PM directly when the  CC headers are enabled, Akatec can try checking this with the Portal DevOps team.
But if this is the only customer facing this issue, so it is better to disable it for this particular customer instead of making the entire platform change.
root_cause:
The high traffic was observed to be associated with Cache Prefresh to a specific file extension (QMX).
Configuration has honor origin cache control header feature enabled and the document clearly tells about the incompatibility between the prefresh and the cache control headers.
creator: Tyler Deary
mitigation_plan: Disabling Prefresh
longterm_mitigation: Disabling Prefresh

summary: Playback errors due to ghost rolls and suspend flags
description:
Customer reported a spike of video playback re-buffering on Akamai in Georgia US for period on 08-27-2025 at 07:20 -07:30 GMT for the CP Code 1452205.

We performed client session analysis on the client IPs provided by customer and observed high turn around time. Further analysis shows that region 40517 was experiencing high flits along with First Byte Timeouts. 

NOCC team was consulted and ghost rolls suspend flags were observed during the issue timeframe for the region 40517 which could have caused the timeouts.


From region 360, we observed ghost rolls around the reported issue timeframe.

https://region360-aps.akamai.com/?inputValues=40517&startDateTime=2025-08-27%2001:49:09&endDateTime=2025-08-27%2004:49:09

Etherpad: https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10293209
NOCC Ticket: B-W-14IBJQR
Load graph - https://lg.netarch.akamai.com/cgi-bin/loadgraphs?period=1w®ion=40517&network=A&maprule=&display=total&ymax=&utcoffset=-4
Retransmit graph for region:
http://flames.akamai.com/~lichen/cgi-bin/ney/batchcon.py?mode=region&ids=40517

*From the Loadgraph for the above regions  could see around the same time maprule 7232 with spike and regions are under stress.* 

[https://lg.netarch.akamai.com/cgi-bin/loadgraphs?period=2d&region=35636+46866+43889+35636+44103&network=A&maprule=&display=maprule&ymax=&utcoffset=5]



[https://map.akamai.com/cgi-bin/FreeFlow/Analysis/HDB_Server.pl?startmonth=09&startday=03&startyear=2025&starthour=04&startmin=53&endmonth=09&endday=04&endyear=2025&endhour=04&endmin=53&param1=41492&dbname=production&display=graph&normalize=none&ptdisp=normal&yaxis=y-axis&size=large&scope=all&query_name=REGION_BY_MAPRULE_FLYTELOAD]

"{*}Possible Attack: High Origin Error Rate CP: SAPI - PROD - [secureapi.cricketwireless.com|https://secureapi.cricketwireless.com/]: (662738) on [Cricket Wireless LLC|https://control.akamai.com/apps/home-page/#/manage-account?accountId=F-AC-1370889]  Origin Responses: 0xx: 0.47M/sec 5xx: 0.15M/sec tot: 0.62M/sec "{*} 

from the traffic graph for this cpcode could see around the same time huge spike of traffic started flowing with 250k hits/second.  (screenshot attached)

checked estats for traffic and could see 100% failures for the cpcode- 662738 and tracing one of the requests could see requests being forward multiple times to the peer, parent and in loop beyond the default re-forwards. 

https://tools.gss.akamai.com/estats/estats.cgi?cpcode=662738®IP=&network=essl&type=midgress&zone=All&exclude=&limit=&Submit=Submit

[https://tools.gss.akamai.com/art/#0.8c1ddf17.1756968000.7ca9cd6c]  

(logs are more than 1k and hence the art tool most likely will crash) added few sample logs for same request id in etherpad line 472)

from the config secureapi.cricketwireless.com v1036 could see that they have setup origin as [127.0.0.1|https://127.0.0.1/] with forward hostname as incoming hostname. 

Based on the traffic we can see that already 4-5 US regions are under stress and causing Sony traffic as well to be impacted. 

Customer IAT is available during US hours and as this is impacting our platform is there any interim fix that we can perform to ensure that this would not cause any further impact and fix the impact on Sony traffic seen.
root_cause: Misconfig in one of CricketWireless properties started amplifying localhost requests, resulting in memtotaled SS regions.
creator: Suman Mishra
mitigation_plan: CricketWireless fixed their property.

While the customer migrates this Ion traffic to CW web map, can the VR limit be increased to prevent this issue short term?

summary: Stale metadata "Include" file change on multiple regions
description:
This is a stale metadata issue on ghost. Going by ERE-1168 it wouldn't fall within ERE scope. If that's the case that would be the correct escalation path?. Would also appreciate any help/feedback on why  it the change didn't reflect on the machines if possible.

====
 
Customer: Bank of Montreal - EP-2LU
 
*Context on setup:*
Customer uses "Property Manager Includes(FCM)" module to enable maintenance mode on their domain
*Main Property:* usdigital.bmo.com_pm v58
[https://tower-ui.akamai.com/file?fileNo=859976&channelName=arl.data&page=1&page_size=25&selectedPosition=end&end_time=2025-08-29%2021%3A42%3A34]
*Include Property/file (the one with the issue):* usdigital.bmo.com_maintenance
[https://tower-ui.akamai.com/file?fileNo=933510&channelName=arl.data&page=1&page_size=25&selectedPosition=end&end_time=2025-08-29%2009%3A23%3A09] 
Usually they flip flop between v6 (normal traffic) and v7 (var MAINTENANCE_MODE=PlANNED) of the include file to toggle maintenance on their domain
 
*The maintenance only triggers on certain paths and only for mobile devices:*
/www/
/www/index.html
/sso-login/
/sso-login/index.html
/api/*
/aac/*
/common/maintenance/ak_config.js
 
Depending on the path they'll usually get a 503 response from the edge and we redirect them to *"/common/maintenance/"  (when maint enabled v7).*
**

*Problem:* 

On Aug 27th they pushed v7 of the include property for routine maintenance and then rolled back to v6 like they've done multiple times before on other occassions. On Aug 28th once their normal traffic picked up (when the day started), they noticed a lot of users still going to maintenance unexpectedly.
 * Issue persisted until they did a no-op update in the include property(v6 to v11). As soon as v11 went live the machines stuck on maintenance mode (v7) started to work again.
 * For a failing machine, logs show it was sending 100% of users to maintenance even though v6 of the include property (maintenance disabled) was active at the time. WSA reports and response headers support this. 
 ** [https://control.akamai.com/apps/security-analytics?accountId=EP-2LU&contractTypeId=1-2RBL&configSelector=88793&view=&hash=b3359d58-cbe3-42ac-830b-aeba88618fe0]

====

Based on all the analysis multiple regions/machines definitely held on to stale metadata of the include file (v7). We unfortunately don't have mdtagent logs from when it happened to figure out what went wrong.

Full details here:
[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/ER-247889]

There was an ongoing install on many of the top failing regions/IPs.

Not all impacted IPs had received the install or were suspended when they switched  back from v7 to v6 to disable maintenance, but many of the top offending IPs were, which seems too like too much of a coincidence. You can check etherpad from line 663 for those details.

I know it's a long shot with no mdtagent logs to check, but again any feedback would be appreciated. NOCC ticket is also being filed  to get their input.

Further log analysis showed below.
 * No logs were found on NSDS for #2 and #3
 * No issues were found on NSDS
 * Checking 200 response logs, NSDS is responding perfectly to any requests made by MCH machines
 * Configuration has Tiered Distribution enabled using property manager behavior. Below metadata (policy=tiered-distribution) was found which explains why reforwards went to NSDS

{code:java}
[yiguchi@lsg-gss16 ~/sony]$ cat printmetadata.txt | grep cache-parent.policy
X-Akamai-Metadata3: forward:cache-parent.policy=fail-over [S] [baseline|baseline-hacks.xml] : [73]
X-Akamai-Metadata3: forward:cache-parent.policy=tiered-distribution [S] [pearldata|web_common_pearls.xml] : [152] {code}
_tiered-distribution: go to the parents first and contact the origin server directly only if the parents fail to respond._

[https://docs.akamai.com/esp/user/edgesuite/guides/metadata.htm#50638876_forward+cache-parent.policy]
h1. Ask
 # My understanding is that requests going to NetStorage should go through parent ghost to prevent NetStorage overload. Why is PM behavior not designed in such way?
 # Are there any PM behavior that would enable the use of alternate MCH map for forward MCH failure? (like how they do in quick-retry for media products)
 # Are there any know issues that would cause NSDS to drop requests coming from ESSL edge?

Etherpad: [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10328210] (line 220 and beyond)
executive_summary:
Edge directly going forward to NetStorage after Edge to MCH failure
As the download delivery property is used to access NS, suggested them to validated the health and connectivity of the NS replicas to see if there's an issue.

It was discovered that the problematic URL had a space (" ") within the query parameter which was not URL-encoded. NSDS does not support such character thus URL parse failed resulting in the error.
root_cause: The problematic URL had a space (" ") within the query parameter which was not URL-encoded. NSDS does not support such character thus URL parse failed resulting in the error.

summary: Token revocation doesn't work as the asynchronous revalidation doesn't go outside of the region
executive_summary:
I did check random multiple requests and it seems like the issue is happening with every prefresh requests. 
Raised a DPEREQ ticket https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/DPEREQ-372 to review the prefresh (e.g. disable), cc metadata of the TAAS property.
We can continue to do our follow-up on DPEREQ ticket.
root_cause: Token revocation doesn't work as the asynchronous revalidation doesn't go outside of the region, since the jitter is disabled, I do see that the issue is happening for all the prefresh requests. Hence raised a DPEREQ ticket to review the Prefresh in TAAS config.

summary: {F-CS-10327379} - Midgress SSL errors due to 2048 sflags
description:
The customer has reported several instances of SSL error spikes across multiple days. They all show up as midgress errors. They  use the same SS map across multiple domains/properties:

 
 * Sample Domain: [services.publix.com|https://tools.gss.akamai.com/ip-host-search/?ipaddress=services.publix.com]
 * SiteShield Map: s1345.akamaiedge.net

 *   There's always high load from maprule 1039 e;ch39.akamaiedge.net (presumably tiktok)

summary: High request end time due to metadata application time
description:
ABN Amro has reported a sudden spike in request end time.

+*Details:*+
Account: ABN AMRO Bank N.V. (1-16JMZM0)
Hostname: www.abnamro.nl
Configuration: [www.abnamro.nl|http://www.abnamro.nl/]
Timeframe: *Sep 10, since 05:30 until around 11:00* when the region was suspended.
Impact: *r48545,* specifically ABN's traffic was on *2.20.138.90 and 2.20.138.96*

 

Customer has escalated this as continuation of the ERE-2888 issue, but actually we're not seeing the same symptoms:
seeing no drop of flits, no suspension flags, no stalled threads, loadgraphs well within margin.

The traffic level on was following the daily pattern (early stage of ramping up for the day). But as of *05:28:50* there was a sharp jump in request end time which sustained at high level (strictly a ret spike - dns and ssl were steady)

!image-2025-09-18-20-12-28-884.png|width=923,height=603!

[https://pliny-aps-viz.akamai.com/kibana2/goto/39ed04a0-9232-11f0-909f-937bd8884061]

 

I checked the full traffic on those two machines: seeing the exact same deterioration pattern as [www.abnamro.nl|http://www.abnamro.nl/] also on {*}api.airbnb.com, www.airbnb.com, www.airbnb.it{*}. But lots of other hostnames had no deterioration at all.

 

Avg request end time:

!image-2025-09-18-20-12-59-548.png|width=1018,height=720!

[https://pliny-aps-viz.akamai.com/kibana2/goto/8826ce30-9232-11f0-909f-937bd8884061]

2.20.138.90 has since then updated to 22.2.4.1, but at the time of the issue I believe both machines were on 22.2.3

I did not see any pattern in terms of mle, client ASnum etc. We're checking with NOCC to rule out any network issues, but seeing how impact pattern is so clearly by hostname, I wouldn't expect network to be the issue.

 

+*Ask to ERE:*+

*Can you help us understand the reason for this bad perf deterioration? Currently the region remains suspended, we need to get to the bottom of the issue to safely restore traffic.*

 

Etherpad at [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10225588_1] from line 120

summary: Pristine Failures During Asia Cup Due to High TD/OS Load from APIx Traffic
description:
During the Asia Cup 2025 – India vs. Pakistan match on 21st Sept, we observed multiple 0xx ERR_SSL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT | SSLTimeout spikes on the MT Pristine workflow, resulting in 503 errors being served to MT polling agents. Please refer below screenshot:

!image-2025-09-22-15-53-31-892.png|width=706,height=429!

Upon investigation, we found that:
 * Timeouts were occurring across multiple TD/OS regions.
 * There was a significant spike in APIx traffic in these regions.
 * Using APIx Edge Maps (dscapi) and Pristine Edge Map (dscz), we identified overlapping regions with TD (387) and OS (4498) maps.
 * In particular, regions with TD map chc1 (387) showed heavy flit-intensive spikes driven by APIx traffic.
 * From the logs, the errors are associated with SSL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT, likely due to high flits.
 * Traffic distribution analysis shows that APIx maps dominated traffic across the affected TD/OS regions at the time of the spike.
 * To mitigate the impact, we suspended TD maprule 387 from the most impacted regions (43829 and 44365). After this action, no further spikes were observed.

executive_summary: During the Asia Cup 2025 – India vs. Pakistan match on 21st September, we observed multiple ERR_SSL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT errors on the MT Pristine workflow, resulting in 503 responses to polling agents. The issue was traced to high load on TD and OS regions, primarily driven by APIx traffic. executive_summary:
For the size of smaller than 860 bytes, compression should not be applied to these objects, as they can already be transferred in a single packet due to their small size.
lma.incoming will get inserted at client response stage, it seems like it will compress whenever it will get in the response. 
As per the metadata guide, it should have match conditions outside of 3xx

Raised DPEREQ ticket https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/DPEREQ-376 to review the pearl.xml

description:
Property: h55na.gph.easebar.com v23
Domain: h55na.gph.easebar.com

From the logs, we found that the 404s occurred because the forward ARL appended the base path twice, causing the origin to return 404 to Akamai Edge requests.

Prepend the incoming path is only applied in default origin rule and again in fail-action behavior

Path duplication happening on the forward request to origin
Investigated the request with error, looks like the "h55na.gph.netease.com" string is being added earlier in the request flow itself (before the last hop) to the 'ARL' field (f line).
On the other hand, in case of request without error, We see the string added to the 'Forward ARL just before the origin.
Requested this metadata <cache:poc2.make-masters-public-early> to be enabled. 
As there are multiple config so it seems difficult to apply it in an individual configuration,  requested here https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/LUNAPROESC-909 to modify the default logic from PM side.

resolution_description: None available in the short term.
root_cause: That's a known caveat. MCH and FA mapping using two different mapping strategies. The former relies on SRO, while the latter uses fallback mapping akin to RA mapping. There's no shared state of information between the two. The forward serial hashing for MCH and FA mapping use different serial ranges, but given a single machine serves multiple serials, this could still lead to corner cases where not just the parent region, but the same machine could be handed out for a small subset of requests leading to this behavior. FA/QR isn't expected to be 100% efficient with the current design. There are product level discussions on how to address these, but I don't expect this to change anytime soon.
creator: Dimitris Kim
mitigation_plan: n/a
longterm_mitigation: Products to review fallback mapping strategy. Options could include using second hop SRO for FA instead of SCM.

Please update the EIPB configuration to have a single cloud ({*}eip-terr-as{*}). Details below:

Account: Deutsche Bank AG Eschborn

EIPB Config Name: [dbdigitalonboarding-uat-db.com|https://dbdigitalonboarding-uat-db.com/]

 

*Context:*

Edge IP Binding provides a set of static Anycast IPs: 10 IPv4 addresses and several IPv6 CIDR blocks.

 

*Customer requirements:*

When the customer’s hostname is queried from a specified ASN, they aim to return only one of six predefined IPs for each IP version (IPv4 and IPv6).

This restriction is crucial because the customer cannot hardcode IPs in their environment (similar to manually editing the hosts file).

If DNS returns more than the limited set, the customer may receive IPs not whitelisted on their side, so simply providing a subset isn’t sufficient unless all possible IPs are whitelisted.

 

*Proposed Solution (Agreed by the customer):*

This EIPB config is expected to serve the clients only in Asia. So, we will configure EIPB  (IPv4-only) with a single cloud - Asia. The customer will get 2 IPv4 IPs, and that aligns with their expectations.

summary: CW Availability in BR - Packet Loss reported in GRU ecors
description:
Three ecors, SDN-GRU2, SDN-GRU3, FABRIC-GRU experienced packet loss due to the IEN sessions on their border routers hitting a maximum limit in the number of BGP prefix limits its allowed to be handled. When these limits were hit, the traffic for the ECORS was shifted to transit, which led to that transit being congested, which led to the packet loss that was observed.

Since 75% of CW capacity resides in these three ecors, this issue resulted in traffic being moved away from CW. There were SRO failed paths with 'No map in assignment msg' error logged, so increased traffic to origin due to RA fallback being used. There has been spike in Turnaround time due to this RA fallback mapping.
root_cause: IEN sessions on their border routers hitting a maximum limit in the number of BGP prefix limits its allowed to be handled. When these limits were hit, the traffic for the ECORS was shifted to transit, which led to that transit being congested, which led to the packet loss that was observed.
creator: Aruna Uthayakumar
mitigation_plan: Prefix limit has been increased to 1020000 on the impacted border routers.
longterm_mitigation: NOCC-facing alert which detects when a peer exceeds their route limit to take proactive action before the limits are hit.

summary: Perf improvement on AWS clients seeing high transfer times intermittently
description:
The customer reported intermittent high transfer times for some of their AWS requests from as early as July 2025, and possibly before that. Their expectation is for these API calls to take less than 500ms, but we're seeing requests take more than 4 seconds, and sometimes more than 10 seconds. 
Customer has [Trafficpeak monitoring |https://grafana-us.trafficpeak.live/d/f39dbf94-7a0d-42d0-aa01-e01190ad91fd/akamai-observability?orgId=160&from=now-1h&to=now&timezone=browser&var-statusCode=$__all&var-cacheStatus=$__all&var-reqHost=$__all&var-reqMethod=$__all&var-UA=$__all&var-rspContentType=$__all&var-errorCode=$__all&var-ServiceType=$__all&var-Partition=$__all&var-ServiceAPI=$__all&var-Env=$__all&var-GroupAPI=$__all&var-OperationAPI=$__all&var-AdditionalAPI=$__all&var-edge_response_time_percentile=$__all&var-reqPath=&var-cliIP=&var-transferTimeMSec_percentile=&var-cpCode=&var-Origin_IP=&var-queryStr=&var-epd_match=$__all&var-epd_category=$__all&var-epd_action=$__all&var-country=$__all&var-metric_name=$__all&var-metric_filter=$__all&var-metric_value=&var-x_end_user_time_zone=$__all&var-x_end_user_location=$__all](dashboard -> Principal -> Akamai Observability)
user: akatec-support
Password: ClaroVideo123!

We collected logs for a time period on Sept 22nd, and we can see some requests with transfer time > 4 seconds. Looking at the total hits, we had around 15 - 25k requests/ minute.  * We've opened [NOCC ticket B-W-15GLPOJ,|https://issues.deploy.akamai.com/cgi-bin/view.cgi?issue_id=B-W-15GLPOJ] where it was escalated to T3. NOCC responded that the region is a high AVG management cycle, with many flits, maximum CPU usage, and stuck threads. The mapper is sending more traffic than the region can actually handle, causing high transfer times.

Let us know if you need any other information.

case 1 - Dos attack - CRP can help in future

suggestion to try APIx to see if we can gain more consistent performance.

Background: Microsoft Xbox PC download client is experimenting where PC download client currently opens 8 concurrent threads/connections. This experiment ups that to default to 24 connections per client, and as part of their experiment, they will be dynamically adjusting the connection count from each device to a number between 4 and 32, adjusting up or down depending on what the client observes during the download.

Issue: While conducting the test, MSFT reported large stutters and drops in speeds across multiple test runs. This is happening specifically on Akamai and not on other CDNs

 

Test and Log Information:
Akamai IPs tested against: 2600:1460:10:1::1720:2ed8 and 23.32.75.17
Time Start: Sep 29, 2025 21:58:20.863218000 UTC
Time Stop: Sep 29, 2025 22:01:05.821185000 UTC
URI: [http://assets1.xboxlive.com/Z/b8965de6-14bc-4ca0-ada2-50ce5f3a2442/807c7d6a-409f-48be-8190-30b09baf7cd4/1.0.28720.0.be3df6f9-92a6-4d67-9344-fdedcbadd0bc/TeamCherry.HollowKnightSilksong_1.0.28720.0_x64__y4jvztpgccj42.msixvc]

IAT checked with Jain, Sandeep from Eng:
_From a brief review of the logs, it looks like over half of the requests that fail with ERR_READ_ERROR were cache hits at the edge. I don't see the machines running hot to able to explain these timeouts. It looks like this might've something to do with a race condition when multiple parallel requests are made for a POC object (GHOST-303)_

summary: {F-CS-10412036} - Edge not refreshing and keeping the object in cache for longer than expected
description:
* PM Config: images-ssl.amazon.com v323
 * Test URL: [https://a.media-amazon.com/images/S/mobile-weblab-allocations-prod/allocations/v2/prod/a]
 * Origin URL: [https://mediax.origin.media-amazon.com/images/S/mobile-weblab-allocations-prod/allocations/v2/prod/a]
 * Issue:

Customer has [this rule|https://control.akamai.com/apps/property-manager/#/property-version/10450260/323/edit?gid=14197&view=edit&rule=ed969a75-6e08-4ab3-bbb7-469b52be892b] in the PM Config, where forces Akamai to Honor origin Cache-Control and Expires.

The origin server is currently returning these headers:
{noformat}
[jugaldeg@lsg-gss7 ~]$ curl -s -S -IXGET "https://mediax.origin.media-amazon.com/images/S/mobile-weblab-allocations-prod/allocations/v2/prod/a"
HTTP/2 200 
date: Fri, 03 Oct 2025 21:26:38 GMT
content-type: text/plain
content-length: 2033624
server: Server
x-amz-ir-id: 2a0a83dd-6d04-46a8-b054-f2d2763f3f96
last-modified: Fri, 03 Oct 2025 21:25:28 GMT
cache-control: public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=900
x-amz-meta-checksum-rodb-sha256: ong5xjqrL0spSBNb3n/Lh6P23p1mzcbAlrdnvooGOzU=
edge-cache-tag: x-cache-596,/images/S/mobile-weblab-allocations-prod/allocations/v2/prod/a
surrogate-key: x-cache-596 /images/S/mobile-weblab-allocations-prod/allocations/v2/prod/a
x-nginx-cache-status: HIT
accept-ranges: bytes
{noformat}
As you can see, it's responding with the "cache-control: public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=900", so Akamai is supposed to cache this object for 60s.

Looking at the logs, we can confirm that the object max-age is 60s:

!Screenshot 2025-10-03 at 3.28.31 PM.jpg|width=347,height=72!

Sample log line:
{noformat}
23.221.215.142 S 1759185378.013 54 59 0 233 2029456 2029456 2031113 186.151.98.79 GET 1994 559332 media-origin-na.ssl-images-amazon.com 200 - mjuAeW text/plain - D 1 295 3508 - - - - orHK sgbr8 images/S/mobile-weblab-allocations-prod/allocations/v2/prod/a - a.media-amazon.com ^ - curl/7.71.1-DEV ^ ccbe08a - - 60 Hit%7c23.221.214.79 ^ - - ^ Catc_153034|| - ^ - ^ - - mid=3000;ocl=535104;mxc=//waf@ra/1/d/186.151.98.79;mtse=g|4294967295;pcf=//@tcp/24400FFFF205841306118400+0A\//@tls/286e0262e7deb748\//@tls3/3~f4680262e7deb748\//@ja4/t13d4807h2_d6740521f3cb_7395dae3b2f3;waf=|||||;wre=5%7c%7c8;sn=142214||142214|;aid=363151;cs=23.49.253.151|3|17ddd78e01962668|0|0|-|0|r2;cert=ecdsa-with-SHA384;gd=//0@0;reqb=//1/79516/e-a;dstr=//DS/-/0;pin=http|ion;alpn=h2;h2=15512964:1:0:15:0:0:0:31:0:0;aidv=323;cpu=//ctx@waf/2129/1363\//prod@aib/234\//prod@bm/44\//prod@bmi/54\//prod@sec/1396\//prod@sur/50;mle=32535;trno=0;af=0:16:0;vcd=2799;cta=1DCF|1D171819|8G6B6D8F5B5D8E4B4D2B2D - - ^ 1994.dscr 6505:191307:0:19 L1:L1:s:L1:: 1 - - 5b9927f - - 80794 40426 10008 4973 2653 - - - 23.221.215.143|1|2|1|1994|128|45007|16|0 - - ^{noformat}
The problem is, that Akamai is not refreshing with the origin server as often as it should.

The Origin "Last-Modified" value keeps changing automatically, and since Akamai is supposed to refresh every 60s after the TTL expires, it's expected that Akamai also serves the content with the updated "Last-Modified" value. However, this is not the case: Akamai continues serving stale content with stale "Last-Modified" for up to 1 hour or more.

For example, this was a test to Origin:
{noformat}
[jugaldeg@lsg-gss7 ~]$  for i in {1..100}; do    curl -s -S -IXGET "https://mediax.origin.media-amazon.com/images/S/mobile-weblab-allocations-prod/allocations/v2/prod/a" 2>/dev/null ; done | grep -i "last-modified" | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr

So Akamai doesn't refresh the content every 60s, as the cache-control from origin dictates.

IN PM config, we see the "cache:honor-expires" being applied:

!Screenshot 2025-10-03 at 3.41.45 PM.jpg|width=545,height=106!

At this time, su suggested the customer to remove the "stale-while-revalidate=900" from the origin cache-control directives, as they already have the behavior  "Force revalidation of stale objects: Serve stale if unable to validate", and also asked to include the "must-revalidate" in the cache-control directives, to force the revalidation after TTL expires.

However, since customer temp is increasing and we don't want this to get escalated, we request your help to determine why Edge is taking longer than expected to refresh content with Origin, as the TTL is 60s and it's supposed to revalidate with origin after TTL expires.
executive_summary:
The edge server oftentimes marks the resource as stale when it should and goes forward to validate, but a stale response is served from parent servers without validating with the Origin((particularly around the time we should validate), this could be because of the G2G age-jitter and some unintended interactions it can have because jitter can change the age by +- 10% of TTL up to 60s,

Suggested to disable jitter to the path "/images/S/mobile-weblab-allocations-prod/allocations/v2/prod/a" to force the jitter to be disabled and applied to those requests. This has been tested in Cloned (Test) Config. After the Cloned (Test) Config was pushed to both stag and prod, now we do se refresh_hit and refresh_miss matching the Last-Modified at origin

Right now, we're waiting for customer's approval to make the changes in the PRODUCTION PM Config
creator: William Ugalde

summary: {F-CS-10414672} mTLS Flow – Missing Trust Chain in Request to Origin
description:
Issue: The Trust Chain is missing in the Request to Origin when mTLS is enabled between G20.  

Details:
Account: SAP SE
Configuration: kobi-istio-cdn v8
Client certificate: kobi2new (Signed by Third-Party) - CURRENT

To capture the details of the request flow, the setup has Linode as the origin. In Pacp, we can see that when the negotiation happens, the Origin sends the complete chain, whereas the parent only sends the leaf. 

The customer has a strict requirement to validate the complete chain for a successful handshake. 


Pcap showing cert from Origin to Parent
 !image-2025-10-06-13-42-36-239.png|thumbnail! 

Pcap showing cert from Parent to Origin

description:
Account Name:  Directv LLC

Account ID : F-AC-1500804

 
On Sep 28, between 21:27 - 21:31 PT (04:25 - 04:35 UTC), DTV reported a rebuffering event. This was tracked under : #F-CS-10405730
Upon analysis it was observed that the rebuffering was mainly caused due to significant increase in HTTP 504s due to ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_|commConnectTimeout._ Based on the findings we reached out to the NOCC who confirmed that this was casued due to a maintenance activity that impacted the traffic path to the parent region that traversed through our backbon network.  More details, NOCC ticket for reference : #B-V-5WRIU0J

23.45.173.6 \{HERO} --> 23.32.154.6 (r38540)
[psalunke@lsg-gss12 /home/stilak]$ iptool 23.32.154.6
ES [r38540:FABRIC-LAXc] 23.32.154.6  \{ff_ghost}               (group 8)
Total: 1 machines
*Edge IP with the issue : [r50382]*
=================================
[psalunke@lsg-gss12 /home/stilak]$ iptool 23.220.202.8
ES [r50382:FABRIC-HOUo] 23.220.202.8  \{ff_ghost}              (group 2)
Total: 1 machines
 
The edge request reached out to the CW in LAX, and once it encountered an ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT, it failed over to the failover Map for CW i.e, ch492.
Upon reaching the request on the ch492 map, it again encountered an ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT due to which the failover was not successful leading to error being served downstream as 504 to the end-user.
On checking the logs, we see that below are the 2 regions which saw the failover requests that came to it once the problematic edge regions timed out with CW (due to ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT).
The CW, and failover TD both belonged to same ecor: 9015 and within the same location (LAX) due to which the failover could not succeed.
Ask: The ask from IAT who reached out to their EA and got a recommendation to check with the ERE if they can leverage any other map or use CW-East as failover mechanism to avoid such scenarios in future or any other insights which ERE provide that can be helpful to IAT.
resolution_description: Since this involves routers at two different metros of US, Networks team have to be consulted to understand the possibilities to gradually bringdown the requests well earlier to not pass through the ones which would be soon going down for any planned maintenance.
root_cause: Maintenance of two bundle routers brought them down which resulted in packet loss across the intermediate hops in the IxN path causing 504s errors downstream which lasted for approximately 1 minute. This happened because, when a bundle goes down, it typically takes a short interval recalculate and stabilize the path, which explains the observed behavior.

summary: AMD template max-reforwards limit impairs retries for ERR_PURGE_SEQ_OUT_OF_DATE
description:
The limits "forward:availability.max-reforwards=1" and "forward:availability.max-reconnects=1" tags in "delivery_amd_best_practices_v4.xml" reduce resiliency against purge sequence out-of-date conditions on both peer and parent nodes.

Review DELIVERENG-8153 as possible long term resiliency solution.
executive_summary:
we cannot adjust max-reforwards to 3 on all delivery products. Issue mentioned here is specific to last hop settings. max-reforwards can only be set in client-request where we don't know about whom the edge or parent is going to contact.  Ghost change should be tuned to set this setting when forward request is identified as origin.
Midhun raised a ghost ticket https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/GHOST-6934 for further analysis and work.
creator: Albert Yee

summary: CW config activation failing with Too many retries
description:
Customer: Shanghai Multibeauty Network Technology Co., LTD （tiktik）

Issue: CW Activation Failed
Error: Too many retries. Retry count exceeded max allowed retries

Check:
- There are no special characters found in the usage notes/comments.
- The activation time does not fall between 00:00 and 01:30 UTC, and the customer has retried several times but still encountered the same error.

Based on KB [000095214] 
[https://akamai.lightning.force.com/lightning/r/Knowledge__kav/ka3a7000000OQRBAA4/view , |https://akamai.lightning.force.com/lightning/r/Knowledge__kav/ka3a7000000OQRBAA4/view]the error observed in Splunk matches the one described in the KB (error=status 400, MROM error: Arl Id(s) 1251697 used in other fp configs).

Splunk Log: Line 17 - 53 in [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10469010|https://akamai.my.salesforce.com/servlet/servlet.ExternalRedirect?url=https%3A%2F%2Fetherpad.akam.ai%2Fp%2FF-CS-10469010]

Ask: It seems that this issue requires manual adjustment, as mentioned in the KB article. Could you please help to identify the root cause and advise on how we can fix it?
resolution_description: To resolve the issue, we removed the existing config (cw-s-use_cw-F-AC-4915861-CWSK) since it was unused. After that, we reactivated the intended config, and it successfully moved to the Active state.
root_cause: The root cause of the issue was identified as the arlId being already linked to another config: cw-s-use_cw-F-AC-4915861-CWSK. This config was an FPA config and was not in use, which is why we were receiving a 400 status error.
creator: Floyd Francis

executive_summary:
Nov 8:
Most of the action items for the incident have been completed, except for updating EdgeWorkers to prevent modification of "Akamai-Origin-Hop." This change is scheduled to go live (WD) on Nov 17.
Nov 13: No new updates
root_cause: In a two-tree config, the loopback (127.0.0.1) IP set as origin and discarded "Akamai-Origin-Hop" header resulted in request amplification within Midgress, Impacting SS regions.
creator: Suman Mishra
mitigation_plan: Disjointed Sony's SS map from the offending customer, CricketWireless and property optimization done for loopback-IP and AOH head for CW
longterm_mitigation:
Mostly here:
https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/ERE-3005#:~:text=added%20a%20comment%20%2D-,25%2DOct%2D25%2001%3A28%20AM,-Updating%20incident%20progress

Other customers with such setups have asked to update their property for honoring the header and the portal (MUI rules) and other products (like EW) updated to prevent future modification.

executive_summary:
ERR_PURGE_SEQ_OUT_OF_DATE errors after origin migration to GCP cloud interconnect. 
This error is by design, the ghosts are processing the requests as expected. It is meant to avoid serving stale content to end-users and update Akamai cache with fresh content , it is inline with maximizing offload and reducing requests to origin. 
We found that the customer is submitting constant cache-tag purges, often twice for same tag within same second, 

Hence suggested Akatec to check with customer - 
1. Remove Google Interconnect.
2. About the purge frequency

If adding CI to the configuration caused an increase in that error, then it is likely metadata related to CI that may have caused it. So, as we have recommended previously, CI product architect should review resiliency for purge seq. Further questions can be tracked with the CI/AppNetRE team.
root_cause:
w.r.t the purge, customer is submitting constant cache-tag purges, often twice for same tag within same second, suggested to check with the customer about the purge frequency and remove CI.
If you continue to purge all the time, FPJ will be behind all the time.  it will not be synchronised simultaneously on every single Ghost on the entire platform.
creator: Sameer Gupta
mitigation_plan: Removed CI and suggested to check with customer regarding the purge frequency.
longterm_mitigation: Removed CI and suggested to check with customer regarding the purge frequency.

summary: {F-CS-10468090} - ESI tags not parsed when br compression is done
description:
Account: Nestle Operational Services Worldwide S.A.

URL: https://www.pureencapsulationspro.com/our-products/health-categories/heart-metabolism.html

CPCode: 453463

We could see the ESI tags in the page source on the browser. 

<esi:include src="[/head.html|https://www.pureencapsulationspro.com/head.html]"/>

When testing the request on browser by forcing Accept-Encoding: gzip the issue was not seen. Response was served to client gzip compressed.

When testing with Accept-Encoding: br in the request , the issue was seen and the response was served to end user to br compression. 

Sample logs line 48: [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10468090]

Working logs we see: 


{code:java}
u - Ghost decompressed brotli encoded object at some point.
a - Client accepts brotli. The request has value br in Accept-Encoding header.
T - Undocumented{code}
Non Working logs: 
{code:java}
b - Client was served with brotli object. The response has header Content-Encoding:br.
u - Ghost decompressed brotli encoded object at some point.
a - Client accepts brotli. The request has value br in Accept-Encoding header.
C - A brotli compression was performed to serve current request. {code}

They do not have RO enabled in the configuration. 

Customer has disabled the BR compression to mitigate the issue.

Checked if this is related to the rollback in someway [https://collaborate.akamai.com/confluence/spaces/DynamicMedia/pages/1106561667/Rollout+Plan+-+RO+to+BOTF+Migration#RolloutPlanROtoBOTFMigration-subnet.W.ro-to-botf-rollback] 

Checking on a region which is in the next Phase also replicated the issue. [https://gripe.akamai.com/rollout/subnet.S.ro-to-botf-rollback] . So not sure if the rollback is related. 

Could you please review and check what is causing the issue with ESI when br compression is happening? 

There was an issue reported during the RO > BOTF migration previously https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/ERE-2684 .
creator: Sandeep Bhat

summary: {F-CS-10489200} - Cookie header not sent to origin intermittently
description:
Account: [Singapore Airlines Limited|https://akamai.lightning.force.com/lightning/r/Account/001A0000004ugOxIAI/view] 

Cpcode: 15726

Hostname: www.singaporeair.com

Sample URL: [www.singaporeair.com/redemption/submitFlightSearch.form|https://www.singaporeair.com/redemption/submitFlightSearch.form] 

Customer found the cookie was not sent to origin randomly for the same URL [www.singaporeair.com/redemption/submitFlightSearch.form|https://www.singaporeair.com/redemption/submitFlightSearch.form]  . 

We are not able to replicate the issue and the issue is intermittent. 

The issue is not specific to any user or edge server regions. 

The behavior of missing cookie is observed for multiple URLs. 

Sample instances in [https://control.akamai.com/apps/security-analytics?accountId=VC-A6RA&contractTypeId=1-2RBL&configSelector=3402&view=&hash=5d3732aa-a751-4745-bef7-7b1328484a8f] 

The working ones have a status code 303 or 200 . the non working URLs see a 302 status code. 

We see that the Cookie is logged in the child server and in case of non working instances, the cookie is not logged in the parent server and we see a 302 status code. 

Sample logs in the etherpad: 

[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10489200] 

I have add more samples here with logs for the requestID irrespective of the cpcode.  [Includes btofender and queue-it url calls].

[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/ER-252452] 

Customer is seeing the issue from June 18th.

the issue is escalated to CEO level at customer end and there is a call tomorrow in APJ hours to discuss this. 

Could you help understand what could cause such a behavior? Nothing in the customer configuration stands out which could be stripping the Cookie header. 

We have a SECESC ticket open as well https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/SECESC-28572 

CPR was disabled to rule out as an issue. However issue still remains.
creator: Sandeep Bhat

summary: 503 errors served to end users beginning Oct 16
description:
The issue was not readily reproducible at the time and is no longer occurring after a configuration change which disables POC in v29. 

Property: dn.tr.playblackdesert.com v29 (Activated Oct 29, 2025, 03:13:11 UTC)

Beginning Oct 16 the customer started to see 503 errors for small objects. The configuration is old with last modification in June 2025 and no errors prior to Oct 16.

Observations: 

- POC was enabled in the configuration but it was incorrectly applying also to small objects.
- The client request comes as a full GET.
- Ghost forwards to MCH with 0-0 request and gets an error.
- Failover triggers to the CFH map which goes to CW with 0-0 request.
- CW makes a 2MB byte range request and successfully fetches the object from origin (or serves from CW peer cache based on some of the traces) but serves it to Parent with content length mismatch and a 503.
- The content comes from origin and/or peer with 200 response code as the object is smaller than 2MB.
- Nothing interesting in cache.log.


!Screenshot 2025-10-29 at 1.16.21 PM.jpg|thumbnail!

There are several log traces showing the behavior. A trace corresponding to the screenshot above: https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10507658-ER#L250.

There were multiple forwards on the same CW machine 95.101.54.29 with same behavior of 200 in the forward request followed by 503 in S line.

!Screenshot 2025-10-29 at 1.40.51 PM.jpg|thumbnail!

The issue disappeared after POC was disabled in the config. 

Ask: can you help understand why these errors started Oct 16 but were not there before? Why would a range request result in an error even though all the bytes have been fetched?
executive_summary:
It seems related to the rollout and currently it can be seen that there are no 503 due to rollback happened on 31st October. 
Further actions are being tracked under the ghost ticket https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/GHOST-6975
root_cause: The issue was occurred due to the rollout https://gripe.akamai.com/rollout/subnet.W.rollout-poc-reduce-round-trips-client-side and the rollback had been done to fix the issue.
creator: Deyan Selverov [X]
mitigation_plan: Rollback
longterm_mitigation: Rollback

There was an update in April to the config for the POC part.  Unfortunately, we don't have a way to confirm if there was a purge after this change. 
{code:java}
<!-- Large file POC optimization -->
<cache:poc2>
  <status>on</status>
  <abort-user-request-on-inconsistent-fragment>on</abort-user-request-on-inconsistent-fragment>
  <acs-etag-to-acs>on</acs-etag-to-acs>
  <check-expired-fragments>off</check-expired-fragments>
  <icp>on</icp>
  <min-object-size>20MB</min-object-size>
  <fragment-size>2MB</fragment-size>
  <make-fragments-public-early>on</make-fragments-public-early>
  <save-inconsistent-fragments>off</save-inconsistent-fragments>
  <prefetch-fragments-during-request>1</prefetch-fragments-during-request>
  <prefetch-fragments-after-request>0</prefetch-fragments-after-request>
  <new-master-on-inconsistent-fragment>on</new-master-on-inconsistent-fragment>
  <trust-etag>on</trust-etag>
  <trust-lastmod>on</trust-lastmod>  
</cache:poc2>
<!--Partial Object Caching settings END-->
{code}
 

Based on the error in logs the problem is related to this kb:  [https://akamai.lightning.force.com/lightning/r/Knowledge__kav/ka30f000000kSuJAAU/view]

I haven't found an instance where the Origin response differs in the bytes sent to TD, so it looks that the Edge has the fragment in cache for long time and when there is a request for the oject the LM header in cache does not match with the actual LM header coming from Origin causing the POC error and the fragment is release so when the next request comes the Edge will cache again the fragment and we don't see the error.

 

Looks that we should be able to fix this issue changing this tag to "OFF"

 <trust-lastmod>on</trust-lastmod> 

[http://mdsearch.engr.akamai.com/?name=trust-lastmod&automap=&version=11.2.2&datatype=&listable=&scope=&default_value=&can_appear=&allowed_by_default=&stage=&author=&feature=]

For now, PS will do the change in Staging  and will test it but please let us if we should try something different

https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/GSPMAPSTRA-4841

resolution_description: Map-ops rolled back the score quantization change for api1 shard which Coupang uses.
root_cause:
Map-ops implemented the platform wide Score quantization change for API Product maps in FF and this resulted in multiple KR regions belonging to API maps to end up with same score resulting in fewer regions to be selected by mapper for serving the traffic.
This resulted in Coupang traffic to be served from limited set of regions which become flit full causing performance concerns.
creator: Suman Mishra
mitigation_plan: Map-ops rolled back the score quantization change for api1 shard which Coupang uses.
longterm_mitigation: implementing traffic sharding across multiple API shards to prevent overloading and concentration of traffic in specific regions. This should be considered a permanent solution to ensure stable and efficient delivery of Coupang traffic without platform disruptions.

a - Client accepts brotli. The request has value br in Accept-Encoding header.
{noformat}

The complete test details are under: https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/ER-252807
Based on the test we could see, 

When the first request is made to the machine where the object is not in cache, the request made with br, we get br object in response, and once its cached in br form, we make another request with gzip, we get gzip object. So in this case we are getting both br and gzip responses based on what we are making a request with.


However, in the case of the request that is first made with gzip on a machine where the object is not in cache, we get a gzip response. But when we made the next request on this machine with br, we still got a gzip from the cache. In this case machine always serves gzip for both br and gzip in the request. 

The expectation is to get a gzip response when a gzip request is made and a br response when a br request is made, irrespective of what was cached in the first place.

root_cause: Behaviour is working as intended—object size was smaller than the default (re)compression minimum size.

summary: {F-CS-10557570} EIPB Move to Single Cloud (Asia)
description:
*(Submitting on behalf of the account's IAT, as they currently lack access to the project and have no apparent means to engage ERE through their available processes)*

 

Hello,

 

We received the following request, which is similar to ERE-2977.

 

Please update the EIPB configuration to have a single cloud (eip-terr-as). Details below:

 
 * Account: Deutsche Bank AG Eschborn
 * EIPB Config Name: apac.db.com

 

Context:
Edge IP Binding provides a set of static Anycast IPs: 10 IPv4 addresses and several IPv6 CIDR blocks.

 

Customer requirements:
When the customer’s hostname is queried from a specified ASN, they aim to return only one of six predefined IPs for each IP version (IPv4 and IPv6).
This restriction is crucial because the customer cannot hardcode IPs in their environment (similar to manually editing the hosts file).
If DNS returns more than the limited set, the customer may receive IPs not whitelisted on their side, so simply providing a subset isn’t sufficient unless all possible IPs are whitelisted.

 

Proposed Solution (Agreed by the customer):
This EIPB config is expected to serve the clients only in Asia. So, we will configure EIPB (IPv4-only) with a single cloud - Asia. The customer will get 2 IPv4 IPs, and that aligns with their expectations.

 
[~akleytma] tagging you here as you took care of the previous similar inquiry.

 

We appreciate any help you can provide,
executive_summary: Aleksey push the changes for this request as EIP_BINDING_ADMIN access users has the right to perform all operations like add cloud, edit cloud cidr, and all operations related to EIPB Configuration.
creator: Hugo Luquet

description:

* 17:58
* 18:08

{code}

[Mapper DNSP for r49882|https://mapper.akamai.com/dnsp/#from%3D1762185600000%26to%3D1762214400000%26dataFrom%3D1762214389000%26useGMTTime%3Dtrue%26timeRange%3D%7B%22min%22%3A1762185600000%2C%22max%22%3A1762214400000%7D%26regionId%3D49882%26service%3DS%26] shows 11 out of 16 machines self-suspended multiple times aligning with the timeframe customer provided above. 

The same pattern was observed from around 22 UTC later that day as well. We can see the same pattern with [load graphs|https://lg.netarch.akamai.com/cgi-bin/loadgraphs?period=1w&region=49882&network=A&maprule=&display=total&ymax=&utcoffset=-4&diskcpu=on] as well. 

We escalated the issue to NOCC via [ticket B-V-6177PC3|https://issues.deploy.akamai.com/cgi-bin/view.cgi?issue_id=B-V-6177PC3] and they provided the following. 
{quote}
They (NOCC tier3) found that machines were fluctuating between good and bad (sflag 16, liveness test timed out). These multiple instances of sflags on multiple machines were due to spike in request on *digicert.com
If you would like these sflags reviewed further please escalate to ghost ERE.
{quote}

We reviewed the data further, and we can see that multiple domains of Digicert were causing the region to overload, followed by self-suspension. Once it recovered, it unsuspended and then experienced the overload, which continued throughout. Checking the [historical grapher for maprules that have high flyteload|https://map.akamai.com/cgi-bin/FreeFlow/Analysis/HDB_Server.pl?startmonth=11&startday=3&startyear=2025&starthour=16&startmin=0&endmonth=11&endday=3&endyear=2025&endhour=20&endmin=0&param1=49882&dbname=production&param2=&param3=&param4=&display=graph&normalize=none&ptdisp=normal&yaxis=y-axis&size=large&scope=all&query_name=REGION_BY_MAPRULE_FLYTELOAD&customSql=], we can see maprule 9244 (e;cd2) starting the spiky traffic. 

Checking ghostmon and cache.log, we see the unsuspension lasted for about 15 seconds during which the number of accepts increased significantly, and AVG manager cycle went up to 26k microseconds during that time. This aligns with the read timeout that customer experienced from their clients.

[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10437636#L3] ( line 3 onwards)

 

Couple of CW regions stood out but there was no prominent pattern. Lattice jobs was setup between these regions and origin to review routes with NOCC

[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10437636#L170] ( line 170)

 

+*OHD disabling and QR implemented:*+
 * IAT suspected OHD as a cause and disabled it on 1st Nov.
 * Also QR was enabled.
 * Since it impacted VSF and re-buffering metrics , customer moved traffic to Fastly
 * Post OHD disablement and QR enablement (29th Oct), logs analysis showed error rate dropped from ( 4-0.1% of connect timeout errors at edge and 0xx also dropped towards origin). But majority of the traffic is moved away its hard to validate.

 

+*Route issue between origin -> Akamai*+ 

Traces between CW -> Origin did not capture any issue. However when customer shared reverse traces between Origin -> CW regions we noticed their Liberty origin peered via TATA FRANFURT and there was a consistent path loss and packet drop.

Reverse route was not same as CW-> origin route. The issue is still investigated with TATA : B-V-60G6Y0J *.* NOCC confirmed the issue was closer to the origin and TATA peering was seen for major EU regions

Couple of steps taken by NOCC
 * 
 ** They have capped TATA peering link in FRANFURT
 ** Suggested the customer to use non TATA peering

 

+*Performance is good for Fastly*+

Customer is sensitive to performance and they reported the issue was not seen for Fastly. Observations:

1) Connecting Fastly IPs to Origin, do not use the TATA route and are located in NL.

2) Currently CW EU live is used and majority of non NL regions are routed via TATA.

 * Comparison of connections to origin during and after issue : [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10437636#L1743 |https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10437636#L1743]

 

Ask ERE,

While NOCC is working on the issue, customer is looking for immediate fix to overcome the congestion issue.
 * ADC , was suggested but would be considered in future
 * IAT reached out to CW product team for custom map and recommendations, but they asked for a review from ERE. Checking feasibility of a setup similar to Fastly, where Fastly servers connecting to origin are located in same city as Origin i.e Amsterdam (probably same Data Center). While our Top IPs via which we majority connect to origin are not even in NL, but are in Germany, France and Sweden.

 * OIPACL would help here?

Please review and provide suggestions
