executive_summary:
After running the metadata trace, we see that the property aid is 170644 along with the aidv 213, while the log shows aidv 1 which seems to be a version of 1254101 ( Include). Ghost is just taking the last instance of the <arl-version> tag seen. 
As a short term mitigation, we suggested to try to put the <arl-version> tag at the end of the file instead of the beginning.
After discussing this internally, hence we have also filed a ghost ticket GHOST-7032

summary: Issues with parallel downloads of Linode Images - Internal
description:
Some background information first:
Akamai/Linode is using DD property images.internal.linode.com / CP 1619877 for downloading large filesystem images during deployment of customer Linodes from images.

Customer Bitmovin has a quite unusual workflow in which he is deploying dozens if not hundreds of linodes around same time resulting into parallel downloads of same 6.8 GB large image [https://images.internal.linode.com/internal-images-par3-1/34692521.gz.enc]

Recently Custoemer did complain about very slow linode deployment in PAR3 which is getting images from r49594:FABRIC-PAR32w (2.20.133.22, 2.20.133.18) and we found many downloads taking over 600 seconds on 2.20.133.18 and over 2000 seconds on 2.20.133.22.

Log sample from : lsg7 - /home/adidebul/imagenext/CP1619877-202511031800-23.33.25.197-325-1762506357.gz
{code:java}
[adidebul@lsg-gss7 ~/imagenext]$ zgrep " S .*internal-images-par3-1/34692521.gz.enc" CP1619877-202511031800-23.33.25.197-325-1762506357.gz | awk '$9==6879468217' |sort -nk7  | tail -n 1

2.20.133.22 S 1762194328.330 11 12 95 2433500 6879468217 6879468217 6879468736 2600:3c0f:19:5::267 GET 1097 1619877 internal-images-par3-1.fr-par-1.linodeobjects.com 200 - djeV binary/octet-stream - D 1 270 3819 - - - - tor sgaH8 internal-images-par3-1/34692521.gz.enc?__token__=st=1762194328%7eexp=1762237528%7eacl=/*34692521*%7ehmac=b415f0cd2928b6c5694ee9ba0ab393556163024cff08662fd32673bfbed125cc - images.internal.linode.com ^ - Go-http-client/1.1 ^ 506088a2 - - 2592000 ^ ^ - - ^ - - ^ - ^ - - mid=2006;dev=w:go_http_client|1;pcf=//@tcp/26400F61822328481308+0E\//@tls/c6a4ce37a8dc4153\//@tls3/3~de293936a8dc4153;sn=263532||263532|;aid=1042248;cs=104.78.67.143|3|21485160c12d45a|0|0|-|0|r46;cert=RSA-SHA256;gd=//0@0;clauth=//aws/-//fr-par-1/;ucb=//1@1619877/foreground-download/catsz/unknown/objsz/gt100mb/ctype/unknown/pop/unknown#0,34,100,19,16;pin=http|dod;alpn=http/1.1;aidv=175;fp=298;mle=1;vcd=20015;cta=1DJ6CF|!11EC1D171819|8E4D8H8F8G4B5B6B5D6D2B2D - - ^ 1097.dscdi3 4545913:48749:272867:21 L1:L1:s:L1:: 8 - - 50f8abea - - 999198637233283968 499599318616641984 15596 94861 865 - - - 2a02:26f0:680:9e::214:8512|1|2|1|1097|516|55|21|0 - 10:0:8:8:0:::f:f ^
[adidebul@lsg-gss7 ~/imagenext]$
{code}
It looks like "usually" transfers of this 6.8 GB image take about 200-300 seconds (client might be doing on-the-flight decryption/decompression etc) but when issue occurs transfers take 600+ seconds on less loaded 2.20.133.18 and 1800+ seconds on 2.20.133.22 .

When doing test downloads using curl (token is needed and can be found in logs/eStats) I we first got a very good throughputs with 6.8GB being downloaded in 15-20 seconds but later when doing same test while image was being used/downloaded for deployment same curl download was often taking over 5-10 minutes.

Later we have been able to reproduce the issue by running multiple curl downloads for same object in parallel curl requests slowing down(or kind of stalling) each-other.
In next step it was possible to reproduce the issue directly on the edge via 127.0.0.1 completely eliminating network and client from the equation.

Issue reproducibility and magnitude of slowdown/stalling seem to be related to load on the edge and to number of parallel requests which need to be on same object...

Issue:
Multiple parallel downloads on same edge and on same object seem to be running into some bottleneck within the Ghost. 
It feels like different reads from same Store Entry might be kind of blocking each-other under some conditions. Machine load seem to play relevant role but issue seem to be partially reproducible even on server with low load.

summary: Issue during MCH overlap with OS for STAR delivery.
description:
This is in line with the escalation [ERE-2677|https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/ERE-2677] , where when the MCH and OS overlap is seen  we aren't seeing ERE_DNS_IN_Region but others like SSL_timeout/Connect timeout etc. 

While we do have successful request for the same flow with overlap , wanted to understand on the above behavior seen . Another instance tracked here [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/ERE-MCH-OS-Issue]
executive_summary: The ghost code is checking against the in-region service ip's or against the in-region vips. I do see that the MCH and OS are from same region But what has been sent to 47.114 from 47.129 is not a peer/parent request. It is an origin request. The OS request will be considered as a DIRECT rather than PEER request. So that could be the reason it might have skipped.
root_cause: It seems to be an expected since the forward to OS is treated as an origin and not as a forward to peer or parent  hence the lack of ERR_DNS_IN_REGION

*Subject:* Re: PhonePe - 75% Traffic Analysis

 

Hello Rithvik,

The given mitigation tested on staging did not work, because of the variables don’t get defined in the staging, that’s why we see the issue.

There is a match on region attribute “use-staging” at the beginning if that is on "false", then it is production metadata. If it is true, then it is staging. That match prevents any metadata inside it from executing in staging.

<akamai:choose>

<match:region.attribute value="use-staging" result="false">

<!— OIPACL prod mdt —>

 

</match:region.attribute>

          <match:region.attribute value="use-staging" result="true">

            <!-- Go via RA staging maps to Origin as they are part of the supernet -->

            <akamai:choose>

              <match:region.attribute value="network-freeflow">

                <forward:cache-parent>

                  <status>on</status>

                  <policy>site-shield</policy>

                  <selection-method>domain-lookup</selection-method>

                  <map>a%(SIACL_IMPL_SERIAL).ch.akamai-staging.net</map>

                  <enable-all-methods>on</enable-all-methods>

                </forward:cache-parent>

              </match:region.attribute>

              <match:region.attribute value="network-essl">

                <forward:cache-parent>

                  <status>on</status>

                  <policy>site-shield</policy>

                  <selection-method>domain-lookup</selection-method>

                  <map>e%(SIACL_IMPL_SERIAL).ch.akamaiedge-staging.net</map>

                  <enable-all-methods>on</enable-all-methods>

                </forward:cache-parent>

              </match:region.attribute>

            </akamai:choose>

          </match:region.attribute>

</akamai:choose> 


Staging and prod IMPL are vastly different for OIPACL, so the given snippet didn’t work on staging but should work in prod network. 

As discussed, the Rollout is going-on, I don’t recommend any sort of advanced override metadata as a fix with the rollout to avoid any other issue. 
Please refer [https://collaborate.akamai.com/confluence/spaces/DynamicMedia/pages/1257888826/Rollout+Plan+Introduce+HTTP+Status+Codes+to+Origin+IP+ACL+Acceptance+Criteria]

Regards,
Sarabjeet

*Subject:* Re: PhonePe - 75% Traffic Analysis

 

Hi Sarabjeet, Thilaga, 

 

Based on our webex conversation, we had raised an Akatec case when customer was testing the metadata on staging: Case Id-  F-CS-10521044 and below were the findings:

 

- From the logs related to the reported error, we observed the following message: ERR_NO_FWD_HOSTS fwdStartFail. This error indicates that the edge or parent server attempted to forward a request but could not find any available or valid hosts to forward the request to. This often results in an HTTP 503 Service Unavailable error. 

- Additionally, in our internal logs, we noticed the following message: ERROR: no parent-map configured for cacheh. 

- We observed configuration changes where the staging version was V132, while the production version was V128. 

- Version V132 contains an advanced metadata entry for forward:cache-parent, which appears to be causing the error. 

- We activated V128 on staging and tested it, and we did not encounter any 503 errors.

executive_summary:
Requested via email 
Customer added the provided snippet as a part of ERE-2975 on staging but as informed it did not work. Further investigated why the given mitigation tested on staging did not work, because of the variables don’t get defined in the staging, that’s why we see the issue.
There is a match on region attribute “use-staging” at the beginning if that is on "false", then it is production metadata. If it is true, then it is staging. That match prevents any metadata inside it from executing in staging. Staging and prod IMPL are vastly different for OIPACL, so the given snippet didn’t work on staging but should work in prod network. 
The Rollout is going-on, hence recommended not to make any sort of advanced override metadata as a fix with the rollout to avoid any other issue. 
Please refer https://collaborate.akamai.com/confluence/spaces/DynamicMedia/pages/1257888826/Rollout+Plan+Introduce+HTTP+Status+Codes+to+Origin+IP+ACL+Acceptance+Criteria

Background/context:
Just to provide some more context as this issue will become more critical in the near future. Very soon, open banking legislation is coming into effect in NZ which regulates how and when banks must supply customer data. This will cover BNZ’s requirements to provide reliable access to customer data to authorised 3^rd^ parties as part of that banking sector framework. These 3^rd^ parties access BNZ securely via our services(i.e. Akamai). 

We’re seeing these 3^rd^ parties get rejected intermittently. They retry and it works fine. From what we can see of the reported instances is that OCSP validation fails i.e. the certificate is accepted but when Akamai goes to complete the OCSP validation, it fails. 

It's happening enough that the 3^rd^ parties are raising it as an issue to their counterparts in BNZ who have raised it with us. As open banking expands and the act comes into effect, there are severe financial penalties if BNZ is deemed to not provide a reliable service. 

We need to provide potential or definite “why’s” to the parties (issues with OCSP endpoint, network latency etc) so that we can ensure a dependable system in place.

Ask:
* Is the OCSP validation failure because of timeout? Is the timeout caused by the responder slow response?
* What’s the default timeout value for Akamai OCSP?
* Is there a timeout configured on the Akamai platform for the OCSP request/response?

executive_summary:
We enabled debug logging CLIENT, FWD, FWD_SL, HTTP and analysed the logs. 
Based upon our analysis, we saw more than 3k hits/sec to a machine. Hence we suggested to enable the serial prespread if this can help us somehow https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/MAPPINGENG-7943
Upon further  analysis with Engineering with more debug logging, we conclude that the Region health detects mid-tier regions as bad and origin IPACL has no fallback mechanism even with Acceptance criteria enabled.  
Team has enabled RA fallback instead of SR for Origin IPACL as a short term mitigation and we haven't seen error post that change. The permanent fix for the SR2 map will be a fix needed in ghost, https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/GHOST-7069 has been raised for the same.
root_cause: The Region health detects mid-tier regions as bad and origin IPACL has no fallback mechanism even with Acceptance criteria enabled. Actually, the Edge normally uses two tier to go forward: SIACL (primary) and SIACL-ALT (backup). SIACL tries to provide two forward paths, but both get removed because the ghost marks those regions as bad while SIACL-ALT provides one forward path, but it has strict acceptance criteria, so Ghost is not allowed to use it. With no valid forward paths left, Ghost does not trigger any forward request at all, which leads to the observed errors.
creator: Alan Boon
mitigation_plan: Team has enabled RA fallback instead of SR for Origin IPACL as a short term mitigation
longterm_mitigation: The permanent fix for the SR2 map will be a fix needed in ghost, https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/GHOST-7069

executive_summary:
As per the provided logs, the issue looks similar to the SI-00023285. It does not make any forward to the parent, it detected the bad parent/region, 
We can use the provided workaround the ERE-3057.
root_cause: The Region health detects mid-tier regions as bad and origin IPACL has no fallback mechanism even with Acceptance criteria enabled. Actually, the Edge normally uses two tier to go forward: SIACL (primary) and SIACL-ALT (backup). SIACL tries to provide two forward paths, but both get removed because the ghost marks those regions as bad while SIACL-ALT provides one forward path, but it has strict acceptance criteria, so Ghost is not allowed to use it. With no valid forward paths left, Ghost does not trigger any forward request at all, which leads to the observed errors.
creator: Sandeep Bhat
mitigation_plan: Enabled RA fallback instead of SR for Origin IPACL as a short term mitigation
longterm_mitigation: The permanent fix for the SR2 map will be a fix needed in ghost, https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/GHOST-7069 has been raised for the same.

summary: Inconsistent Segmented Media Mode Requirement When Creating Edge Hostnames
description:
IAT has identified an inconsistency in the workflow for creating edge hostnames within Media Properties.

When adding an edge hostname from the Media Property, the “Create” button does not appear unless a Segmented Media Mode (LIVE or VOD) is selected beforehand—even though this field is shown as optional (see Fig. 1).

However, when creating an edge hostname directly from the Edge Hostname section, the UI displays an alert indicating that selecting a Segmented Media Mode is mandatory (see Fig. 2).

While we understand that the selected media mode influences the mapping logic, the current behavior is inconsistent between the two interfaces and may cause confusion for users.

Request:

Could we make this requirement clearer or more consistent—for example, by adding a message, warning, or indicator (similar to the alert shown in the Edge Hostname section) when adding an edge hostname from the Media Property interface?
creator: Sabarinath Sundaram

summary: {F-CS-10611138} Max-age value not decreasing due to transformation
description:
Account: Xero Ltd
Not-working sample: https://workpapers.xero.com/app/clients
And testing on *Staging*.

Etherpad: https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10611138


Issue:
Customer is testing caching feature "Downstream Cacheability: Cache Lifetime: (Default) Smaller value: origin header or remaining edge TTL" in staging environment and they expect to observe decreasing TTL in Cache-Control: max-age when TCP_HIT since origin is always replying max-age=300.

They have observed decreasing max-age successfully when hitting https://go.xero.com/app/testing, however it is not working for https://workpapers.xero.com/app/clients

PS team has reviewed both configs and confirmed that both configs have correct "Downstream Cacheability" setup and should behave the same. However, when we look at workpapers.xero.com.xml, we oberved additional response headers:
a) additional '?akamai-transform=9'
b) x-akamai-transformed: 0 - 0
c) additional Set-Cookies:
* _abck=0D668E86F5317DC8AADC86CFC390ADB2~
* bm_sz=6F3E52D65900C632878A5AA9354BBED8
==> these are most likely related to BMP

And there are other Xero properties that exhibits this 'wrong' behaviour.
While https://go.xero.com/app/ behaves correctly (and without these 'extra' headers).


Ask:
# Why is max-age of https://workpapers.xero.com/app/clients is not decreasing even when TCP_MEM_HIT and Smaller value: origin header or remaining edge TTL is enabled?
# How do we Downstream Caching to work in such cases?

We have also filed a new SECSEC JIRA asking the same question:
https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/SECESC-29127

summary: [AKAM-CASE #F-CS-10625200] Cant create a DPM config
description:
IAT is unable to select "Policy Type" due to which a new DP cannot be created.

When they tried to create a new DPM the Policy Type is grayed out, which we assume is the reason why the Policy attribute also shows an "error" in the UI:

 

!Delivery_Policy_Manager.png|width=519,height=230!

The account has Site_Accel::DeliveryPolicyManager, APIAcceleration::DeliveryPolicyManager in the contract, and the only 3 configs that this account has are Dynamic Site Accelerator.

 

We need your help to find out why the Policy type shows grayed out for this customer? Are they missing a line item in their contract?

 

Steps to reproduce the issue:

1. Access DPM and click on Create a Policy Assignment (direct link)- [https://control.akamai.com/apps/delivery-policy-manager/#/delivery-policy-assignments/create]
2. Select contract and group from the dropdown (only one option)
3. The Policy Type option is greyed out, and we cannot select it.
4. Policy Attributes is blank – we believe this will show up once we select Policy type (which is the current issue)
executive_summary:
The customer was unable to create the DPM configuration because the DPM Policy Type remained disabled even after entering the contract details.
26/Nov/25 : we had identified a workaround: they needed to add the required product list items so that the validation would pass and the policy type would be enabled as the product list items were in an expired state.

27/Nov/2025: Reporter confirmed that the product line items are not having a required list items with the correct availability date.As the workaround provided ,issue got closed.

3/Dec/2025: PSG notified us that the issue persisted even after adding the product line items.

4/Dec/2025: When we reviewed the case after reopening the ticket, we found that the customer still had not added the product line items correctly.we sent them the complete and correct list of items they need to add, including the appropriate start and expiration dates.
root_cause: Product Line Items are present incorrectly in the contract.
creator: Rebeca Gonzalez Porras
mitigation_plan: the complete and correct list of items provided, including the appropriate start and expiration dates.
longterm_mitigation: Not Applicable

summary: Requests being forwarded to an ICP machine which was self-suspended
description:
There is an on-going platfrom review for Jio Hotstar and ERE performance team noticed an unexpected ICP mapping behavior in the ERE-3029 
{quote}_Almost all errors stemmed from requests being forwarded to a single ICP peer machine (49.44.175.5) that was [self-suspended|https://mapper.akamai.com/dnsp/ghost-machine/#from%3D1763909400000%26to%3D1763911200000%26dataFrom%3D1763910202000%26useGMTTime%3Dtrue%26timeRange%3D%7B%22min%22%3A1763909400000%2C%22max%22%3A1763911200000%7D%26regionId%3D32762%26ghostIp%3D49.44.175.9%26service%3DW%26] for ~5min. We continued to fwd traffic even when the ghost suspend flag was set. This is similar to the [previous observation|https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/ERE-3029?focusedId=12103695&page=com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.issuetabpanels:comment-tabpanel#comment-12103695] made by Trisha and looks like a variation of GHOST-3082._ 
{quote}
As per the Jira it says child ghost server shouldn't go to ICP if the suspension is in place but sample instance shows it went to ICP. Akatec pulled region wide logs for samples and traced ICP requests for every 30 seconds.

summary: [SI-00023309] Enclave DNS machines decommissioned impacting ACC Portal applications
description:
Starting around 11:10 IST on November 25, 2025, several customers began experiencing problems accessing or updating certain applications in Akamai Control Center.

These issues did not affect Akamai’s ability to deliver traffic across its edge network. However, they did prevent customers from modifying existing configurations or creating new ones.

The affected applications and services included, but were not limited to: Alerting and Notifications,Analytics Configuration,Bot Management Configuration ,Certificate Provisioning System ,Client Management ,Diagnostics ,Event Center ,Media Reporting ,Network Configuration ,Property Manager configuration activations ,Traffic Reporting ,Web Application Firewall (WAF) activations

As for ERE Side  We received reported from mulitple customer reporting ACC modules is not loading properly. That include Property manager, cps, bot man...etc

ERE inform to prtldvps team regarding the 0% availability of 'portal-cw-api'. After further discussion with the PSG ,issue is become more severe as it is spread for multiple apps (list specified above).(Screenshot is attached on the ticket)



Incident Criteria : Sev 1 - Portal: Application Availability - Failure of any Time-critical Portal application(s) lasting over 4 hours.
executive_summary:
At November 11, 2025 11:10 IST :Internal DNS servers supporting Akamai Control Center traffic were unintentionally disabled during server decommissioning maintenance.

November 25, 2025 11:20 IST :Multiple customers started reporting issues accessing or updating certain applications within Akamai Control Center.

November 25, 2025 11:44 IST : Akamai's investigation began.

November 25, 2025 12:50 IST to 15:00 IST : Additional subject matter experts were brought in to investigate new potential root causes, including network connectivity and key distribution.

November 25, 2025 15:30 : The root cause was identified as the expiration of DNS zones two weeks after internal DNS servers were decommissioned.

November 25, 2025 15:34 IST : DNS servers were restored, and the impact was fully mitigated.
resolution_description: To prevent a recurrence, Akamai will enhance monitoring and alerting for internal DNS services and will update operational documentation, training, and procedures for internal DNS services.
root_cause: The investigation revealed that the problem was caused by DNS resolution failures affecting internal application hostnames used by Akamai Control Center. These failures occurred after the servers responsible for DNS resolution were unintentionally taken offline. Akamai restored the impacted servers, and services returned to normal operations at approximately 10:05 UTC(15:35 ist) on November 25, 2025.
creator: Naman Agarwal

summary: Lower DOM/FOM on r42594 and r43441
description:
Hello GPO,

Summary:  r42594 and r43441 both saw high cpu/flits and suspensions when requests  going to these regions showed a very high TAT for a brief window. However the  load graph for the regions show repeat suspensions and the customer claims that the timeouts still affect 0.24% of traffic going to the EdgeWorkers, which is still a considerable amount of requests.

Copying the analysis by CSE below:

~~~

[Environment]
Account: DPG Media Services NV
Property: dsa_frontend_libelle_production (Product: Dynamic Site Accelerator)
Subrequests' Property: dd_sim_url_resolver_prod (Product: Download Delivery)
Hostname and CP Code: [libelle.nl|https://libelle.nl/] (1159171)

Subrequests' Hostname and CP Code: url-resolver.sim-jupiter.dpgmedia.cloud (1837369)
EdgeWorkers ID: 98515 and 96172 for prod and non-prod

[Issue]
An issue has been observed with an EdgeWorker that makes a subrequest to another property's hostname, where the request times out before reaching the origin.

Call Flow: [libelle.nl|https://libelle.nl/] (1159171) —> (EW) —> url-resolver.sim-jupiter.dpgmedia.cloud (1837369)


[Analysis Summary]
- Some slowness originated from the Akamai Midgress for requests to EW: 'url-resolver.sim-jupiter.dpgmedia.cloud’, which led to the timeout errors (HTTP 504 status code) for the original request to ‘[libelle.nl|https://libelle.nl/]’.

- Below are the examples. High request end time is observed in the forwarded requests (f line) to MCH. The actual ddc.log are placed on the etherpad.
----------------------------------------
Example 1) Req ID: 1e475d62
Etherpad: [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10562037#L542] (from line 542)

Example 2) Req ID: 6278c20c
Etherpad: [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10562037#L554] (from line 554)
----------------------------------------

- The affected forwarded IPs (for MCH) are aggregated into IP: 23.209.125.x (r42594) and 104.109.143.x (r43441).

- There was no expected retry mechanism executed in the forwarded MCH requests. The retries were sent to the same edge machine, which doesn’t seem appropriate. --> Engaged IAT

- Looking at each region, we can see spikes of over-capacity and suspended/dead machines occurring sporadically, but fairly frequently.


----------------------------------------
r42594
Mapper: [https://mapper.akamai.com/short/MKkpQ3qk8p]

r43441
Mapper: [https://mapper.akamai.com/short/M7guyZVPLO]
----------------------------------------

- The error rate does not appear to be high, but it's recurring.

- High flit and CPU rates were observed in both regions, r42594 and r43441. cache.log is placed in [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10562037#L570].

- Further investigation revealed that this is a noisy neighbour issue. There was an abrupt traffic spike from a specific account, leading to a region overload. executive_summary:
IFOOD.COM faced 503  "ERR_READ_ERROR fwdStateFree" during Black Friday
As per the provided logs, the issue looks similar to the SI-00023285. It does not make any forward to the parent, it detected the bad parent/region, 
We can use the provided workaround the ERE-3057.
root_cause: The Region health detects mid-tier regions as bad and origin IPACL has no fallback mechanism even with Acceptance criteria enabled. Actually, the Edge normally uses two tier to go forward: SIACL (primary) and SIACL-ALT (backup). SIACL tries to provide two forward paths, but both get removed because the ghost marks those regions as bad while SIACL-ALT provides one forward path, but it has strict acceptance criteria, so Ghost is not allowed to use it. With no valid forward paths left, Ghost does not trigger any forward request at all, which leads to the observed errors.
creator: Gil Bandele
mitigation_plan: Enabled RA fallback instead of SR for Origin IPACL as a short term mitigation
longterm_mitigation: The permanent fix for the SR2 map will be a fix needed in ghost, https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/GHOST-7069 has been raised for the same.

summary: 504 spikes reported in CW regions
description:
There were 2 5xx errors spikes reported today related to 504 errors: [https://grafana-apj.trafficpeak.live/goto/OcK8n2WDg?orgId=674]

*1 spike from 08:00 UTC to 12:00 UTC Nov. 30th*
*2 spike from 14:00 UTC to 16:00 UTC Nov. 30th*


For 1 spike from 08:00 UTC to 12:00 UTC:

• Tracing the 504s we see SSL timeouts towards one of the CW region 40310
• Region was looking bad with constant flit drops and it was taken out to mitigate the issue (B-V-63SOGNB).
• Issue was also escalated to NOCC (B-V-63U11KF). As per NOCC T3:
{quote}Looks like Jio Hotstar is causing the chaos here. The fluctuating traffic pattern is observable on the mapper charts here:

>https://mapper.akamai.com/short/6IjA6ykJtR

As you can see by the pattern in both the above mapper charts and loadgraphs; traffic does shift out of the region for a brief period before it gets mapped back after it recovers. This occurred several times today.

sflags are seen in region due to the overloading after the spike in traffic returns; the in-region load balancer tries its best.

We in NOCC can't definitively speak on what is causing this behavior in Jios config. Best to get this answer from Eng. As far as the region is concerned, it's in good health from NOCC perspective. It's this sudden traffic spike causing suboptimal conditions.
{quote}
 
For 2 spike from 14:00 UTC to 16:00 UTC


• We can see a similar behavior Tracing the 504s we see SSL timeouts towards one of the CW region 36251
• Region was looking bad with constant flit drops.
• Issue was also escalated to NOCC (B-V-63UH5VJ). As per NOCC T3:
{quote}Looks like Jio Hotstar is causing the chaos here too similar to the one seen under B-V-63U11KF
{quote}
On the other hand Akatec was told 
{quote}_I’ve identified what went wrong with the CW regions, so let’s keep those two regions in suspension for now. Recently, we worked with map-ops on a logic change in the Live regionset that was meant to be pushed out for all geos except India. Although in the map-ops ticket, clearly specified not to include IN, the change still went through for India, which caused LCS HW regions to serve Live map—and they aren’t able to handle the flit load. I’ll coordinate with map-ops to get the logic corrected._
{quote}
Can you please review this and identify where the issue happened? IAT also would like to understand the reason why the CW region was not automatically suspended or mapper did not pick a different region in better shape.

[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10650272] has detailed information on the issue.
resolution_description:
Worked with map-ops to get the logic reverted for India geo.
As part of mitigation, got cw-s-in-live map suspended for LCS regions being added.
root_cause: In India geo, LCS regions with low flit capacity were added to serve flit intensive CW Live event traffic mistakenly by map-ops resulting in regions being overloaded and going on self-suspensions.
creator: Dimitris Kim
mitigation_plan:
Worked with map-ops to get the logic reverted for India geo.
As part of mitigation, got cw-s-in-live map suspended for LCS regions being added.
longterm_mitigation:
1. Alert to be in place to capture cases when incompatible HW gets added to serve CW Live map.
2. SRMM Enhancement to work with Mix of HW.

summary: Reduce FOM for +5regions
description:
Hello GPO

IAT/Akatec made the following request to NOCC [B-V-6410I89|https://issues.deploy.akamai.com/cgi-bin/view.cgi?issue_id=B-V-6410I89] but since the number of regions is +5 they wont do it as per their established process.

Background:

~~~~

Customer Coupang Co.,Ltd. reported that there was latency issue on [cmapi.coupang.com|https://cmapi.coupang.com/].

Coupang Co.,Ltd. is quite sensitive about latency of [cmapi.coupang.com|https://cmapi.coupang.com/]. Because this domain is one of the key domain to provide their service.
So they have been monitoring the latency of [cmapi.coupang.com|https://cmapi.coupang.com/] and IAT has been monitoring this also.
This domain is using API-X map(api1, 15211) and the latency of this domain is affected by high flits.
If the flits of api1 map’s KR core regions reach the flit soft cap, this domain’s latency is higher. (Transfer time is affected.)
So IAT requested to set FOM as 0.7 for API1 KR core regions (26727,38402,48921,48922,49630,50064,51456), and they have had 0.7 level FOM.

But a few days ago, maprule logic for API maprules (t&api[1-10]) started being updated.
Below links are about updated maprule logic.
https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/GSPMAPSTRA-4841
[https://docs.google.com/document/d/1uFrGIbyncD4_s26lKvJPnnRln55QInBbW3c7FhmIxtI/edit?pli=1&tab=t.0#heading=h.iid6w11m7d4c]
By this update, API-X traffic started to be served by non core regions.

Problem:
Customer reported that there was latency issue on 29 Nov and 30 Nov.
When I checked the logs, about 15.12% of [cmapi.coupang.com|https://cmapi.coupang.com/] was served by the non core region 47270 and the flit of r47270 was more than flit soft cap.
The region 47270 has 0.8 level FOM.

Following the document [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1uFrGIbyncD4_s26lKvJPnnRln55QInBbW3c7FhmIxtI/edit?pli=1&tab=t.0#heading=h.iid6w11m7d4c], kt-maan regions can be used for KR.
In the api1 map, there are 6 KR kt-maan regions(31010, 33693, 46031, 47270, 48883, 50458), and traffic it expected to be distributed across these regions, as I confirmed from logs.

We need to set 0.7 level FOM for these regions to prevent latency issue of [cmapi.coupang.com|https://cmapi.coupang.com/], so I requested this to NOCC [https://issues.deploy.akamai.com/cgi-bin/view.cgi?issue_id=B-V-6410I89].

Could you please adjust the FOM for these regions and check if there’s any other solution besides adjusting the FOM?

~~~
resolution_description: Set FOM to 0.7 on the regions in primary tier.
root_cause: If the flits of api1 map’s KR core regions reach the flit soft cap, this domain’s latency is higher. (Transfer time is affected.)
creator: Rahul Sawarkar
mitigation_plan: FOM reduction on the regions in primary tier.
longterm_mitigation:
Same as ERE-3024
Implementing traffic sharding across multiple API shards to prevent overloading and concentration of traffic in specific regions. This should be considered a permanent solution to ensure stable and efficient delivery of Coupang traffic without platform disruptions.

summary: Watermarking capitalization inconsistency
description:
The Watermarking documentation under:

[https://techdocs.akamai.com/adaptive-media-delivery/docs/source-content-preprocessing]

Is incorrectly pointing to uppercase `A` or `B` required for The "filename-prefix AB naming" method.

!image-2025-12-03-13-13-39-257.png|width=556,height=443!

 

Tests on customer setup and internal property do return forward path with lower case, either `a` or `b` instead.

The same lowercase can be observed during product tests documented under:

[https://collaborate.akamai.com/confluence/spaces/FFSQA/pages/276945995/Watermarking+Metadata+verification+for+AMD+VOD#WatermarkingMetadataverificationforAMDVOD-SegmentrequestwithparentdirprefixanduseoriginalasA(requestforsegmentB)]

 

Raising as ERE, due to following:

When the "directory-prefix AB naming" method is used the PATH modification will be upper case - in line with the docs.

Not sure though why would we need to create suddenly inconsistency on the naming convention between filename vs directory prefix.

 

*Ask:*

can you verify if is it just matter of incorrect documentation for the "filename-prefix AB naming" method requiring documentation fix?

or "typo" on the product implementation requiring a fix?
executive_summary:
The path returned in case of filename prefix is with lower case (a.segment-0.ts) while the documentation is created with upper case A.segment-0.ts.

So here we have 2 choices on how we wish to see the segment variant.
	1.	Default (variant in file name): Here, the variant 'a' or 'b' is always in lowercase. Example: a.segment-0.ts.
	2.	Variant in URL path(can be chosen in PM when creating ARL): Here, the variant is 'A' or 'B' inserted into the URL path. Example: /A/segment-0.ts.

So this is how we can choose between lowercase and uppercase. The doc might not mention this. Suggested to raise a ticket with dochub to make the required changes.
root_cause: NA, the ticket was raised to check the document inconsistency w.r.t the watermarking filename prefix.
creator: Maciej Maciaszek
mitigation_plan: Raised UXTW-10972 to make the changes in document
longterm_mitigation: Raised UXTW-10972 to make the changes in document

root_cause: SRMM blocked the entire assignments due to high failure rate, resulting in ERR_NO_FWD_HOSTS|fwdStartFail errors on CW maps.
creator: Dimitris Kim
mitigation_plan: SRMM team increased the allowed error limit from 10% to 20% to let SRMM hand over the assignments in the current state of failures in cw-s-in-live map.
longterm_mitigation:
Enhancements required on SRMM 
1. SRMM to not block the entire assignments for all SRO maps across geos on seeing high error rate for one map.
2. The allowed error limit should be relaxed for Live maps compared to VOD maps of CW as the traffic pattern is expected to be more spiky for Live maps.

summary: FF ghost-to-origin error 102 ERR_NO_GOOD_FWD_IP on multiple continents
description:
We're seeing a recent increase in ghost-to-origin 102 errors (ERR_NO_GOOD_FWD_IP). On each continent the degradation begins on different days:

!FF other errors.jpg|width=379,height=393!

[https://www.nocc.akamai.com/miniurl/?id=29144]
 * SA: since Nov 20
 * EU: since Nov 24
 * NA/Caribou-l: since Nov 27
 * AS/X7p-nvme|ssd: since Dec 1

This appears to span multiple customers.

Preliminary analysis of ghost.ddc.log suggests this is associated with SureRoute traffic.

Here's a timeseries showing ghost-to-origin 102 errors (ERR_NO_GOOD_FWD_IP) in North America:

!Error 102 in NA TikTok cpcode 1804669.jpg|width=456,height=239! 
[https://www.nocc.akamai.com/miniurl/?id=29145]

The following qgrep jobs contain f-lines with ERR_NO_GOOD_FWD_IP for several customers:
 * [cp 1347394 AT&T|https://qssi.akamai.com/cgi-bin/qgrep_ui/qgrep.pl?screen=detail&detail=GIP95.100.255.84-202512031100-23.33.25.197-982-1764925648]
 * [cp 1850174 origin.ad-core-lb-alisg-v3.sg-central.byteglb.com, + others|https://qssi.akamai.com/cgi-bin/qgrep_ui/qgrep.pl?screen=detail&detail=GIP190.98.160.60-202512031500-23.33.25.197-632-1764926307]
resolution_description: N/a - consultation
root_cause: Tiktok enabled OHD on a few properties which will cause an increase of these g2o errors and it retains this error to not retry origin and lessen the origin hits. Working as designed.
creator: Fabio Picconi
mitigation_plan: N/a - consultation
longterm_mitigation: N/a - consultation

The pattern _seems_ to be: if there is a ghost in the request chain which logged obj status 'd', then that is the last ghost to report breadcrumbs. Even though that request triggered a normal synchronous forward, and eventually fetched from the origin, that part is not reported in breadcrumbs.
The forward is not even an IMS. Ghost detects object on disk, makes a full non-IMS forward to parent/peer anyway, but breadcrumbs stop there.

Caching option: Honor origin Cache-Control and Expires
Force revalidation of stale objects: Always revalidate with origin
Default maxage: 0 seconds
And we see obj staus     W - The object TTL was set in response headers.

 

*ASK:*

Is it valid for ghost to log 'd' in this situation rather than 's'? 
Does breadcrumb logic depend on object status? (d, or i or m?) 'd' only means that object was on disk, not that the request chain ended there. Breadcrumbs are meant to represent the full chain of fetching an object. The customer uses this data to monitor offload in Traffic Peak and their data is highly inaccurate.

 

I'm seeing unresolved ERE-2916 ERE-2688 and GHOST-6278 which might be related.
Can you help confirm if the object status is at fault here? Is this covered by GHOST-6278? The last updates in there are from Oct - when could we expect a fix in production?

 

Thank you!

summary: [JIOSTAR INDIA] VOD, hes8, off hours 5xx's on December 8th & 9th due to BGP Flaps and suboptimal setup
description:
*Background:*

As part of phase 2 action item for SI: 00023262, ERE has asked for investigation of off hours 5xx spikes and escalate the instances to them for review and logging purpose.

 

*Details:*
TP link: [https://grafana-apj.trafficpeak.live/d/cecu3bebg0we8b/l1-monitoring-vod?orgId=155&from=now-12h&to=now&timezone=browser]

 

*Details Considered:*
Date: Dec 9th 1.01 AM IST [19:31-19:32 GMT 8th Dec]
Cpcodes:
hes8-fmp4-segments (1773737)
hes.akamaized.net-magictoken (1586603)
hses8 (1773723)
hes.akamaized.net-hses8newTRSworkflow (1773730)
hes8-fmp4br-segments (1773739)

 

*Date timestamps provided:*
Dec 9th 1.01 AM IST
Dec 8th 7.04 AM IST

 

Checks are updated in: [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10684609]

 

*INSTANCE 1: Dec 9th 1.01 AM IST [19:31-19:32 GMT 8th Dec]*

 

*Findings:*

1) We are seeing connect timeout and FBTs between multiple BHARENT Edge regions to 36987 (TATA-DELr) regions.

2) Further, we are seeing FBT and connect timeout from TD region: 36987 (TATA-DELr) to multiple different CW regions.

3) On FA front, we are seeing 3 different TATA-DEL regions logging connect timeout and FBTs to TD1 region [ch970 map region]: 34608 (GPX-BOMt)

 

*Issue was escalated to NOCC under: B-V-651W28R*

*NOCC updated:*

We checked issue between given Multiple Bharati Edge and TATA-DEL parent regions. WE found that the path from Tata-Del to Bharati regions IP was over a Airtel PNI. On that PNI we noticed BGP Flaps around the same time stamp. 

We have escalated to Airtel asking for the reason for BGP flap. 

 

*INSTANCE 2: Dec 8th 7.04 AM IST [01:34-01:35 GMT 8th Dec]*

 

*Findings:*

1) We are seeing timeouts between multiple MCH TD regions in US/CA to CW region in India. 

2) Edge from US/CA retried to FA TD [a;chsc01p.akamai.net] in India and logged Connect timeout.

3) Request failed over from TD in US/CA to ch970 map [US/CA]. However, forward to NS in India, saw slowness resulting in ch970 Parent server logging 503: ERR_LIFETIME_EXP error. 

 

4) Due to geographical distance between components, we are seeing losses in the route between source PP to destination region.

--> We are seeing losses between TD PP in US/CA to CW regions in India: [https://rome.akamai.com/cgi-bin/mview/mview.py?start_ts=12%2F08%2F2025+00%3A00&stop_ts=12%2F08%2F2025+03%3A00&pp=23.34.59.4+23.39.48.136+23.40.53.4&region=42694+42684&loss_min=&loss_max=&rtt_min=&rtt_max=]

 

*Property Setup, documentation:*

[https://collaborate.akamai.com/confluence/spaces/NOVIHS/pages/903098540/Novi+IN+VOD]

 

Audience: IN, +*SG,CA,US,GB*+

TD0: MCH

TD1: CW (EU)

Origin: NS4 (IN/IN Layout)

 

*Note:* 

Based on log analysis the impact is for majorly CA (Canada) audience.

Location:
{code:java}
[sshridha@lsg-gss3 ~/F-CS-10684609]$ zcat Client-CP1773737-202512080134.txt.gz | awk '{print $2}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn

      1 ip{code}
 

matching obj_status H (FA), not there two FA's not distinguishable easily, unless would create an custom counter for req_id
{code:java}
[sshridha@lsg-gss3 ~/F-CS-10684609]$ zcat Client-CP1773737-202512080134-failover.txt.gz |awk '{print $2}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn

     10 GB
      1 ip

*Ideally:*

the setup should have at least one NS leg and CW in US to meet the high expectations.

 

*Ask:*
 * Understanding the platform 5xx's and perf wise expectations from such setup
 * Should the BGP Flap be handled as part of SI-00023262 by ERE or the existing NOCC ticket B-V-651W28R?
 * Do you foresee any other potential optimizations, taking into consideration apparently QR is turned off expectedly here?

summary: {F-CS-10687499} - ESSL machines attempting to connect to Freeflow MCH when SR map LL results aren't present
description:
* Domain: www.ewtn.com
 * CP: 1753510
 * Edgekey/Slot: e315521.dscb.akamaiedge.net
 * Property: ewtn-production
 * Their setup is using OIPACL and perf Sureroute (default map).

 
Whenever the SR low-level map results aren't in the edge (l or m logged in f40), we're attempting to go forward to MCH in Freeflow, which leads to SSL errors. After failing the MCH FF connection attempts the Edge is trying to connect direct to Origin, which will end up in one of 2 scenarios:
 
 # If the edge is part of the OIPACL we'll get a successful response from Origin
 # If the edge is not part of the OIPACL list it throws ERR_NON_SUPERNET_IP and the request results in an actual 503 error for the client.

 
 
Based on the log analysis it doesn't look region specific(nor is it really reproducible at will), the only pattern is the missing SR LL map whenever the ESSL edge attempts to connect to FF MCH

summary: 1000+ ESSL machines report low swap space alerts
description:
ERE team, NOCC reported an increase number of ESSL machines report low swap space alerts in the last 3-4 weeks. 

[https://alerts.akamai.com/adms/detail.jsp?definition_id=355]
The existing procedure suggested to restart ghost or reos to resolve this alert. It works on some machines but some continue to report this same alert.

We attempted to reos with no_preserve on ~800 machines. Since then, we see about 10% of machines continue to report the same alert after reos.

summary - 
Customer is experiencing an influx of VPF errors on MCDN regions in FRA. These increase in errors seems to line up with some odd flit events where the same traffic seems to cause a 4x+ hike in flit traffic, generally seen on a few cpcodes
1. requested presrpead be used on said cpcodes
2. FOM the regions to 65%

Post that event there was still flyte spikes which seemed to line up with the VPFs. Looking at the ddc logs for these requests , there  is no increase in hits and no influx of any cpcodes, yet flytes jump.
1. ghost ticket opened to see what could cause this
2. working with RA to see what can be done to leave scale factor or equivalent up to predict these jumps in load.
resolution_description: removed sensitive variables from the golf config which was the larger driver of flit usage and larger usage of these variables
root_cause: There was spin lock occurring that fell in line with the amount of sensitive variables being used caused large amounts of flit spikes and ultimately leading to customer VPF on their MCDN regions
creator: Archanna Sivakumar
mitigation_plan: mitigated by sensitive variables removal on gold config
longterm_mitigation: SI-00023379 - for phase2 and 3 action items

summary: Recurring QUIC_STREAM_UNKNOWN_APPLICATION_ERROR_CODE
description:
Hello

Problem report by CSE follows:

~~~

[Symptoms]
ERR_HTTP2_ERROR|QUIC_STREAM_UNKNOWN_APPLICATION_ERROR_CODE error observed with 0 bytes.

[Findings]
 - The error is confirmed approximately {_}2.5% of total H3 requests for two days log{_}.
 - The error occurred to multiple clients with 200 and 302 status codes, especially served 0 bytes (Content bytes served).
 - _And the error was also observed mostly with a specific user agent type: "BYTEL/espace Client Mobile*."_

 - It is hard to find the information regarding the error "ERR_HTTP2_ERROR|QUIC_STREAM_UNKNOWN_APPLICATION_ERROR_CODE" via internal documents.

 - When I searched for that externally, I am not sure but it looks related to "Application Protocol Error Code" in RESET_STREAM and STOP_SENDING Frames.

logs here: [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10658026-ER]
~~~~~

We want to confirm if this error could be caused by a Ghost self-suspension or anything platform related issue or whether it is more likely related to client app behavior since the error is observed with just a specific U-A? Google says:
{noformat}
The error code QUIC_STREAM UNKNOWN APPLICATION ERROR_CODE is a generic message indicating that the application layer, running over the QUIC transport protocol, terminated a stream for a reason it could not map to a standard or known error code.{noformat}
Thanks

resolution_description: Review client's HTTP/3 protocol handling
root_cause: Client side reset behaviour

summary: Discrepancy in the Footprint ID Reporting in CW Region (r53162:FABRIC‑TYO22f)
description:
I’m reaching out to get your insights on a recent observation made on the newly deployed CW region in JP, *r53162:FABRIC‑TYO22f* in the CW Footprint ID(s) reporting.
Since it began serving traffic on December 19, 2025, this region has been reporting load for all SGJP footprints (using the SGJP dual maprule) under FP1006 — the generic footprint ID of _cw‑d‑sgjp_ — instead of the specific customer CW footprint IDs. FP1006 is typically used when CW is included in the delivery workflow without a proper quota assigned, so it should not normally be reporting traffic. 
The reporting appears correct for JP VOD and JP Live footprints, which are mapped to their respective FP IDs. However, none of the SGJP footprints are showing up under the expected footprint IDs.
From the logs, both the ARL ID and ARL Version are reported correctly. The issue lies with the FP ID, which consistently shows as 1006 for all requests served under the cw‑d‑sgjp maprule. Additionally, the cache‑manager tool indicates that machines in this region are consuming more disk space under fp1006, +[https://cache-manager.akamai.com/?host=23.219.159.60&operation=store_footprint_id_stats]+
At the moment, this issue seems isolated to this region ({+}[https://www.nocc.akamai.com/miniurl/?id=29243]{+}) as other regions in the same ecor are reporting correctly. Since this is a newly deployed region, I’m not sure if the behavior is due to any misconfiguration issue, but I haven’t seen this kind of reporting anomaly before with other new deployments.
 
Any idea on what could be happening here ?
 
Below is the discrepancy in the log reporting on top cpcodes and hostnames for FP1006 on r53162 vs another JP CW region, r44814:SDN-TYO2m. The _hostname,_ _v.tiktokcdn.com_ is part of the Tiktok FP with ID:33 while getting reported under FP1006 in the concerned region.

summary: Investigation on 503 spike for a live event
description:
*Issue Description*

The customer / IAT team reported a spike in 5xx errors occurring between 15:15 and 15:17 Dec. 19th UTC.

!503spike.jpeg|width=571,height=189!

*Impact*
 * End users received a significant number of 5xx responses during a short time window.
 * Despite fail action being configured, approximately 40,000 HTTP 503 responses were served.
 * Approximately 3,000 HTTP 504 responses were also recorded.

*Analysis / Findings*
 * The primary error observed was HTTP 503, delivered to end users.
 * Error spike duration was brief (~1 minute) but high in volume.
 * HTTP 504 errors were also present, though at a lower volume (~3K).
 * Tracing logs there are errors with ERR_READ_ERROR|fwdStateFree and it seems MPE amplifed the issue (1)
 * There are also SSL connect timeout errors between Akamai midgress regions (2)

(1) For errors related to ERR_READ_ERROR|fwdStateFree symptom is similar to [https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/DPEREQ-355] 

[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10725166_tracelog] has end to end logs. Can you please verify if this is the same case?

(2) For SSL connect timeout, it shows strange request flow. Sample log shows child server went to mch and chapacf. They all went to the same CW server. And the CW server went to ch210 which is the same mch region 48062.

[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10725166_tracelog2] has details for that. From Akatec analysis the region 48062 experienced a sudden overload of requests for www.tiktok.com, which led to a sharp increase in hits and flits. This transient spike appears to have caused resource pressure on machines in the region, following which multiple nodes entered self-suspension as a protective measure.

IAT wants to clairfy some questions on the issue (2).
 # When the suspended flags were set, did we still serve the traffic? If so can we please understand the reason for this?
 # Can we please understand why it took time for the underline mapper to shift the traffic to a better region? 
 # What are we doing to ensure that this issue do not re surface?

[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10725166] has more information on the impact.
resolution_description: Downstream impact while significant, was very brief lasting under 40 seconds. Given the current RA feedback cycle times, traffic cannot be shifted sooner by mapper, but will need to rely on product/config workarounds to use alternate path.
root_cause: Overload of a Cloud Interconnect region due to attack on TikTok resulted in self-selfsuspension of multiple machines in the region. Lack of failover path at GCI resulted in 5xx downstream due to negative cache.
creator: Dimitris Kim
mitigation_plan: n/a
longterm_mitigation: Config optimizations to workaround issues at CI tier

Error:  104 - ECONNRESET: Connection reset by peer

 

Good number of requests latched to forward requests and avoiding forward connections but there were too many fwd requests in one second. 

Checking the cpu and flit load of the machine 23.55.163.155, it looks normal during the issue time. 

We are trying to understand how the situation could be avoided for the customer for future instances if customer triggeres a similar scenario. 

About the specific behavior where huge number of requests hit the edge regions at same time. Customer said :
"Typically, one of the (short) teasers is activated at 18:55, shortly before the news. At that time, a large audience is expected to be tuned in. Viewers are invited to press the green button on their remote to switch to ZDF’s internet platform and watch a dedicated movie or show. I do not know how many TVs are tuned in at that time, which makes it difficult for me to estimate the number of more or less simultaneous requests."

We are planning to suggest a few things to prevent similar situation in the future.  
 # Pre-warm cache with expected cacheable objects so that the number of forward requests can be reduced. 
 # Introduce another layer of cache to [TD1] catch requests before going to origin. 

In case of MCH, our understanding is that url hash is created to route traffic to specific MCH machine. Is there no default retry mechanism to another MCH machine/region before going to origin? [Configuration here has normal TD enabled and no Siteshield/OIPACL]

Could you confirm the Connection resets here is because of large number of new connections hitting the same server 23.55.163.155 ? 

Is there any other recommendations to handle the client request behavior in this case? 

Log analysis [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10707321_16] 

Customer had similar situation on Dec 12th [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10707321]

summary: China mapping to HK poor performance
description:
Hello GPO,

Problem report from customer:

~~~

Customer reported slowness in response for traffic going via Akamai. Requests sent directly to the origin server responded quickly.

Hostname - [www.dior.cn|https://www.dior.cn/]

Few reported paths -

/zh_cn/fashion/store/rest/applet_cdc/V1/mp/applet-menu/config.
/zh_cn/fashion/store/rest/V2/mp/catalog/categoryTreeV2
/zh_cn/fashion/store/campaign/OpenSearch/reports

Customer stated that latency is noticed specifically by China Mobile ISP users.

Issue Start Time - Dec 18, 2025
Issue End Time - Ongoing

When we tried checking mapping aspect, we checked the HATS tool and we could see a shift in traffic from China regions to HK regions after Dec 18. This timeline aligns with what customer reported as well.

CN regions which were serving traffic earlier can be seen still but a higher concentration of requests seems to be going to HK compared to before Dec 18 and we suspect this is causing increased latency.

HATS: [https://www.nocc.akamai.com/miniurl/?id=292b2]

[https://mapper.akamai.com/ip/#from%3D1766047300010%26to%3D1767170535705%26treeType%3DA%26mrule%3D489%26viperSlot%3D40087%26cidr%3D218.203.69.238%26resolver%3Dip%26useGMTTime%3Dtrue%26]

Considering there is a significant shift in traffic and it is impacting customer traffic, can we tweak the mapping to prefer some China regions? The top DNS going to HK regions seem to be mostly from China (see attached).

Logs: https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10747078

~~~

Thanks
executive_summary: China mobile users mapping to HK routinely
root_cause: Increase flit consumption from Samsung CPCode -7960 since mid December is causing the china regions to run full and forcing other customer traffic OOC impacting perf.
creator: Rahul Sawarkar
mitigation_plan: Working with Samsung IAT to work on problematic config to alleviate the current situation.
longterm_mitigation: Customer to follow guidelines as china-cdn is EOL.

Sample request at *09:24 UTC* encountered {{{}ERR_READ_TIMEOUT | before_resp_body{}}}.

The origin returned {*}HTTP 200{*}, but only *425,687 bytes* were sent, compared to the expected {*}2,080,313 bytes{*}, which was consistent across multiple previous requests.

*cURL response headers* were not captured during the incident. To check for EOF, cache logs were reviewed; however, these logs have now been rolled out.

Client-facing (r-line) and origin-facing (f-line) logs confirm this is a single correlated request.

 

*Network timeout configuration:*

{{network:http.read120s}} applies {*}after origin connection and headers are received{*}.

Akamai successfully received headers, but body stalled for ~120 seconds, triggering {{{}ERR_READ_TIMEOUT{}}}.

Headers were already committed → HTTP status remained 200 (expected protocol behavior).

References:
[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10764239]
[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10764239_6Jan]

_Based on discussion with customers about their origin Microsoft IIS server log had 995 win32 errors at the time which lead to the smaller than expected content size._

_However from their IIS log they said this request lasted only 6 seconds from the IIS server's perspective._

_From Akamai origin f line we saw 122 seconds_

 

_*Similarities to Prior Incidents: [https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/ERE-2262*_]
_Reference: *F-CS-8650754 – ERR_READ_TIMEOUT before_resp_body*_
 * _Origin returned 200 OK_

 * _Origin read timed out → {{ERR_READ_TIMEOUT | before_resp_body}} in f-line_

 * _f-line object status {{L}} (object deletion due to content-length mismatch)_

_This incident aligns closely with_ _*ERE-2262*_ _behavior, *except this time the object was ~425 KB (not 0 bytes).*_
executive_summary: Akamai received an HTTP 200 response from the origin but timed out after approximately 122 seconds with the error message ERR_READ_TIMEOUT | before_resp_body. Instead of logging an origin 0xx error after the timeout, Akamai retained the 200 response and cached an incomplete object.
creator: Rashida Pathan

summary: Region overloaded issues during Super Bowl for NBC
description:
The we observed an issue during a Peacock Exclusive event on Dec. 27th @ 21:23 ET and 21:59 ET. We raised a NOCC Ticket for the second instance where they had confirmed 51473 was over loaded during the timeframe due to high volume of requests for hostnames tiktokcdn.com & fts.rbxcdn.com. 
        *•*        During this timeframe, a few client aborts were observed, with slowness occurring across multiple mid-tier clusters.
        *•*        The issue was traced to CW regions and confirmed not to be related to the origin.
        *•*        Several SSL timeouts (ERR_SSL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT) originated from a single parent region, resulting in 200 ERR_SSL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT delivery errors.

summary: Large number of machine for 22.4.0 ESSL phase one timed out on mdt-agent update
description:
During phase 1 checklisting, we saw large number of ESSL machine reported suspendflag 1024.  It happened on FF network too. (report 2048 instead). Investigation shows:
 * The issue was *not* seen when Ghost was suspended but mdtagent *was* running. The issue *was* seen when Ghost was serving traffic but mdtagent was {*}stopped{*}. The mdtagent is likely not involved in this errant behaviour.
 * Israth is trying to setup a QA machine to reproduce the issue, she is installing machines now and analyzing the traffic seen on the machine exhibiting the increased mdt processing times.  She has seen that there is TikTok POC traffic with client aborts, which may lead to requests still downloading data after the client closed – are the downloads/requests not being freed?
 * Further discussion: is this X8-specific issue: not clear as most machines on both FF and ESSL are X8s (FF = 78K/127K total, ESSL = 50K/78K total). John reported that a couple of X7s are also reporting this behaviour. Instead of hardware-related, perhaps resource-related (running out of resources due to the client aborts??) Still to be definitively determined.
 * MC for baseline has been filed
creator: John Pan

summary: fail-action2 forward request ignores lma.origin-edge off flag
description:

However, the configuration (AMD-livecloud.akamaized.net) indicates that “Supports gzip compression” is set to “No.” The customer has requested clarification on how these requests could occur despite this setting.


Checking this further on an internal configuration Akatec noticed that the issue happnes when fail action triggered.

- Content size: 23553 (unzip), 127 (gzip)

executive_summary: We investigated the issue and, with code validation from Dennis, confirmed that fail_action2 copies the client request headers into the forward request and does not remove compression headers when 'lma.origin-edge' is set to off. We have tested and confirm that disabling 'lma.accept-gzip-from-origin' is an effective temporary workaround until the behaviour is corrected.

summary: RET+XFER Increase after enabling APISEC on ajdacent domain
description:
Hello GPO

Please refer to attached screen shot about traffic peak.

It seems that RET and XFER time are causing  high flit purely because of the change made by applying API security.

Customer ‘Coupang Co.,Ltd.’ reported that the request end time and transfer time of [cmapi.coupang.com|https://cmapi.coupang.com/] (CPcode 1589472) have increased since Jan 7, 20:00 UTC.
At 20:00 UTC Jan 7, API security was deployed from API security and security configuration API SC v310. 

We are monitoring [cmapi.coupang.com|https://cmapi.coupang.com/] using traffic peak, it shows request end time and transfer time have increased. (Traffic peak’s time zone is KST.) Mapping is local within KR.

CSE checked CPcode 1589472’s flit dashboard, and it showed flit, F2B, F2H have increased.
[https://grafana-dmz.akam.ai/org477/dashboard/db/country-high-flit-usage-cpcodes?from=1767393243395&to=1767915330278&var-country=KR&var-network=ff&var-account=Coupang%20Co.,Ltd.&var-cpcode=1589472&var-threshold=5]

The other domain [mercury.coupang.com|https://mercury.coupang.com/] (CPcode 1723882) with security configuration Oncall SC 173v for this domain had API Security enabled at the similar time stamp,
but API security configuration was not  applied to this domain. CPcode 1723882’s flit dashboard, it also showed flit, F2B, F2H have been increased after API security enabled.

[https://grafana-dmz.akam.ai/org477/dashboard/db/country-high-flit-usage-cpcodes?from=1767393243395&to=1767915330278&var-country=KR&var-network=ff&var-account=Coupang%20Co.,Ltd.&var-cpcode=1723882&var-threshold=5]

Checking load graph, flit has been increased much after API security enabled.
[https://lg.netarch.akamai.com/cgi-bin/loadgraphs?period=3d&region=19101%2C22141%2C24437%2C26727%2C31010%2C32355%2C33693%2C38402%2C42926%2C46031%2C47270%2C48883%2C48921%2C48922%2C49630%2C50064%2C50458%2C51456&network=W&maprule=15211%2C15212%2C15213%2C15214%2C15215%2C15216%2C15217%2C15218%2C15219%2C15220&display=region&ymax=&utcoffset=9&utc=on]

([mercury.coupang.com|https://mercury.coupang.com/] is auto sharded, so CSE checked load graph with maprule 15211~15220. [cmapi.coupang.com|https://cmapi.coupang.com/] is using 15211 map only.)

Logs before and after API security enabled, and it shows avg flit has increased.
Request end time and transfer time also have been increased. 

Logs: etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10789847

Could you please confirm that
1. The increase in flit is caused just by enabling API security?
2. If so, whether this behavior is expected or if we can tweak anything about load distribution to bring it back to normal. The bump in latency is only 10-20msec however customer noticed it in trafficpeak and wants the same old performance.
executive_summary: RET and XFER time are causing high flit purely because of the change made by applying API security.
root_cause: Increase in response time due to security feature's (flit increase) being added to the customer config. KR regions are running flit bound and this could degraded the current state, also the inspection rules could add the delay. There were no logs provided to ascertain the same.

summary: {F-CS-10599375} Linkedin: modify ACAO rule not working after XML opt is enabled
description:
Product: Object Delivery
Config (staging v177) : [https://control.akamai.com/apps/property-manager/#/property-version/8030742/175/edit?gid=37333]

Issue:

 In v175 and v177, we have a similar rule which matches the client-request metadata stage and changes the outgoing response header ACAO to '*'

With version 177 the ACAO rule stopped working after XML optimization was enabled

 
Steps to Reproduce:
 
 - With cracker go to  URL [https://static.licdn.com/aero-v1/sc/h/8siq6sr06g1mc6ovp753jnckh]
 - Sent the request to Staging to get v177
 - you see ACAO value is "Access-Control-Allow-Origin: [https://www.linkedin.com|https://www.linkedin.com/] "   
 
 
I have collected logs, including ouiji cache.logs from Staging v177:
[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10599375]
 
line #1025
 
 
Akatec was able to replicate the same behavior in a test configuration after enabling XML Optimization in PM for the config.  Hostname [www.adivai.xyz|https://www.adivai.xyz/]

          Test URL   [https://www.adivai.xyz/test/headers]

 

 

Investigation of the issue was done already by ERE and it was requested to create a new Jira for ERE-Delivery-Portal. 

 

All the details about the issue and ERE investigation are here https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/ERE-3065
executive_summary:
- modify ACAO rule not working after XML opt is enabled
https://docs.google.com/document/d/14jxj-8sHTNz3wSn2eVQMc6mWHUcT_tbg/edit#heading=h.nbhahd8xpd10
resolution_description: Updated the configuration in v178 by removing the match:metadata-stage = client-request condition, allowing the header modification to occur at the correct stage. This restored the expected ACAO header behavior.
root_cause: The issue occurred due to incorrect configuration where response headers (ACAO) were being modified at the client-request metadata stage, where response headers are not available. This behavior previously appeared to work due to legacy template behavior, but enabling XML Optimization enforced stricter stage execution and exposed the misconfiguration.
creator: Cesar Roque Quiros
mitigation_plan: Validated configuration changes and confirmed correct behavior post-fix. Communicated the correct usage of metadata stages to avoid similar misconfigurations.
longterm_mitigation: Introduce validation checks, warnings, or improved documentation in Property Manager to prevent configuring response header modifications at unsupported metadata stages. This will help avoid similar issues when stricter processing features like XML Optimization are enabled.

executive_summary:
I do see that the original request is served from negative cache and a fail-action is triggered, but the fail-action requests are “latched” to the original negatively cached response and I see the the fail-action metadata includes no-store.
Recommended adjust no-store in fail-action metadata to allow the edge to forward and process fail-action requests. Also review negative cache settings to ensure fail-action logic is not bypassed.
root_cause:
If a request is marked with no-store in fail action metadata, the edge will not cache the error response, so subsequent requests will not hit negative cache. However, if negative cache is already present for a URL, fail action requests may be latched to the original negative cached object, and the fail action may not execute as expected.
For fail-action to work, the edge must be allowed to forward the request and process/store the response.
creator: Tyler Deary
mitigation_plan: Adjust fail-action metadata by removing/relaxing no-store so the edge can forward requests and properly execute failover instead of latching to negative cache.
longterm_mitigation: Refine configuration to align fail-action and negative caching behavior, ensuring failover logic isn’t bypassed due to cached error responses.

The configuration should have failover to backup at each tier. 

We can explain the error spike in that one of the Fastly origin IPs (146.75.93.188) suddenly began returning 0xx FIRST_BYTE_TIMEOUT errors (the other Fastly origin servers appeared healthy). However, edge request analysis showed that requests were not consistently executing failover, which after speaking with the EA we learned is a byproduct of enough requests upstream erroring, and the failover requests bypassing the td tier were going forward to the same problematic origin server. 

Looking further upstream to the td tier there were 2 things preventing edge from fetching a healthy segment request from the td0 tier:

1. 17% of the requests to the backup (Syncbak) origin were returning a 403 response from the origin. This is something we're pursuing with the customer, and not the focus of this jira.
2. In instances where td went forward to the Syncbak origin and successfully returned a 200, ghost still did not return a 200 successful response to the edge


On point 2 here is a sample instance to illustrate. I'm grepping on a segment name, and looking at all log lines requesting or serving that segment from a metrocache td0. There are a number of instances here where the Syncbak origin returns a 200 and receives the full content body, however there is no successful response returned to the edge.

executive_summary:
CBS removed Akamai from the CDN rotation during their coverage of the NFL playoffs on Saturday 1/17/26 after a moderate spike in edge 504 errors. After review it looks as though failover to the customer's configured backup origin is working with relative success but 200 responses are not being returned to the edge causing negatively cached 504 responses to be served at the edge in the presence of an origin error spike.

I do see that the original request is served from negative cache and a fail-action is triggered, but the fail-action requests are “latched” to the original negatively cached response and I see the the fail-action metadata includes no-store.
Recommended adjust no-store in fail-action metadata to allow the edge to forward and process fail-action requests. Also review negative cache settings to ensure fail-action logic is not bypassed.
root_cause:
If a request is marked with no-store in fail action metadata, the edge will not cache the error response, so subsequent requests will not hit negative cache. However, if negative cache is already present for a URL, fail action requests may be latched to the original negative cached object, and the fail action may not execute as expected.
For fail-action to work, the edge must be allowed to forward the request and process/store the response.
creator: Mike Shea
mitigation_plan: Fix the configuration by removing the invalid metadata-stage constraint and ensuring response headers are modified only in supported stages
longterm_mitigation: Introduce validation, warnings, and improved documentation in Property Manager/Optimize XML to prevent unsupported configurations and enforce correct stage usage.

summary: {F-CS-10735111} Issues when multiple failover behaviours match
description:
Hello ERE team,

 

We're having a problem with some tags in failover metadata, when multiple failover behaviours are matched and last match win is expected.

1. *Query String:*

When the failover behaviour sets "Include Query String" to ON, then that generates the tag <preserve-query-string>on</preserve-query-string> .
But there is no way to revert this setting: when "Include Query String" is set to OFF, I'd expect it generates a <preserve-query-string>off</preserve-query-string> . But in reality, no preserve-query-string tag is generated -> the earlier setting persists unchanged. The setting promises to "do not *include* query string", but the behaviour is actually "do not change the last applied setting for qs" - that can be misleading. So if at any point (an earlier match on another failover behaviour) preserve-query-string got set to ON, the request gets stuck with this setting.

 


2. *Failover path:*

It is similar but a little more subtle with Modify Request Path: when set to YES it generates the <path> tag, when set to NO it doesn't generate any tag. I guess there's two ways the custoemr could interpret "Modify Request Path: NO":
A do not modify the failover path at all-> that is, preserve the original pre-failover request path
B do not modify the failover path here -> that is, whatever failover path has been set (in previous match) that value remains. 

The real behaviour is B, although the behaviour tooltip suggests A.
Anyway, if the customer uses a logic where several failover behaviours match, first with modified path then with preserved, then they need workarounds to actually preserve the pre-failover path.
This  can get further complicated further if QS settings also vary between these failovers.

Technically, this aligns with last match win rule https://docs.akamai.com/esp/user/edgesuite/guides/Metadata_html/index.html if you apply it on tag level, rather than on behaviour level. But customers don't have access to xml, so this can get confusing.


*Is it intentional for these behaviour settings to generate metadata like that? Can this be improved?*


Here is a test setup with a few scenarios: pincer-dev-clone-aberdin-test.com v101 (stg).
(account: Akamai Professional Services)

 

+Behaviour vs metadata:+
 * modify path and preserve qs - both tags are generated -> OK

!image-2026-01-20-17-04-33-215.png|width=639,height=339!
{code:java}

executive_summary:
We're having a problem with some tags in failover metadata when multiple failover behaviors are matched and last match win is expected.
Issue is that the pm behavior doesn't generate path tag when option modify incoming path = no and it doesn't generate preserve-query-string tag when option include incoming qs = no
Thus, when a request activated the behavior with one of this option = yes, the tag it generates remains active even when a subsequent behavior is activated with same option = no
It seems like the solution involves fixing the metadata generated by PM, 
Though we tested the tag <preserve-query-string>off</preserve-query-string>  separately and it seems working.

I have raised a https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/DPEXREQ-1128, We can follow-up there.
root_cause:
The ticket was raised to understand when you set "Include Query String" to Yes in UI, it will generate tag <preserve-query-string>on</preserve-query-string>. If you set to No, it does not generate any tag.
what is happening, A request first matches on failover with Include QS Yes, the tag gets applied, but then it matches on another failover, with Include QS No. This is where it breaks. Once you set this behaviour to Yes, there is no way to override it further down in the config.

Tested that tag preserve-query-string>off</preserve-query-string separately, and raised DPEXREQ ticket to understand if this is something intentionally by design or if it requires changes.

summary: Intermittent connection timeouts to some Brazil regions
description:
Customer reported intermittent throughput drop on Dec 20th and 21st during different time periods. All these timeframes correlate to an increase in load for r47504:FABRIC-GRU1u. Reviewing the loadgraph for maprules, we noticed some spikes for unassigned traffic. The customer also uses load balancing to control their traffic to different CDNs, so the CNAME wasn't pointing to an edgekey hostname, as seen below. That LBCDN CNAME used to return Akamai IP addresses. 

{code:java}
$ dig +short mb.api.pagseguro.uol
lbcdn-mb.api.pagseguro.uol.
104.18.2.30
104.18.3.30
{code}

Given the unassigned traffic, we suggested adding reporting:maprule-host with the edgekey hostname, which was activated on Jan 8th. 

Even after that change, they reported throughput drops and also had multiple 5-second connect timeouts on their "health" requests. 
https://mb.api.pagseguro.uol/actuator/health

We didn't get more details on the throughput drop; however received the following for connection timeout samples, along with the server IP. 
* 01/10 15:06:05 - IP 2.20.132.66 (HERO=2.18.20.130) (IG 4) is in region 49247 (SDN-GRU21j) ESSL (DNS:RX)
* 01/11 19:09:08 - IP 23.63.250.165 (HERO=23.62.50.37) (IG 1) is in region 52099 (FABRIC-GRU12w) ESSL (DNS:RX)
* 01/12 01:03:07 - IP 23.63.250.20 (HERO=23.193.118.148) (IG 10) is in region 52100 (FABRIC-GRU12x) ESSL (DNS:RX)

We reviewed load graphs for these regions, and we were able to see a spike in traffic, mainly for MR 1327, around that time. DNSP showed self-suspension for the first 2 timeframes, but the 3rd one didn't have any self-suspensions. 
Links can be found from line 290 here: https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10780845

Reviewing cache.log, we see an increase in AVG manager cycle for the 1st example (going as high as 42k), while the 2nd and 3rd didn't have the spikes.

summary: Dior Config review for - SI-00023426
description:
Ask was to look to see if there was anything in the config that could be tuned to help in the scenario  of oocm mapping - request back is to give any specific examples that are not oocm related / cap related  - SPECIFICALLY in relation to china.

 

PSG suggestion was already put in chat - 

1.The srto is missing from origin, that needs to be fixed

2.they are not using akadns88/edgekey88  which is for compliance in china

3.SS map includes eu servers but does not request anything but china regions

4.lots of data is put into the flex cache key but we are not forcing eccu purge so we likely are not getting optimal caching

5.this could be confirmed but i think image manager is not in china so all those requests have to leave the country to get filled

6.Netstorage origin dior-common is in london and New Jersey

7.does cloudflare have china service? We use [stores.dior.cn.pagescdn.com|https://stores.dior.cn.pagescdn.com/] as an origin which is served by cloudflare

8.ohd and lowering retries can help us and them
executive_summary: Look to see if there is any obvious perf improvements that could help general performance
resolution_description: beyond some other optimizations PSG suggested, adding a few more APJ SS regions could help reduce latency to China Origin if we are OOC, gives more options loccally.
root_cause: SI action item to review DIOR config to see if there are any general improvements that could help in times of ooc.
creator: Kyle Griffin

summary: {F-CS-10786478} MSFT: OIPACL OOC mapping
description:
Configuration: storeedgefd.dsx.mp.microsoft.com_hc

Product: DD + GTM

 

Around Jan 7 , 09:40 GMT, customer reported spike in traffic going to US datacenter.  We could see at the same time spike in 0xx, 5xx and slow requests. 

Checking the logs we found end users in HK going to DC in US because the OIPACL region mapping changed from region located in HK to a region located in US.

The same behavior was found for regions in Amsterdam going to the US datacenter.

 

For example, we found the parent region 45795 geo located in US Santa Clara had suddenly started picking high traffic:  [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-10786478]  line 178 and 191

 

You can see it in hats as well
