summary: Daily peak flit spikes in r53419 causing increased latency for Amazon
description:
Customer reported that they noticed increased latency in the IAD region daily around 1 UTC. We reviewed the logs, and we noticed intermittent spikes in the number of requests taking more than 5 seconds. 

Checking the edge region/ IPs showing high response time, we noticed r53419 standing out with a high number of requests. We also see multiple machines with high latency for r53419.
{code:java}
[fsalazar@lsg-gss13 ~/F-CS-11072915]$ zcat CP1642358-202603110030-23.33.25.197-356-1773696623.gz | awk '2=="r" && !($16~/[fGKPX]/ || $53~/m/) && !($11~/^(10\.|127\.0\.0\.1)/) && $5+$6+$7>4000 {print $1}; $2=="S" && !($18~/[fGKPX]/ ) && !($11~/^(10\.|127\.0\.0\.1)/) && $5+$6+$7>4000 {print $1}' | xargs region | awk '{print $8, $9, $10}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
   1478 region 53419 (FABRIC-IAD51j)
     69 region 49579 (FABRIC-MIA22s)
     29 region 49926 (FABRIC-MIA32b)
     17 region 49689 (SDN-YTO1c)
     16 region 51472 (FABRIC-ATL4c)
     14 region 51174 (FABRIC-DFW14g)
     13 region 9987 (UNSACV-MTY2)
     13 region 50535 (FABRIC-GRU12h)
     11 region 44133 (SDN-QROf)
     10 region 49257 (FABRIC-EWR43j)
     10 region 41964 (IZZI-MTY)

[seselvan@lsg-gss13 /home/fsalazar/F-CS-11072915]$ zcat CP1642358-202603110030-23.33.25.197-356-1773696623.gz | awk '2=="r" && !($16~/[fGKPX]/ || $53~/m/) && !($11~/^(10\.|127\.0\.0\.1)/) && $5+$6+$7>4000 {print $1}; $2=="S" && !($18~/[fGKPX]/ ) && !($11~/^(10\.|127\.0\.0\.1)/) && $5+$6+$7>4000 {print $1}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head
     46 2.17.114.13
     44 23.7.250.203
     42 2.17.114.30
     40 2.17.114.29
     39 23.7.250.145
     34 2.17.114.201
     32 23.7.250.222
     31 2.17.114.5
     29 2.17.114.208
     28 2.17.114.28
{code}

We reviewed a couple of log lines (segment and manifest requests), and we see a high request end time, even going forward to peer. We also saw zero-size object errors from different peers.
Sample logs can be found in etherpad: https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11072915_SPOE

[Loadgraph shows daily flit increases|https://lg.netarch.akamai.com/cgi-bin/loadgraphs?period=1w&region=53419&network=A&maprule=&display=total&ymax=&utcoffset=-6&diskcpu=on] with some self-suspensions from 02/27 when this region started getting heavy traffic. Looking back, it looks like most of the machines were brought online on 02/13 for this large region, based on [Netarch|https://netarch.akamai.com/region/FABRIC-IAD51j]. 

[Mapper historical grapher|https://map.akamai.com/cgi-bin/FreeFlow/Analysis/HDB_Server.pl?startmonth=3&startday=10&startyear=2026&starthour=22&startmin=0&endmonth=3&endday=11&endyear=2026&endhour=4&endmin=0&param1=53419&dbname=production&param2=&param3=&param4=&display=graph&normalize=none&ptdisp=normal&yaxis=y-axis&size=large&scope=all&query_name=REGION_BY_MAPRULE_FLYTELOAD&customSql=] shows high flit from MR 122 (Hulu edge map) followed by MR 19 (ByteDance US-only video edge map). This can be seen yesterday during peak hours as well. 

We pulled ghost and cache.log for one of the machines, and we can see CPU, flit and AVG manager cycle having spikes intermittently for this region, aligning with intermittent latency spikes. https://deadpool.akamai.com/edgelogminer/modern-view?task_id=fd701275-7db1-46fd-87f5-f6bbba1ca8ee

Reviewing top CPcodes, we see Hulu cpcode 1628770 (part of Disney account) having big spikes compared to other CPcodes during that time. 
 !image-2026-03-17-18-09-45-754.png|width=100%! 

{code:java}
[seselvan@lsg-gss6 ~]$ cpcode 1628770
cpcode      : 1628770
cpname      : hulu.vod
contentcode : 1628770
contentname : hulu.vod
clientname  : W-O8K658
masteracg   : W-O8K658
accountname : Disney Streaming Services
tier        : A+
{code}

Looking at FOM, we see this region has 0.8, so should we reduce FOM to mitigate these daily peaks of flit overload, causing latency for Amazon?

{code:java}
sg-gss13 ~/F-CS-11072915]$ date;agg map-dev "select region, flit_overflow_mark from m2RegionOverflowMarks where region IN (53419)"
Tue Mar 17 17:40:47 UTC 2026
region flit_overflow_mark
------ ------------------
53419 0.8
{code}

Also, are there any actions that can be taken to prevent similar issues in the future? Let us know if you need any further info/ analysis.
executive_summary: Customer reported that they noticed increased latency in the IAD region daily around 1 UTC. We reviewed the logs, and we noticed intermittent spikes in slow requests mainly from r53419. We see CPU/ flit and AVG manager cycle having intermittent spikes during that time. Should we reduce FOM to mitigate the issue? Are there any actions that can be taken to prevent similar issues in the future?
resolution_description:
Kernel team to roll out a kernel tweak and for a switch firmware fix which should address the root cause.
The ETA for the kernel rollout, before 03/27.
root_cause: r53419 ahve the backend less problem which leads to ghostmon suspending ghosts which don’t need to be suspended.
creator: Senthuran Selvanayagam
mitigation_plan:
Kernel team to roll out a kernel tweak and a switch firmware fix.
The ETA for the kernel rollout, before 03/27
longterm_mitigation: NA

My main concern here is, should we even be retrying alternate paths for an explicit 504 from Origin?. We connected and got a response, so there were no network/path issues and yet SR is retrying. That can't be intended behavior

Can you confirm that this is unintended behavior?. What would be the best way to stop the alternate path retries  for an Origin 5xx in this scenario?.

I suspect this might've been introduced due to the fix on DPEREQ-355  and [corresponding rollout |https://collaborate.akamai.com/confluence/spaces/DynamicMedia/pages/1257888826/Rollout+Plan+Introduce+HTTP+Status+Codes+to+Origin+IP+ACL+Acceptance+Criteria]

Also I know it's a bit of a gray area. Let me know if I should open a SRMM ticket for the SR folks instead. Thanks!.

===

Another sample here: [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/ER-263671]
Full cachelog for all machines reqID 3889dbef   : LSG 14 - /home/jpadilla/ER-263671/
executive_summary: So the retries on 504 are as expected due to the change deployed as a part of DPEREQ-355 and the ghost does not have a way to selectively apply fallback using acceptance-criteria based on the source of the 5xx status code. We never expect a Ghost to be entirely offline, if we receive a 504 from upstream (whether origin or parent) and the 504 is configured in metadata to mean that parent route is dead, then that is how it goes further.
root_cause: The retries on 504 are as expected due to the change deployed as a part of DPEREQ-355 and the ghost does not have a way to selectively apply fallback using acceptance-criteria based on the source of the 5xx status code.
creator: Javier Padilla
mitigation_plan: Nothing from ERE side
longterm_mitigation: Nothing from ERE side

summary: High RET on EW Subrequest http call
description:
Hello Folks
Affected hostname : webmail.cma-cgm.com
 
Context: Customer is using third party service called DataDome (similar to BMP). The request flow looks like as follows: (Attaching snapshot as well)
1) Client makes a request to webmail.cma-cgm.com
2) Request reached Edge and according Edge worker configuration another request is being made for /validate-request path (3rd party BOTMAN solution)
3) This /validate-request path reaches datadome (origin), it validates and serves the response (deny or allow request)
4) Based on this the original request is either allowed go to origin or send response back to client.
 
Concern:
The customer has started observing elevated latency for approximately 1% of the requests reaching their DataDome service.
 
The IAT team disabled SiteShield to remove the additional hop that could have been contributing to latency. Following this change, response times improved for the 50th, 75th, and 95th percentiles. However, the 99th percentile—representing roughly 1% of requests—continues to show elevated latency.
 
Metric/Benchmark of concern: Requests that are taking more than 300 ms. This creates a security hole for the customer - the 300 ms is a limit set at the EW code itself, if the request coming from a client takes more than 300ms to get a response from DD , their EW code considers it as a fail open.


Below is one sample request that takes too long with :

summary: GRN is missing request id when the url-too-large error was denied by WAF

summary: FOM tuning guidelines ahead of IPL
description:
The IAT has asked us to engage ERE on a few points which would help us better prepare for the upcoming IPL events. 

As suggested in *ERE-3237* backup maps for the existing Web/API Maps ({*}Ch7, Ch42, S250{*}) have been added to better handle potential traffic spikes.

The back map for *ch7 is ch8* and backup map for {*}ch42 & s250 is ch43{*}. The split between ch42 and s250 remains 50:50. This change is in staging and is expected to be fully implemented before IPL. 

All FOM changes in place using the previous [guideline|https://collaborate.akamai.com/confluence/spaces/EPRE/pages/1345968190/FOM+Reduction+-+IN+Event+Delivery+-+Guidelines+for+NOCC+Tier3] provided in *ERE-3207* have been reverted. 

*Ask to ERE:*
We are seeking guidance from ERE to:
1) Revalidate whether any FOM tuning or optimizations are required for the India for primary maps looking ahead to IPL.
2) If FOM reduction is to be applied in similar scenarios can ERE please provide us with a similar guideline or instructions for doing so during Event Support.
resolution_description: Provided the guidelines and completed the proactive FOM reduction for regions part of e;s250 and a;chc1
root_cause: Preparation for IPL tournament based on the issues observed in T20 WC
creator: Tyler Deary
mitigation_plan: Proactive FOM reduction on regions serving spiky traffic
longterm_mitigation: Enhancement of a feature - using MPG ID as key rather than Pingpoint while constructing scorelist - this would help in spreading the forward requests more evenly/balanced

executive_summary:
The migration project involved moving EIPB (Edge IP Binding) configurations for Sharp Corporation from a source contract to a destination contract within the same account. The migration was successfully executed on April 15, 2026, as scheduled. The activity ensured that specific edge hostnames and their associated CP codes were correctly mapped to the new contract ID to maintain service continuity and billing accuracy.
Impact: No customer-facing downtime (Zero Impact).
resolution_description: The migration was completed via a controlled database script execution (DBMC),Pre-migration checks confirmed the existence of EIPB line items in the destination contract.,SQL queries were run to identify the unique IDs (134033, 134034) for the relevant hostnames.A DBMC request (ID: 5e785ea0...) was submitted and approved to update the asapmstr.acg_objects table.The master_acg_id and acg_id were successfully changed from V-4ZW1E5N to V-4ZW1E1T.
root_cause: The requirement for this activity was not a "fault" but a business-driven migration. The customer needed to consolidate or reassign their EIPB resources (prod2-limelightcdn-hro.jp.sharp and stage2-limelightcdn-hro.jp.sharp) from an old contract to a new one. In the internal system (ASAPMSTR), these objects were hard-linked to the source contract ID, necessitating a manual database update (DBMC) to re-parent them.
creator: Ritu Vijayraj
mitigation_plan: The migration date was verified against the Moratorium Calendar to avoid conflicts with global freezes.Data was extracted both before and after the update to ensure no data loss occurred during the UPDATE command.The manual DBMC served as a workaround for the lack of a self-service migration UI in the EIPB portal.
longterm_mitigation: We are already having a EIPB Migration tool in a resource migration tool but due to some ongoing issues reporter not able to use that and went for the traditional mitigation plan

summary: Connection failures for MT servers caused by high flits
description:
*Issue summary -*

Customer reported that they have experienced intermittently connectivity issue which resulted in 504 timeout on their two leg service configuration.

This service has configured spanning two legs with 1 CPcode.
 - Leg #1 : End user => Akamai => Origin (AWS, Media-Tailor called EMT)
 - Leg #2 : EMT => Akamai => Origin

*Symptoms / Problem Statement -*

The customer is experiencing intermittent connectivity issues resulting in 504 Gateway Timeouts on Leg #1. The customer reports that the 504 responses from the Origin on Leg #1 are directly caused by connection delays and exceptions occurring on Leg #2 (toward the Akamai edge).

*Technical Findings & Evidence -* 

1. Based on log analysis and region load graphs from multiple timeframes (03/25 and 03/29), the root cause points to severe resource exhaustion on specific edge regions handling Leg #2 traffic:

2. Impacted Regions: The edge IPs shared by the customer and observed in egress/ingress logs are heavily concentrated in regions r48026, r44521, r43979, r41271, and r52255.

3. Resource Exhaustion (High CPU/Flit): Cache logs show extreme resource spikes in these regions, with CPU usage frequently hitting 90-99% and Flit levels exceeding 100% (peaking over 150% in some instances).

4. SSL Handshake Failures: There is a massive correlation between the high load and SSL handshake failures. Cache logs reveal thousands of aborted and timeout handshake results between the EMT clients and the Leg #2 edges.

5. Ghost Log Confirmation: When connections to the edges are successful, ghost logs show no significant response time delays. The 504 errors on Leg #1 are exclusively stemming from the dropped/timed-out SSL connections on Leg #2 due to edge overload.

*Questions -* 

1. High flits mitigation: Based on the logs and region load graphs, confirm if there are any additional actions or configurations we can apply to mitigate the connectivity issues specifically caused by these high flits spikes.

2. FOM Adjustment: Please confirm if it is possible to adjust it for region r44521 (currently at 0.8) to better handle the potential impact of these high flit loads. Some regions already have lowered FOM but the issue also happened to those regions.
{code:java}
=> Additionally, 3 of those regions were already lowered FOM.

[dbae@lsg-gss17 ~/case/F-CS-11122260/0329]$ date; agg map "select region,flit_resource,flit_overflow_mark from m2RegionOverflowMarks where region in (48026,44520,44521,43979,52255,41271)"

6 rows selected {code}
3. Load distribution methods : The client (AWS) needs to distribute loads across a wider variety of edge IPs and regions to safely handle high RPS requests. Pre-spreading within the Region to balance loads would work in this case?

4. Previoulsy other customers who are using MT(Media Tailor) servers had issues like read timeout, MPE, in-country mapping and so on. Howerver in this case it looks like most of issues happened when there were connection failurs like ssl connection error in those regions with high flits. Their workflow is like 'end user - edge - MT - EMT - edge - customer's origin'. Is there any known issue with EMT regarding the connection failure?

 

[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11122260-ER] has more detailed information.

summary: r48921 overload causing timeouts - spinoff ERE-3226
description:
Customer (Netmarble) reported recurring TLS timeout issues, similar to incidents earlier this month. This time the impacted region is r48921.

*Issue Details:*
 * *Time:* 2026-03-26 22:00:13 ~ 22:00:58 UTC
 * *Duration:* ~45 seconds
 * *Symptom:* TLS ServerHello not returned within 3 seconds, causing timeout errors
 * *Sample URL:* {{https://cms-api.netmarble.com/api/content/402?categorySeqStr=2794&languageCd=en}} (DSA)
 * *Impacted Region:* r48921
root_cause: Hourly TWC flash traffic spike on api7 serial 2049 in r48921 (baseline ~630K req/min spiking to 1.6M req/min at hour boundaries) caused flit overload and Ghost self-suspension, resulting in TLS ServerHello timeout errors for Netmarble DSA traffic.
creator: Thilaga Raju
mitigation_plan: Lowered FOM on top regions serving the api7 map, applied maprule suspensions (w34, APIX) in affected KR regions, and increased prespread to 16 for TWC serial via MAPPINGENG-8303. Netmarble confirmed error rate dropped from ~600 to ~200 hits/hour post-mitigation and issue became non-reproducible.
longterm_mitigation: Review and optimize recurring hourly flash traffic pattern from TWC. Evaluate load-balancing across API shards instead of concentrating on a single shard. Further distribute flit-heavy traffic using MPG ID-based scorelist construction to ensure regions are placed in different positions for different MPGs of an ecor.

We escalated this issue to NOCC via [B-V-6G27CNZ|https://issues.deploy.akamai.com/cgi-bin/view.cgi?issue_id=B-V-6G27CNZ] and following is their response. 
{quote}
As you had mentioned, FRP is active as of now for the domains(including our NS and Compute object hostnames) [1] ,interestingly all of them are G2G (ghost-to-ghost) . It seems this has been active since the 29th [2] and seems to have been triggered due to excessive in-progress requests in queue . Several domains under *frndly.akamaized.net are being denied due to the said reason [3].

This isnt specific to the machine 23.47.125.164, the entire region is currently facing the onslaught of FRP trying to keep the in-progress requests in control . Even CRP seem to not tag any ARLIDs, its possible this isn't meeting any of the defined criteria. The FRP triggers are seen across the region [4] for various domains, with the common factor being G2G . This seems to be a GFI region (GHost-fault-Tolerance) and has CPG/OCG and EPG enabled and monitored by ghostmon , not sure if this region is optimised to serve traffic.

I'd suggest getting this vetted by Engineering team . If this is causing a problem , you could perhaps perform a MR suspension
{quote}

This region is being [maprule suspended|https://www.nocc.akamai.com/nert/view.cgi?mode=suspension&id=10043] as we speak due to on-going issue, especially during peak hours. 

Reviewing [alerts for this machine|https://alerts.akamai.com/cgi-bin/reporter/alertreporter?__option_summary_collate_by=percent&__option_all_attributes=no&__option_over_time_groupby=hour&__option_over_time_groupby_definition=no&__option_over_time_use_graph=yes&__option_most_frequent_groupby=Alert+Instance+Key&__option_most_frequent_use_defs=no&__option_most_frequent_threshhold=50&report_type=alert_history&__option_p1_thres=1&__option_p2_thres=20&__option_p3_p5_thres=50&__exact_Definition+ID=exact&__exact_Alert+Name=substring&__exact_Ecor+Number=exact&__exact_Region+Number=exact&__pattern_Machine+IP=23.47.125.164&__exact_Machine+IP=exact&__exact_Alert+Instance+Key=exact&__exact_Owner+Email=substring&__exact_Ticket+ID=exact&__exact_AMS+Alert+Definition+ID=exact&__dynamic_filter_=Install+Group&__exact_alert_data_value_1_=exact&__exact_alert_data_value_2_=exact&__exact_alert_data_value_3_=exact&__exact_alert_data_value_4_=exact&gmtoffset=-14400&__time_options_=__use_start_&__month_From=3&__day_From=24&__year_From=2026&__hour_From=20&__min_From=33&__month_Until=3&__day_Until=31&__year_Until=2026&__hour_Until=20&__min_Until=33&__time_relation_Age=1&__time_unit_Age=Days&output_format=HTML&useNewWindow=on&timezone=gmt&datasource=Production&Action=Create%20Report], we see some GFI process rolls, so wondering if the FRP denials are due to GFI settings in this region as identified by NOCC.

Ack: Can we review the FRP errors in this region and take necessary steps to avoid customer impact due to them?

resolution_description: Mitigation is under discussion with the CW Product team, focusing on either increasing the SG VR bucket max deny threshold to 100 or deploying a dedicated VR bucket for TikTok to prevent impact on other footprints during future spikes.
root_cause:
VR denials occurred on SG CW due to a flit load spike in TikTok cpcodes.

Since TikTok contributes more than 50% of CW traffic in SG, the VR bucket parameters were tuned to deny only TikTok traffic during such spikes. However, in this instance, the default max deny threshold (currently set at 80 per Footprint) for Tiktok footprint was reached, resulting in denials across all FPs to maintain demand within limits.
creator: Senthilkumar Rajendiran
mitigation_plan: Mitigation is under discussion with the CW Product team, focusing on either adding  the parameter for maximum keys to deny or deploying a dedicated VR bucket for TikTok to prevent impact on other footprints during future spikes.
longterm_mitigation: Anomaly detection VR feature to deny only the keys causing traffic spike anomalies

summary: Failure to move error when trying to move the cloud wrapper config
description:
Hello team,

The SAM performed the migration which included CW but he gets an error that it failed. Please see the screenshot and all prechecks were completed.

Please note that all the delivery assets were moved successfully. 

Source Account: Fox Entertainment
Source Contract ID: 3-3IFMD7
Cloud Wrapper Configuration Name: FoxDTC

Destination Account: Fox DTC
Destination Contract ID: V-4WBOUVT

 

!image-2026-04-07-23-01-40-832.png|width=1239,height=440!
executive_summary: During the migration of assets from the Fox Entertainment account to the Fox DTC account, the migration of a specific Cloud Wrapper (CW) configuration (FoxDTC) failed using the automated migration tool. The failure was caused by a system limitation that prevents the partial migration of CW configurations from a single source contract. The team successfully resolved this by manually recreating the configuration on the target account using a staged transition approach to minimize traffic impact and cache evictions.
resolution_description:
Since a tool-based migration was impossible for a single configuration, the team executed a manual transition:
Validated that the target contract (V-4WBOUVT) had sufficient purchased capacity (100 TB).
Created a new CW configuration on the Fox DTC account associated with a test property. Removed the specific ARLs from the legacy Fox Entertainment CW configuration.Immediately added those ARLs to the new Fox DTC CW configuration.
Pushed changes via UMP and confirmed traffic began flowing through the new footprint.
root_cause:
The automated Cloud Wrapper migration tool does not support "Partial Migration." If a source contract (3-3IFMD7) contains multiple CW configurations (in this case, three: FoxDTC, foxvdms, and FoxEntMedia), the tool cannot migrate just one. It requires an "all-or-nothing" migration of all CW objects under that contract. 
Manual recreation was initially blocked because the ARLs were already bound to the legacy configuration. Akamai controls prevent the same ARL from being associated with two different CW configurations simultaneously.
creator: Sharille Rodrigues
mitigation_plan:
The transition (Creation of a new CW configuration on account associated with a test property.and Removed the specific ARL & Immediately added those ARLs to the new Fox DTC CW configuration.) was recommended to be performed during off-peak hours.
During the "gap" period while UMP configurations were propagating, traffic was directed to use the default Cloud Wrapper footprint available for each map. This ensured continuity of service, though it carried a minor risk of increased origin pull due to temporary cache evictions.
longterm_mitigation: It will suggested clearer guidance for IATs and internal integration guides to explicitly highlight the "Partial Migration" limitation. And Establish a standard "Manual Move" checklist for CW configurations when full contract migrations are not feasible, ensuring QA validation is performed in a lab environment prior to production changes.

based on the product design, past experience, state the flow for MultiCDN-CW for VOD should be:

Edge(uncacheable proxy)<>CW1<>CW2<>Origin.

 

We did also notice that ERR_NO_FWD_HOSTS are there whenever the machine contacting the NS4 Origin is not TD1, but for example TD0 or ICP part of the same forward chain.

 

*Ask:*

What is the reason behind and mitigation for ERR_NO_FWD_HOSTS ?

Broken tier definition order under the product baseline?

or <forward:cache-parent.sureroute.contact-multi-protocol-next-hop-on-failure>

should we try disabling <forward:cache-parent.sureroute.contact-multi-protocol-next-hop-on-failure> in first place?

Issue Summary:

MCO was alerted to a spike in HTTP 503 for the CPCODE : 1705081 (digital.fidelity.com) at around 03:05 UTC (04/11/26). Upon analysis, it was identified that one of the parent regions i.e. r40846 more specifically on one IP: 23.55.167.30 had *_ERR_FWD_SSL_HANDSHAKE|unable_to_set_supported_groups_* errors that lead to those 503 responses downstream at the edge.

While there was no major impact, we could see that these errors were intermittently have been causing spikes for Fidelity

Checking the same for 12-hour window, we can see the same occurring intermittently

!Screenshot 2026-04-11 at 6.08.43 PM.jpg|width=510,height=204!

We reached out to the NOCC under : *#B-W-1D4CPJ7* and they reached out further to T3 after the initial assessment provided below,

 
{noformat}
1] RHM looks good | load graph | high flits noticed - it is a regular pattern[
2] Mapper DNSP - Suspended 750 Fault noticed on 5 machines on region 40846
[3] Cache logs : sample checks on 2 machines shows high flit utilization and high  Average Manager Cycle
[4] Historical traces looks good[5] Nexus : Noticed maximum CPU usage | flit % @ 109%{noformat}
NOCC T3 provided us with the following set of details regarding the *IP : 23.55.167.30* mentioned in this ticket,

 

 
Reviewing the ticket , the error "{*}_ERR_FWD_SSL_HANDSHAKE|unable_to_set_supported_groups_{*}”  isn’t caused by the usual combination of load and suspend flags etc . The error seems to be specific to an encryption/elliptical curve used by OpenSSL binary .
 
This problem is still happening at this point with multiple hostnames /properties, and the same error shows up [1] , with Ghost logging errors about missing a group /curve “{*}_X25519_{*}" . At the time of writing, the error has occurred over 107345 times , repeating the same openssl-error code “{*}_168296710_{*}” . The error seems to be exclusive to G2G (Ghost-to-Ghost) requests /connections [3] and earliest occurrence of the error was on April 10th, ~15:53 UTC  [4] . 
 
This seems to be problem with Ghost or/and Ghost-OpenSSL as I was able to successfully finish the SSL handshake manually [5] . A possible root cause can be likely that the Ghost version ({*}_22.4.4.4)_{*} and Ghost-OpenSSL   ({*}_8.3.1.8.3)_{*} version are older than the rest of the peers in the region as seen in  [6] . You can confirm with engineering , if this behavior is a result of version mismatch on the machine vs the rest of its peers in region.
Note : This behavior seems to be local to this machine and have been suspended the machine as of now [7] at 06:45 UTC

executive_summary:
Incorrect unzipped Content served to end-user with no Content-type header

21st April
The customer observed this string abcd1234efgh5678 whenever they see the corrupted content, while analyzing the logs, we understood that it is not a random strong, it was a ghost internal upload buffer. 

29th April 
upon further investigation, we found that the working requests has only one IP while the non working has multiple Akamai IPs along with localhost IP, it indicates that the request had looped through Akamai once.

30th April,

We further enabled the CLIENT debug ID 24665 to analyse the client headers, we observed that the test object header was present in the cache logs, and tried reproducing the issue with this header and we could see it matches with what customer mentioned as the incorrect content and the client IP 183.110.97.251 is a part of netmarble and this problematic request arrived at Akamai from this client. So it seems like the customer has looped sure route requests back to Akamai.
root_cause: we observed that the test object header was present in the client requests and while reproducing the issue with that header, we could see it matches with what customer mentioned as the incorrect content
creator: Suman Mishra
mitigation_plan: Test object header was present in the client requests, suggested to check with client and adjust this header
longterm_mitigation: Test object header was present in the client requests, suggested to check with client and adjust this header

summary: [F-CS-11054139]-ESI parse tree cache-hit is resulting in unexpected/wrong content when using Edge Side Includes(ESI).
description:
Issue -  ESI parse tree cache-hit is resulting in unexpected content caching when using Edge Side Includes(ESI).   Environment - PM config - opendata_pm Test URL: [https://election-municipale.linternaute.com/test-04032026-fred?cookie&esi=actu] The Cache behavior is set to "no-store" by default in the configurations; Customer transmit caching directives from the origin via the Edge-Control header. They have two main use cases: Anonymous access, for which they send: Edge-Control: dca=esi, !no-store, max-age=XXX, donwstream-ttl=0 Authenticated access (presence of a LINTERSESSID cookie) for which they send: Edge-Control: dca=esi, !no-store, bypass-cache (in order to avoid deleting any cache that may exist for anonymous users) Bypass cache in criteria cookie LINTERSESSID exists (the rule "Advanced Metadata" > "Non Static objects" > "Cookies" that includes this behavior triggers also when other cookies exist)Without this behavior, the responses stored in object cache for anonymous access may be read from the object cache for authenticated access. So the requests coming in with cookie should be treated to bypass the cache.  Problem scenario - When they have many authenticated accesses to a URL (presence of cookie), the cache becomes poisoned with the content served for these requests (the headers served to the client are indeed those of an anonymous version of the page, but the content corresponds to the content served to the authenticated request). This occurs as soon as they activate the ESI preprocessor via the Edge-Control header: dca=esi (whether or not there are ESI elements in the page).   Investigation - To differentiate the content in responses - They have a request ID set by origin in the headers. (Example: x-ccm-req-id: 1772803284.69aad4d489d427.46939635) This same ID is written in the body of the page: (Ex:

Reqid: 1772803284.69aad4d489d427.46939635

) They also have an authentication indicator in the page code: for anonymous access:

Auth: pas authentifie

for authenticated access:

Auth: Authentifie jODInsituEdit

  Tests- A good example - In this request we are not sending a cookie, so the request will be from cache and we see the req id "x-ccm-req-id: 1773238074.69b1773a8881c8.82439875" is same in header and the body.  [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/ER-263297] line 10 A bad example for comparison. Shows that the value in header x-ccm-req-id: 1773238074.69b1773a8881c8.82439875 and the body are different. Also the body should not contain "Auth: Authentifie jODInsituEdit", as this is only seen when the request comes in with a cookie and bypass-cache is applied in that case. However, in this instance, it gets returned as part of the response.  [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/ER-263297] line 50 Checking the log line for this request, we can see that object status logs "r - An esi parse tree cache was hit." Additional logs and http captures are in - [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/ER-263297] There were some old CRs that talk about a similar issue with esi-parse-tree/responses not honoring bypass-cache resulting in a cache hit and affecting responses/cache poisoning. [https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1S39j4fDKXRqWzNr6OwQ97JesttuWz2jO] These tags were discussed as part of a solution in those CRs - edgecomputing:esi.limits.tree-pin and edgecomputing:esi.tree-caching.disable-cache Could you please confirm if these tags can be used as a workaround in this scenario? Why does esi-parse-tree cache hit happen intermittently, resulting in an incorrect object being returned in response?

summary: 503 spikes for bolt-cp1.phonepe.com - Websocket review
description:
Requesting you to help with any recommendations that can be done for this configuration: bolt-cp1.phonepe.com. 

This is also app-based end-user traffic but on websockets, the overall concurrency connection is 500k for websockets. 

The customer's traffic is at 20% on Akamai. Account level grafana  details for websocket(search by account name).

Here is a summary of the technical issue and its resolution based on the investigation:

What went wrong?
The domain bolt-cp1.phonepe.com experienced significant 503 error spikes between April 1st and April 2nd, 2026. While the errors were visible on the traffic dashboards, they did not appear on the origin server graphs, indicating the issue was occurring at the network edge.


Why did it happen?
The root cause was a WebSocket connection bottleneck at the edge server level:
Socket Limits: The number of active WebSocket connections exceeded the 32K threshold per edge server, triggering an LRU (Least Recently Used) connection pruning.
Traffic Hotspots: Because SureRoute (performance-based routing) was enabled, the system was funneling the majority of traffic through a few high-performing regions (specifically TATA-BOM32p and TATA-BOM32o).


Result: These specific regions became "hotspots" that hit their connection limits, resulting in ERR_CONNECT_FAIL and "Cannot assign requested address" errors.
What fixed it?


A metadata (MTD) change was implemented on April 6th to change how traffic is distributed, this metadata is the same fix that we applied for SR+OIPACL issue:
Disabled SureRoute: This stopped the system from concentrating traffic in a few "fastest" regions.


Enforced CH42 RA Map: This shifted traffic to a more direct, distributed mapping.
Outcome: Traffic is now more evenly spread across a larger number of servers. This prevents any single server from reaching the 32K socket limit, which has eliminated the 503 errors for now.
root_cause: WebSocket connections exceeded 32K per-server threshold due to SureRoute concentrating traffic into a few high-performing regions (TATA-BOM32p/BOM32o), causing ERR_CONNECT_FAIL and 503 errors.
creator: Thilaga Raju
mitigation_plan: MTD change to disable SureRoute and enforce CH42 RA map for better traffic distribution. Prespread to 32 requested to reduce hotspot risk.
longterm_mitigation: Inputs to be shared with the Product team to confirm if the client’s use-case can be supported by the platform and whether any feature/design enhancements are required.

description:
*Issus summary:*

Between April 10 and April 12, 2026, multiple performance issues and 5xx error spikes were observed for CPcode 1881644. While failover mechanisms were triggered in most cases, they were either unsuccessful due to regional resource exhaustion (flits) or rendered ineffective by Origin-side errors.

-------------------------------------------

*1. Incident on April 10, 2026:* Midgress Performance Degradation
Timeframe: 04:20 PM – 04:22 PM GMT (09:50 PM – 09:52 PM IST)

The primary issue was concentrated at the Midgress (Parent) layer, specifically within regions serving the Indian market. While Edge-to-Client 200 OK responses remained high (~99.4%), the internal forward request success rate dropped due to parent server saturation.

Error Types: Significant spike in 503 (Service Unavailable) and 0xx (Connection Errors/Timeouts).

Root Cause: Several parent machines (Regions r36987 and r40321) reached critical CPU utilization levels (>95%).

Specific Impacted Nodes:

23.212.99.108 (r36987 - TATA-DEL): CPU hit 98%.
23.55.245.71 (r40321 - GPX-BOM2): CPU hit 97%.

Result: The high load led to ERR_LIFETIME_EXP|clientTimeout and ERR_SSL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT, as parent servers could not complete handshakes or process requests in time.

{*}2. Incident on April 11, 2026{*}: Origin-Level Errors
Timeframe: 02:34 PM – 02:36 PM GMT (08:04 PM – 08:06 PM IST)

Unlike the previous day, the errors on April 11th were largely traced back to the Origin infrastructure.

Error Distribution: Post-failover (FA) statistics showed that 31.4% of requests resulted in 503 errors.

Origin Performance: Log analysis confirmed that the Akamai TD1/Cloud Wrapper layers were receiving 503 responses directly from the Origin IP (34.8.232.57).

{*}3. Incident on April 12, 2026{*}: Region Suspension and Traffic Spikes
Timeframe: 02:03 PM – 02:05 PM GMT (07:33 PM – 07:35 PM IST)

Primary Failure: A single machine, 23.213.0.128 (Region r37451), was suspended, causing immediate ERR_SSL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT for a large block of traffic.

Failover Impact: Traffic successfully failed over to secondary regions(ch970), but this caused a sudden traffic spike in Region r40321 (GPX-BOM2e).

Load Spike Details:

Servers 23.55.245.22 and 23.55.245.76 saw CPU usage jump to 98-100%.

flits levels exceeded 110%, leading to high latency and ERR_LIFETIME_EXP (Client Timeouts) during the handshake phase.

-------------------------------------------

>>> Specifically IAT would like to know how to mitigate and prevent for the issue happened on Apr. 12th(3)

Observations :
Error seen on primary leg due to 2 reasons where FA recovery was not great:
a) Small amount of timeouts between CW and TD0 but MPE has amplified the error rate - 14 timeouts on CW led to 4K+ errors at edge \{primary contributor}
b) Timeout on single machine at TD0 tier

For (a) - failover triggers to TD1 alternate ch970 - request is concentrated hitting 2 machines and ends up with connect timeout.
For (b) Failaction to alt TD0 - chapacb kicks in and response is successful
{quote}Ask: Post failaction, the number of successful requests are very less. Hence, please help us on the recommendations with the load spreading and CH-970 map.
{quote}

summary: [ghostdir.hd.data/amos_best_practices_v1.xml] Cascading timeouts, read higher than fbt
description:
*Background:*

The customer reported some incomplete delivery for FULL GET with POC enabled over MultiCDN-CW config.

 

*Investigation:*

There are some first byte timeouts taking place due to latency between OOC (out of country) CW0 and CW1 hops.

When such FBT triggers for POC Byte-Range related requests created by ghost there is an built-in retry, reforward.

However there is also is read timeout before response body triggering downstream due to http.read threshold being lower than fbt, such results in incomplete delivery and lack of successful midgress retry capability delivered downstream to the Client req.

    110     <!-- timeouts applicable on edge -->
    111     <forward:cache-parent.non-tail-connect-timeout>2s</forward:cache-parent.non-tail-connect-timeout>
    112     <network:http.first-byte-timeout>6s</network:http.first-byte-timeout>
    113     <network:http.read>2s</network:http.read>

    123         <network:http.first-byte-timeout>1s</network:http.first-byte-timeout>
    124         <network:http.read>2s</network:http.read>
    125       </match:tier>
    126     </akamai:choose>{code}
 

*Ask:*

While the value of <network:http.read> can be controlled in CW Multi-Config through UI:

after enabling: `Advanced Override (internal only)`

!image-2026-04-16-16-34-31-715.png|width=412,height=192!

and PS just increased the customer config value to 7s to mitigate the integration problem.

 

is it expected and is there any particular reason that the current default values of cascading timeouts for:
{code:java}
network:http.first-byte-timeout{code}
are higher than
{code:java}
network:http.read{code}
?

 

Typically best practice is to have network:http.read higher than network:http.first-byte-timeout and network:http.first-byte-timeout the lowest available.

Is it intentional to allow signaling third party CDN down-stream that we could have delivered incomplete for range request?

Or maybe is it pure gap that requires adjustment?
executive_summary:
Ticket was raised to understand setting the read timeout lower than first-byte timeout, 
Consulted the team that originally established these cascading timeout values. 
As per the following breakdown details, it is perfectly acceptable for the FB timeout to be set higher than the Read timeout. The configuration is intentional and does not represent an error. 
For more details, please refer to the attached email FW- Cascaded Timeouts for CW-MCDN.eml

root_cause: MCH region 46563 experienced persistent flit overload primarily driven by elevated flit consumption from Verizon's WAF policy change (pisces.cdn.fios.tv added April 9th), causing frequent region suspensions. The WrestleMania live event traffic surge (4× on April 18–19) exposed this contention, resulting in ERR_SSL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT and ERR_READ_TIMEOUT errors for Disney Streaming live channels.
creator: Rahul Haridwari
mitigation_plan: FOM was reduced on region 38977 and MCH/zch3 maprules were suspended on region 46563 to redistribute load. NOCC investigation ticket B-V-6HMM2ZR was raised for region 46563. summary: Optimize maprule load on r50258
description:
Hello GPO

As per  NOCC#B-W-1DPTN1T spiky flit traffic was observed - "walmart seems to be culprit for 9680 MR traffc".  Is there a scope to optimize the load on this region without having to lower FOM in the long-term?

The region was maprule suspended under NOCC#B-W-1DQ5245 as a quick mitigation  but we want to smoothen the traffic load on this region before unsuspending the maprule again.

Original problem statement:

~~~

Property: mobile.ak.omni.bankmandiri.co.id_optimized

Customer reported that they observed elevated latency (~5s) in their traffic. Based on log analysis, the latency is attributed to ERR_SSL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT (SSLTimeout) occurring at midgress, predominantly within region 50258. Refer etherpad line (https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11227293 line 235-275)

Further validation via load graphs indicates that this region is consistently operating at or near capacity, with intermittent flit drops:

[https://lg.netarch.akamai.com/cgi-bin/loadgraphs?period=2d&region=50258&network=A&maprule=&display=total&ymax=&utcoffset=8]

Although the issue is intermittent, it is impacting our customer, PT Bank Mandiri, who closely monitors traffic performance 24x7 and is highly sensitive to any degradation. Similar impact from this region has been observed in previous cases (F-CS-11212894 / B-V-6H9CCRX).

As a mitigation, we have temporarily suspended the customer’s map rules from this region. This issue has also been escalated to NOCC under B-W-1DPTN1T, where initial findings suggest that traffic spikes from map rules (e.g., MR 9680, MR 1626) are contributing to the overload condition.

~~~
executive_summary: Optimize spiky traffic on r50258
root_cause: Region overload due to attack on Walmart (CP1450274)

#3 During ghost-reforward in this case out of ERR_POC_FWD_NOT_206 ghost utilizes the modified path.

#4 When going forward to NS again it modified the path again adding Netstorage CP: 275596.

 

*Ask:*

As per the title: MultiCDN-CloudWrapper generated delivery property is appending CP Code twice on forward path modifications during re-forwards, resulting failure on delivery (404) as the forward path is incorrect compared to what was originally requested.

Beside the product is counting on re-forwards for POC + NS4 instead of chasing the redirects.

 

Can we fix the template to avoid appending the CP Code twice on path modification?
executive_summary:
There is a metadata template for forward path modification, when a request is re-forwarded (e.g., after an error or redirect), the path already contains the CP Code from the previous modification. The template runs again and prepends the CP Code a second time, resulting in /275596/275596/...
We may need to add a match condition to check for the CP Code before modifying the path.
CW team is working on this.

summary: Investigation of increased midgress traffic since April 2026
description:
*Issue Summary:*

Since April 2026, there has been a significant increase in midgress traffic (bytes) for CP 479242 (apps.samsungcloudcdn.com), despite no changes to the configuration and stable ingress request volume. Initial analysis suggests that .img files are not being cached correctly, leading to an influx of 200 OK responses from Parent to Child edges instead of expected 206 (Partial Content) or 304 (Not Modified) responses.

*Findings:*

summary: Increased SSL connection time during 21st April Match
description:
*Background:*

Increased SSL connection time during Match [T20 World Cup and IPL] days.

Context shared by customer:
for the host apix.hotstar.com , we are seeing increased ssl connection time for past couple of months, we compared our data from dec 2025 till april 2026, there was an increased SSL connection time during this time period , particularly during match days, t20 worldcup , IPL matches etc,
there has been 50% increase in connection acquired time which is the time taken for dnsstart->dnsEnd->connectionStart->secureConnectionStart->secureConnectionEnd->connectionEnd->connectionacquired.
the time was increasing till march 8 which was end of t20 world cup , went back to normal from march 9 till IPL start and again increased.

 

*CSE Findings:*

1) We are seeing high SSL overhead time logged in multiple Edge regions. 

2) Checking Edge region health for top 6 regions, I do not see any high load/suspensions/RHM losses in the region.

3) From sample traces, i could see high SSL time in r line. However, there was no slhds field seen in ddc log nor cache log for the client IPs considered. Further, cache logs and ghostmon logs showed average load on the server and no server suspension seen.

 

*Further Investigation:*

Both ssl overhead time increases seems to follow req endtime.

Do also follow the traffic pattern, indicating itis load induced (comparing with 10th of April trafficPeak with APIx dashboard confirms the same)

 

What is concerning though is ongoing ESSL release having problems and keysigning slowness surge specific to 21 April not seen earlier.

Therefore raising the ERE ahead of time as data is indicating an either capacity or release problem / both altogether.

 

[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11239961]

resolution_description:
Added the PP CIDRs currently in unpingable list. 
For now, included the manual PP IP which belong to a router of JP Ecor to let the PPs always available to map to JP regions.
Long term solution is getting IBM IPs to not filter Akamai ASN for ICMP pings.
root_cause: Pingpoint IPs part of IBM network filters out ICMP pings from Akamai servers, so JP regions seen consistent heavy loss leading to OOC regions to get placed in front of the scorelist.
creator: Yasuhiro Oyabu
mitigation_plan:
Added the PP CIDRs currently in unpingable list. 
For now, included the manual PP IP which belong to a router of JP Ecor to let the PPs always available to map to JP regions.
longterm_mitigation: Netservices to work with IBM to not filter Akamai ASN for ICMP pings.

summary: Packet analysis review request between brave and edge server
description:
*Issue summary:* 

Netmarble has experienced recurring intermittent timeout errors across several API domains using EIPB. While initial escalations confirmed that platform-side issues—specifically regional flit overload and self-suspension in KR regions—caused TCP and TLS handshake delays, a residual stream of errors persists that cannot be fully explained by platform congestion alone. Please refer to previous jiras which engaged performance team.

ERE-3201
ERE-3226

A major concern has emerged regarding whether EIPB is the technically appropriate product for Netmarble’s specific traffic profile, which is characterized by aggressive application-side timeouts (2-3 seconds), HTTP/2 multiplexing, and heavy traffic concentration from kubernetes pods.

More over, current diagnostics indicate that a deeper investigation into the transport layer is required. Specific latency anomalies observed within the EIPB pcap data necessitate an investigation by the EIPB engineering team. This investigation is essential to determine if the delays are inherent to the EIPB mapping mechanism under this specific traffic shape or if an alternative solution (such as a different sharding or API accelerate product) would better serve the customer’s sensitivity to transport-level latency.

Checking qgrep logs it shows there is only one client IP and they were hammering one edge server mostly at that time.

summary: {F-CS-11223522} Riot Games: 400 from Origin + MPE causing cache poisoning
description:
Test URL: [https://lolstatic-a.akamaihd.net/rso-authenticator-ui/0.123.4/rso-authenticator-ui.js]

Product: DD

 

=> US West
URL: [https://lolstatic-a.akamaihd.net/rso-authenticator-ui/0.123.4/rso-authenticator-ui.js]
Config: [https://control.akamai.com/apps/property-manager/#/property-version/10329754/54/edit?gid=64631]

Issue:

Customer was informed of a bug in their bug-bounty program of a possible DoS attach
The way it works is that customer uses a program called Turbo Intruder which can simulate requests at many requests/sec, but the request header size is >24K.  Causing a 400 from Origin.

This program is hitting the Edges, simultaneously, they will simulate a real-user (normal size request headers) hitting the same machine and that person will get a 400 as well instead of a legit 200

From logs we can see samples where the real-user gets the 400 from parent-cache. Please check the logs in the etherpad

The configuration have advanced metadata to disable 400 caching. We can see the object status "k" in the requests but it still has S in it which means it is detecting the object as cacheable. 

<!--Disable caching for 4xx and 5xx-->
<match:response.status value="400:599">
<cache:bypass>on</cache:bypass>
</match:response.status>



Etherpad showing MPE working for path "assets/riot_desktop_background_2x.f1100272.jpg" (used to replicate): [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11223522#L1257]

 

Attached is a HAR capture with both the 200 showing the no-store and private heading and the 400 that's being cached by MPE.

 

This looks like cache poisoning vulnerability that impacts any property configs not explicitely disabling MPE as we would cache the 4XX/5XX that's caused by an end-user sending invalid requests and if this is done continously,  a DOS will be caused.

 

Based on the logs and config; could be related to the static files rule taking priority, for example:
 * *Match:* {{.jpg}} -> {{{}cache:max-age = 365d{}}}.

 * The file  was not in cache.

 *  S3 responds with a 400.

 * Because the object matches the 365-day rule and the config has 'negative-ttl  off'  the Edge assumes the origin response is valid content that should be stored for one year.

 
{code:java}
 <comment:note value="Start Feature cacheError"/>
            <cache:negative-ttl2>
                <status>off</status>
            </cache:negative-ttl2>
            <cache:preserve-stale-objects>on</cache:preserve-stale-objects>
            <cache:fwd-ims-flag-fix>off</cache:fwd-ims-flag-fix>
            <comment:note value="End Feature cacheError"/> {code}
Full investigation is here

https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11223522
executive_summary: 400 from Origin + MPE causing cache poisoning
creator: Cesar Roque Quiros

summary: PS having issues using spread EIPB serial - Verizon
description:
Summary :

ERE-3305 was raised for Disney Streaming where the customer reported VPF and CIRR leading to performance impact during their live event. MCO reached out to ERE to seek recommendations regarding the possible mitigations and it was identified that the regions underwent spiky flits due to a particular hostname i.e *_pisces.cdn.fios.tv_*

The spiky nature from the above hostname lead to the oscillations in load assignment due to high flit demand and hence, ERE suggested to reach out to the Verizon IAT to make few changes that could help in mitigation of the underlying issues due to the hostname : *_pisces.cdn.fios.tv_*

 

Below were the recommendations provided from ERE

_{{From a platform perspective two things could be tried}}_
 # {{Try the full prespread serial - 2047 for the edge serial - have PS help migrate the edge serial from 1955 to 2047 serial could help  ( [https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/ERE-2802?focusedId=11061563&page=com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.issuetabpanels%3Acomment-tabpanel#comment-11061563] we have done so in the past on EIPB it seems, likely worth the try here too)}}{{ }}

 # {{One other thing that could be entertained from a platform perspective, I have noticed that these requests seem to be synchronized every minute causing spikes in load and throwing off how our platform reacts (dnsp inflate and deflate) , would highly encourage a desync of these requests with customer to lessen the hot spotting, especially since the f2h is much higher.  }}

{{!Screenshot 2026-05-05 at 1.38.07 AM.jpg|width=660,height=213!}}

 

PS tried to implement / change the serial number from EIPB interface and were unable to do so as they lacked the proper access to implement those changes. Hence, MCO tried to open a MPDEVOPS ticket as per the documentation : [https://collaborate.akamai.com/confluence/spaces/MPEFPS/pages/78654204/EdgeIP+Binding+Change+Management+Workflow] 

 

Ask : Since the Media Portal Devops ticket is obsolete, reaching out to _*ERE-Delivery-Portal*_ team to check and assist PS in their queries / implementation of the serial changes and any other information need by them.

 

More details can be found under ERE-3305 (https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/ERE-330 )
executive_summary: Verizon experienced performance degradation for Disney Streaming due to traffic spikes on the hostname pisces.cdn.fios.tv. To resolve this, the EIPB Edge serial was migrated from 1955 to 2047, which stabilized load assignment and optimized traffic distribution.
resolution_description: The ERE-Delivery-Portal team manually updated the backend configuration for CP code 1817883 to utilize the full pre-spread serial 2047. This change ensures traffic is redistributed effectively across the GHOST network to prevent regional hot-spotting.
root_cause: Technically, synchronized minute-by-minute traffic spikes triggered aggressive platform load oscillations, specifically dnsp inflate and deflate cycles. Procedurally, Professional Services lacked the EIP_BINDING_ADVANCE permissions required to implement the fix, and the legacy request workflow was obsolete.
creator: Pratik Salunke
mitigation_plan: The team successfully implemented the serial 2047 update and advised the customer to desynchronize their request intervals to reduce sudden flit demand spikes.
longterm_mitigation: Future efforts will focus on evaluating "Serial Update" access for Professional Services to reduce manual intervention and updating internal documentation to replace obsolete Media Portal DevOps workflows with current processes.

summary: {F-CS-11311709} Cont. ERE-3147 - Interim solutions are still required
description:
+*Environment:*+

Product: Dynamic Site Accelerator

Property Hostname:  gw.aeonpayment.com

Edge Hostname:  gw.aeonpayment.com.edgekey.net

Slot: 26017, Enhanced TLS (SNI)

Maprule ID: 1327

CPcode: 826437

Client IP: 52.197.137.56, 52.197.158.90, 52.198.9.30, 52.198.79.125 (All are located in AS16509 of Amazon Data Services)
h2. +*Issue:*+

The customer’s payment transaction in POST from the clients above which is an API server aggregating the end users application request intermittently fails in C2G connection level. 

*The timeframe is:*

2026-05-02 6:33:37-6:34:54 UTC

2026-05-02 6:48:22-6:49:03 UTC

2026-05-03 6:46:03-6:47:09 UTC

After the discussion in ERE-3147 last January, the effort to implement solutions has been paid in IAT side, but it’s not easy to force the change of map to Japan Racing Association due to business/customer engagement reasons. Instead of that, IAT has proposed Cache/Downstream cache tuning to alleviate the spike of JRA’s traffic itself. The task is actually ongoing but it will take more months to complete. 

Log analysis and mapper tool links are in [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11311709]. The root cause is same with ERE-3147. The pre-spread in MAPPINGENG-8122 is still effective, but FOM change in B-V-6A6ZYT1 has been reverted in the last February.    

The affected regions which the clients were assigned this time were r52909, r48512 and r36439.
h2. +*Ask:*+

AEON Financial Service Co.,Ltd is a critical service provider for shop payment transactions, and very sensitive to this type of error. IAT is looking for any mitigations by the time that  the cache tuning project completes (ETA: July 2026). 

Can you please consider FOM reduction as the temporary alleviation by the end of June 2026?
root_cause: Platform flit overload in Japan regions (r52909, r48512, r36439) caused by JRA horse racing event traffic spikes. The flit load spike triggers Ghost self-suspension, which directly causes C2G connection failures for AEON Financial Service payment API traffic on maprule 1327 (DSA, gw.aeonpayment.com). The FOM change (B-V-6A6ZYT1) that had been pre-spreading AEON traffic away from these regions was reverted in February 2026. This is a continuation of ERE-3147.
creator: Yasuhiro Oyabu
mitigation_plan: FOM reapplied under B-W-1G7SZ1D  until the JRA /Netdreamers account/customer makes the needed caching changes at their end.
longterm_mitigation: Better mechanism to track api like traffic on other product/ maps impacting regions/platform.

summary: ERR_NON_SUPERNET_IP from FF parent to Origin using OIPACL
description:
Hello

The customer reported error on traffic: [api.zomato.com|https://api.zomato.com/]

Based on our analysis user seeing error since our system routed traffic to out side of ACL Region (ERR_NON_SUPERNET_IP )

Mostly from region 39641 ( we see some requests on other regions as well )

[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11321906] Line#323

Impact was significant with 14% of hits DoS'ed after 3x fwd retries.

ERR_NON_SUPERNET_IP                        459407   14.608% (line#237)

At this moment as workaround we suspended the region
[https://issues.deploy.akamai.com/cgi-bin/view.cgi?issue_id=B-W-1G4D46R]

Request flow was from FF edge 23.193.114.5 to FF parents 104.91.59.x which then decided to try direct origin to log ERR_NON_SUPERNET_IP. As per 2025 update 104.64.0.0/10 was removed from OIPACL:  [https://techdocs.akamai.com/origin-ip-acl/docs/update-your-origin-server] which also covers the 104.91.59.x IPs.

The /a/etc/ghost/maprules.data/allowlist.xml on a sample 104.91.59.x IP does not match on r39641 for any assign:maprule-member either. Yet these IPs tried to go direct Origin (no D - DR direct policy no SR races seen). 

OIPACL metadata is in advanced override and sample logs attached to this case for reference. 

i suspect that this map needs to be updated:
{code:java}
<match:region.attribute value="network-freeflow">
    <reporting:maprule>a2047.dscapi5.akamai.net</reporting:maprule>
    <assign:variable>
        <name>T0</name>
        <value>a2047.ch7.akamai.net</value>
    </assign:variable> {code}
Can you confirm?

(api.zomato.com v411)

[https://control.akamai.com/apps/property-manager/#/property-version/10325093/411/edit?gid=104815&view=review]

Can you help us understand why machines in r39461 as an example tried direct origin instead of a valid OIPACL region?
executive_summary: FF parent tried direct origin instead of OIPACL region and logged ERR_NON_SUPERNET_IP  with significant impact (14%)
root_cause: Due to issue with llmap update on edge region Swans went to trusted fallback using g-map (maprule 1) and returned region 39641 which is not on the OIPACL. This resulted in ERR_NON_SUPERNET_IP and 14% partial DoS for api.zomato.com. The swans dynamic config trusted_maprules for service W points to maprule 1 (g-map) instead of an OIPACL-compliant fallback map.
creator: Rahul Sawarkar
mitigation_plan: Region 39641 suspended (B-W-1G4D46R). PHENS-13460 opened to update swans dynamic config trusted to use a fallback map compliant with OIPACL for service W instead of g-map (maprule 1).
longterm_mitigation: SWaNS fallback need to be compliant for OIPACL allowlist

summary: Increased TCP Connections to Origin Servers
description:
Issue summary: Starting at approximately 2026-05-09 14:00 UTC, Zomato has observed a sharp change in Akamai's edge-to-origin TCP/TLS connection behavior on our property [api.zomato.com|https://akamai.my.salesforce.com/servlet/servlet.ExternalRedirect?url=https%3A%2F%2Fapi.zomato.com]. The origin AWS ALB scaled from 13 nodes to 100 nodes (hitting the AWS internal max) to absorb the additional handshake load.
{code:java}
Comparison

>> Before issue
Total origin reqs = 4,465,040
req == 0 count = 29,210
Rate:
(29210/4465040)×100≈0.654%

>> During issue
Total origin reqs = 6,372,597
req == 0 count = 56,148
Rate:
(56148/6372597)×100≈0.881%
Percentage increase in req == 0 rate
((0.881−0.654)/0.654)×100≈34.7% 
Percentage increase in number of reqs
((6372597−4465040)/4465040)×100≈42.7%  {code}
So far what we know is there were new parent servers(traffic change) hitting customer's Origin -> Customer's ALB scaler noticed increased tcp connections and added more origin nodes -> Akamai parent servers got mapped to those new nodes -> it increased more tcp connections.

!parent.png|width=582,height=93!

[http://grafana.opal.akamai.com/goto/nYvZzYADR?orgId=1]

{code:java}
<comment:note value="1. Force parent edge to go to the origin ip determined by child 2. Make this resolution as round robin."/>

<comment:note value="End Feature advanced"/> {code}
Customer has below questions and would like to know how to mitigate the issue. 

1. Did the parent-IP set for api.zomato.com (cpcodes 1575923, 1411589, 1436182, 1055672, 1403227) change around 5/9 14:00 UTC? We see visible parent IPs in 23.210.74.0/24 dropped from 36 to 22 across this window and have stayed in that range since. - our findings on this from logs on line 1169 - we see the drop in IPs 23.210.74.0/24 from 26 to 17.  What is causing the change in parent Ip set from within a CIDR and the change in parent CIDRs?

2. During the change, were existing TCP/TLS sessions to our origin severed at the parent edge (e.g., parent shutdown, process restart, or configuration reload that flushed pools)? That would explain the transient new-conn rate burst that first tripped our ALB autoscaler.

3. Mitigation - looking for your guidance. Based on our analysis, the cleanest unwinding path appears to be temporarily disabling <round-robin.status>on while keeping force-origin-ip-from-edge=on, which would concentrate traffic onto ~23 ALB nodes (since each parent would pin to 1 DNS-resolved IP per TTL). Our pre-incident baseline served this same traffic on 13 ALB nodes, so 23 should comfortably absorb the load and let the ALB scale back down over the next few hours. Would that work safely from your side, or do you see a less invasive Akamai-side lever we should consider instead?

 

Please review this and let us know if there is any workaround to mitigate the issue. It looks like the only change was those new parent servers when the issuse started to happen and nothing changed from Akamai config and customer's AWS ALB.

[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11331153] has more information on the issue.
resolution_description: Customer resolved the surge by changing their default origin to a fixed pool of 15 IPs. No Akamai-side config change was required or applied.
root_cause: Zomato's AWS ALB began handing out a large number of origin IPs (scaling from 13 to 100+ nodes). Akamai parent servers connected to each IP as it was handed out, resulting in a sharp increase in TCP connections to origin.
creator: Dimitris Kim
mitigation_plan: Pin the origin to a fixed pool of IPs rather than allowing the ALB to dynamically hand out new nodes. This prevents Akamai from connecting to auto-scaled IPs, breaking the connection surge.
longterm_mitigation: Avoid configurations where the ALB auto-scales unboundedly in response to connection load — this creates a feedback loop when the upstream (Akamai) connects to every new IP handed out. Work with AWS to set appropriate auto-scaling bounds and ensure the origin IP pool remains predictable.

summary: Edge went fwd to incorrect parent regions  and got ERR_NON_SUPERNET_IP
description:
Hello

The customer reported error on traffic: api.zomato.com

Based on our analysis user seeing error since our system routed traffic to out side of ACL Region (ERR_NON_SUPERNET_IP ).

Both r48005 and r39641 are in edge map a2047.dscapi5.akamai.net yet Ghost(s) in child r48005 went forward to r39641 instead of any ch7/ch8 region like 39640.

Most errors were  from parent  region 39641 ( we see some requests on other regions as well )

https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11321906 Line#323

Impact was significant with 14% of hits DoS'ed after 3x fwd retries.

ERR_NON_SUPERNET_IP                        459407   14.608% (line#237)

At this moment as workaround we suspended the region
https://issues.deploy.akamai.com/cgi-bin/view.cgi?issue_id=B-W-1G4D46R

Sample request flow is from FF edge 23.193.114.5 to FF parents 104.91.59.x which then decided to try direct origin to log ERR_NON_SUPERNET_IP. As per 2025 update 104.64.0.0/10 was removed from OIPACL:  https://techdocs.akamai.com/origin-ip-acl/docs/update-your-origin-server which also covers the 104.91.59.x IPs.

The /a/etc/ghost/maprules.data/allowlist.xml on  sample IPs in edge r48005 ex: 23.193.114.5 and also the bad parent r39641 ex: 104.91.59.x IP does not match on r39641 for any assign:maprule-member either. Only r39640 exist for [ch7|ch8].akamai.net. 

We need help to understand why the child routed to a wrong parent region when allowlist looks good.
executive_summary:
Regions in edge map a2047.dscapi5.akamai.net like r48005 went forward to r39461 (instead of a valid OIPACL region like 39460 in a2047.ch7.akamai.net) which then tried direct origin as there is no other Tier configured -  and hence returned ERR_NON_SUPERNET_IP  with significant impact (14%)

OIPACL metadata is in advanced override and sample logs attached to this case for reference.
root_cause: Duplicate of 3337
creator: Rahul Sawarkar

The problem is that TrafficPeak, since it's not getting correctly the BC info, is presenting wrong or incomplete data, which is a big issue for this customer.

Based on [https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/ERE-3208] we understand that the flag ``add-reply-header`` needs to be turned on explicitly in the PM Configuration, but the problem is that this customer uses Breadcrumbs in many of their PM Configs, and other customers are complaining about the same issue. 

So we wanted to ask you fi you can:

#1 take a look at this request to determine if the issue is the same as reported previously

#2 check if there is a way this fix can be added to a gHost version instead of needing to apply a flag manually in every config with issues.

c.c [~efonaas] [~jurui]
executive_summary: The issue is Breadcrumbs not logging "c=o" in forward requests to origin. As per the given log samples, the parent writes no BC into its reply header, so the edge assembles a trail with only (c=g, c=c) and c=o is not seen. As per the GREL ticket GREL-4745 The fix is already in Ghost 22.4.0  but engineering could not reproduce the exact production scenario, so the flag was made opt-in to validate the fix customer-by-customer before enabling globally. Once several customer configs are remediated successfully, a decision can be made to enable the flag by default.
root_cause: The edge assembles a trail with only (c=g, c=c) and c=o is not seen. As per the GREL ticket GREL-4745, The fix is already in Ghost 22.4.0  but engineering could not reproduce the exact production scenario, so the flag was made opt-in to validate the fix customer-by-customer before enabling globally.
creator: William Ugalde
mitigation_plan: Setting this tag reporting:breadcrumb.add-reply-header to ON, enables the feature of GREL-4745 on per customer basis, of utilizing breadcrumbs recorded from forward reply.
longterm_mitigation: Setting this tag reporting:breadcrumb.add-reply-header to ON

Now my question is, what can we do to improve reliability & performance here?. Specially since they mentioned they plan on ramping up traffic & don't want to see perf issues when they do.
 - Pconns are being used
 - Their SS map is set to handle 1001 Mbps it doesn't seem like much of a bottleneck Since they funneled everything through the same Edge region we were limited to the selected SR parents at the time. 

Maybe increase SR max-parents to 3 to have more options from the edge?.

Not sure if considering prespreading should also help prevent issues on the edge regions further down the line (their traffic is mostly non-cacheable going by ACC dashboard)

Thanks.

root_cause: Ashburn last hop  SR regions are already flit bound and has flit spikes from multiple cpcodes which impacts JPMC SR (via SS map) delivery.
creator: Javier Padilla
mitigation_plan: FOM was reduced on the affected Ashburn regions to stabilize load, and additional SS regions were requested for the SS map. SRMM indicated that adding an extra SR path would not help.
longterm_mitigation: OIPACL maps should be leverage over custom SS map.

Would like to understand why exactly we are unable to turn off MTLS selectively for specific path and why is MTLS G2O running for the net-storage origin and should it not be off by default for internal requests ?
executive_summary:
The global NetStorage mTLS disable guard depends on this variable "AKA_PM_ORIGIN_TYPE".
When the policy activates on /ib4b and rewrites the forward destination to bnz-oc3.download.akamai.com, AKA_PM_ORIGIN_TYPE remains "customer" but it is never updated to the netstorage when the NIMBUS Cloudlet changes the forward destination. 

Site-failover works because that path explicitly sets AKA_PM_ORIGIN_TYPE=netstorage in metadata, which triggers the guard correctly.

summary: 1/0 byte CL getting cached and served downstream for "ERR_READ_TIMEOUT|before_resp_body" with 200 OK to the origin.
description:
Blank page was served intermittently to the end users. Upon checking logs we can see 1/0 byte CL getting cached and served downstream while "ERR_READ_TIMEOUT|before_resp_body" with 200 OK seen to the origin.

The sample log in https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11337642 line 20 shows that cache was refreshed & served to client after completing 304 validation with origin, but content length is 1 and page is blank.  However, the working sample in line 10 shows the correct content-length is 9989. The issue has been resolved by purging the cache.

Wider log analysis shows corrupted cache was only served from certain edge servers, the other edge servers were able to serve correct cache. Tracing the corrupted cache, found the first instance (request ID 98bd1582) at 2026/05/08-05:17:36 GMT(Line 160). 

The log of 98bd1582 (line 180) shows parent server 23.200.140.77 returned 200 OK with 1 byte after contacting origin.

Origin was stressful at the same time (Line 130) and returned some 200 OK with ERR_READ_TIMEOUT|before_resp_body and 0 content length(Line 165).


This issue matches KB000097028. Log from 23.200.140.77 with mtse=tl|4267663528|9e1789e based on the the request id 98bd1582 shows it synchronously refreshed cache in 23.46.180.208 under mtse 4294967295 (request ID 98ba62ed: line 191)

Hi,

 

You need to see *when data becomes available in the store* (sections 20, 133) and *how Ghost reads and delivers it to the client* (33, 75). The forward-side section 119 can also be added (not useful if the object is always served from cache) otherwise very useful as it logs {{ChunkedResponseInputStream}} at level 10 - logs every origin CTE chunk-size header, body bytes, trailer etc. Shows exactly what boundaries origin is sending.

 

So sections - 20 33 75 119 133

 

Note: this is going to produce a lot of log lines and might even lead to rolls. Please enable it at an arl-ID level and on specific 1 or 2 IP’s only. 

 

Regards

-Savan

They would like to have ERE's review and help apply pre-spreading from DNSP-Dev over the hostname that has high concurrent server-to-server test as well as used for end user's live streaming.

Backup TD map ([chausf.akamai.net|https://akamai.my.salesforce.com/servlet/servlet.ExternalRedirect?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchausf.akamai.net])

longterm_mitigation: Customer to follow best practices.

summary: High response times during peak hours for TWC
description:
Customer has been tracking the response time for their API calls on api.weather.com and seeing P99 reaching 5 seconds during peak hours. We've maprule suspended certain regions that had a relatively high number of slow responses; other regions continue to show high response times, indicating a need for change at a config/ platform level. 
Their P99 values hover around 1-2 seconds for most of the day, while it goes up to 5 seconds during their peak hours (morning when folks check the weather). Customer mentioned that the West Coast seems to be more impacted, while they also see instances from the East Coast as well. Clients are AWS machines, so they're isolated to a handful of regions. They're also making 100 streams per connection with HTTP/2, which we're considering bringing it down to a manageable 25 streams per connection. Not sure if this will help, as the number per connection while connected should be manageable by the server.  

[The change to shard MPG spread on FF API map rules|https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/GSPMAPSTRA-5510] doesn't appear to have helped with response times, while it was enabled.

May 14th, 12:55 - 12:58
P99 from our logs show 5.52 seconds. For the specific subnet 23.219.77 (which r50188 and r50189 are part of), we saw P99 at 9.76 seconds, while for other regions, P99 was 1.18 seconds.

executive_summary: Customer has been seeing high P99 response times for their api.weather.com property, especially during peak hours for their traffic, going to around 5 seconds or so. Our log analysis shows certain regions contributing mostly to those high response times. Origin response times are mostly low, and the ones customers have been reviewing are for TCP_HIT. What options do we have to reduce the P99 value for response time?
resolution_description: there was not one commonality on the ghost regions that would cause these issues. There was some signs of load issues, but not always the same customer at fault. Customer is testing split hostname for aws connections to us (2 leg  setup clients > akam > aws > akam > origin ) , expectation that both legs should yield <1s at 99th %ile and reducing h2 # connections
root_cause: monitoring at 99th %ile - ask for improvements
creator: Senthuran Selvanayagam
mitigation_plan: split hostname to api shards, lower connection on h2, expectation
longterm_mitigation: there was some observation of imbalanced cpu, looking at more details under GURU ticket.

executive_summary:
April 29 – Early May 2026 :
Expedia began migrating traffic (api.epsapi.cn) from ChinaCDN to Tencent EdgeOne, injecting ~300K RPS (30 GB/s) of server-to-server load. Localized edge CPUs spiked to 100%, triggering an automated deny rule (crp-rule-req-deny-lat20-1sec) that dropped traffic with HTTP 503s. Complex GTM indirection also broke the CNAME chain, misreporting the load as "unassigned load" (Maprule -1).

May 27, 2026 :Engineering rolled back the strict 1-second latency rule and deployed a safer threshold. This immediately cleared the massive HTTP 503 drops for Expedia.

June 2 :The heavy traffic volume began bleeding outside of China, causing severe load spikes in South Korea and Belgium, risking impact to major customers like Coupang. 
On June 4, a permanent reporting fix (MAPPINGENG-8539) was deployed via a CNameAssociations.json override, fully restoring monitoring visibility.

June 9, 2026 :EngMapping teams finalized the long-term solution under MAPPINGENG-8547. It was confirmed that active traffic is landing on the new slot 372250. The team agreed to remove the China region restriction from slot 40209 and map slot 372250 to a dedicated Serial 4025 with 32 minGhosts.Which will take place on. a 3rd week of June(Around 15th June)
resolution_description: The customer-facing impact (HTTP 503 errors) was resolved by rolling back the aggressive CRP deny rule and replacing it with a safer latency threshold. The backend visibility issue was fixed by deploying a CNameAssociations.json override under MAPPINGENG-8539, which corrected the CNAME chain routing and restored full load-reporting visibility. Permanent capacity and stability are being finalized under MAPPINGENG-8547 (scheduled for the week of June 15, 2026), which will transition slot 40209 and the new slot 372250 to an expanded, region-free global pre-spread to safely absorb the massive Tencent migration load worldwide.
root_cause:
Massive traffic from localized Tencent IPs was concentrated on a few edge nodes instead of being spread out globally.
An extra layer of GTM indirection broke the CNAME chain, blinding our monitoring systems by tracking traffic as unassigned load (Maprule -1).
Localized 100% CPU spikes triggered an automated deny rule (crp-rule-req-deny-lat20-1sec), dropping 100% of requests and causing 503 errors.
creator: Jerrika Chinchilla
mitigation_plan:
Engineering rolled back the strict 1-second latency rule and replaced it with a safer threshold, immediately eliminating the HTTP 503 errors.
Expedia temporarily shifted a portion of traffic away from concentrated EIPB VIPs to non-EIPB hostnames to lower immediate pressure.
longterm_mitigation:
Reporting Fix (MAPPINGENG-8539): Deployed a CNameAssociations.json override fix on June 4th, fully correcting the CNAME routing and restoring complete monitoring visibility.

Global Pre-spread Plan (MAPPINGENG-8547): Scheduled for execution next week (week of June 15th) to permanently absorb the load:
Slot 40209: Remove the ChinaCDN_ESSL restriction to turn the 24-ghost pre-spread into a global, region-free setup.
Slot 372250 (New Slot): Move it to a dedicated Serial 4025 with a bumped capacity of 32 minGhosts to safely handle the upcoming June ChinaCDN EOL traffic double-up.
