summary: {F-CS-11344833} TCP Connection Failures due to overloaded parent regions
description:
Account: PT Bank Mandiri (PERSERO) Tbk
Domain: mobile.ak.omni.bankmandiri.co.id
CPCODE: 1558149 and 1558150
Property: mobile.ak.omni.bankmandiri.co.id.optimized v25

Issue:
Customer reported high Edge Turnaround Time in TrafficPeak monitoring during 2026/5/15 19:17–19:32 JKT.

We found that the high Edge Turnaround Time appears to stem from midgress connection failures with the error ERR_CONNECT_FAIL|linux between regions 38879 and 51946.

From the sample logs, the midgress child edge in region 38879 showed around 17s transfer time when connecting to parent region 51946, before eventually encountering *ERR_CONNECT_FAIL|linux. This ~17s transfer time* was then reflected in the customer’s monitoring as high Edge Turnaround Time.


Sample logs can be found here:
https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11344833 refer to lines 225–388.


We also validated the network condition for regions 38879 and 51946, but we did not observe any significant network issue. Therefore, we further checked the cache logs for region 51946, where we found high forward-in-progress and high network transmit values:
{noformat}
HIGH_FWD_INPROG=5018 HIGH_NET_TX=2135Mbps MEM_PRESSURE=N FreeFds=7609 client_inprog=5421 fwd_inprog=5018 fwd_new_done=9610/9607 websockets=3185 NET_TX=2135Mbps SSL_Q=0/0
{noformat}

This suggests that the machine or cluster may have been overwhelmed by traffic, which could have contributed to the slowness.

Region logs (https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11344833 line 501 -521) suggested surge of traffic due to tiktok. And from the logs, almost all ERR_CONNECT_FAIL|linux instances ended with *approximately 17s transfer time*. Please refer to the same Etherpad, lines 570–582 and 628–640.

However, we could not find any timeout setting or configuration that explains why the connection fails after approximately 17 seconds.


Ask:
a) Is this ~17s wait before ERR_CONNECT_FAIL|linux controlled by metadata or any preset configuration? If yes, which configuration controls this value?
b) Is there any way to override or shorten this timeout?
root_cause: Parent region 51946 was overwhelmed by traffic (HIGH_FWD_INPROG=5018, HIGH_NET_TX=2135Mbps) due to a surge of tiktok traffic, causing midgress TCP connection failures (ERR_CONNECT_FAIL|linux) between regions 38879 and 51946. The ~17s timeout before failure is due to 4 tcp_syn_retries — a platform-level kernel setting with no available ARL-level config override.
creator: Alan Boon
mitigation_plan: Information request resolved via consultation. The ~17s wait before ERR_CONNECT_FAIL|linux is controlled by 4 tcp_syn_retries (platform-level kernel setting). No configuration override or shortening is available at the ARL level.
longterm_mitigation: NA

summary: {F-CS-11310950} HTTP Header Injection (SSRF) scan failure for client ITRI
description:
Account: Industrial Technology Research Institute (Indirect_Customer)
Host: ops.kcg.gov.tw / ops.kcg.gov.tw.edgekey.net
Cert CN: ops.kcg.gov.tw
Slots: 64056
SNI-only: On

Issue:
Customer conducted a recent security vulnerability notification for '150307 HTTP Header Injection' and it failed their test.

Please note that the primary site in question for this investigation is
https://ops.kcg.gov.tw/geoserver/

{quote}
The security scanner identifies a potential SSRF risk by injecting a test domain into the HTTP header, such as the Host header. If it detects a subsequent DNS query for that test domain, it flags the vulnerability

As the client's service domain is protected by Akamai and CNAME'd to Akamai Edge servers, we conducted some lab testing using webhook.site to reproduce the issue. We noticed that although the traffic does not appear to reach the Akamai Property, the DNS query is still triggered. Upon further investigation, we found that the source IP of this DNS request belongs to an Akamai Edge server

Could you please help us analyse this behaviour and clarify the technical reason why the Edge server initiates a DNS lookup for the injected domain in this scenario

We would also like to confirm if this is an expected mechanism on your end, and would highly appreciate your advice on whether it can be mitigated or fixed, as the current behaviour continuously causes the client's security scans to fail
{quote}

The customer's DNS servers logged DNS query from Akamai Edge servers for the test HOST header.
The injected HOST header = test20260518.0bf58b71-ce17-4eda-bd9c-4fbd2c4ab705.dnshook.site
And this was logged:
#9.2ff37468.1779093250.285e91cd
{noformat}
104.116.243.47 r 1779093250.540 - 0 0 1 312 312 522 61.66.78.70 GET /khpipe/default_c.aspx 400 ERR_INVALID_URL|invalidurlorhost - text/html test20260518.0bf58b71-ce17-4eda-bd9c-4fbd2c4ab705.dnshook.site - - - - - 97 - 48 - - f2dca8f9 0 - 285e91cd 16382. - - nrp - - - - - 116 116 44944 0 - - - WJ - r7e5d7dbb6bd0.-1.n.g - 8 - 8f1c4880 - - - - - 0 - - - - - h - - - sn=||64056|;netp=s;tff=0;mle=34042;rx=43||37:83:2 - - - 12:854:0:0 UNSET:UNSET::UNSET:: - ett=1;cpu=//thd@phtm54/57;rct=n;swapsz=ok;rawhs=0 - - - - - 244 0 - - - - - -
{noformat}

We told the customer:
_Since the Host header did not match any hostname configured on Akamai, a 400 Bad Request response was returned._

And this community post was shared with the customer:
https://community.akamai.com/customers/s/article/Is-the-site-vulnerable-to-Host-Header-Injection

Customer has accepted the answer. However they are concerned with GHost trying to resolve the injected HOST header. And they are concerned with high volumes of DNS lookups overwhelming their DNS servers if such an attack takes place.

Etherpad: https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11310950


Ask:
Could you please help us understand whether this behaviour is expected?
If yes, what can we share with the customer regarding this behaviour?
executive_summary:
Customer conducted a recent security vulnerability notification for '150307 HTTP Header Injection' and it failed their test. The Edge server initiates a DNS lookup for the injected domain
It is a built-in pipeline behavior. Ghost first starts resolving the Host header for origin connection preparation before the property validation check and returned the request with 400 ERR_INVALID_URL|invalidurlorhost and aborted the forward path, so their backend was never reached and nothing was forwarded.
root_cause: It is an intentional behavior of Edge server initiates a DNS lookup for the injected domain
creator: Alan Boon
mitigation_plan: NA
longterm_mitigation: NA

As per RFC https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7230#section-5.4 is sending "Host: m.zara.com:80@bugbounty-test-host.vercel.app" should strictkly be blocked and served with 400 Bad request, however we are not seeing the RFC being honored.

It violates the ABNF Syntax Rule
RFC 7230 - 5.4 explicitly dictates the allowed grammatical structure for the header:
Host = uri-host [ ":" port ]

The standard definition of a uri-host (defined in RFC 3986) absolutely prohibits the @ character. A host can only be a domain name (like test.com), an IPv4 address, or a bracketed IPv6 address. Because the string contains an @ symbol, it completely fails to conform to this mandatory structural format.

summary: {PT Bank Mandiri} SSL Connect Timeouts due to overloaded Parent regions
description:
Account: PT Bank Mandiri (PERSERO) Tbk

Domain: [mobile.ak.omni.bankmandiri.co.id|https://mobile.ak.omni.bankmandiri.co.id/]

CPCODE: 1558149 and 1558150

Property: mobile.ak.omni.bankmandiri.co.id.optimized v25

Issue: Customer has been reporting slowness(high turnaround time) from parent servers starting around April 24th.

Based on the log analysis, we observed spike in SSL connect timeouts between Edge parent regions and there was no 5xx errors at the delivery observed due to these timeouts as the retries were successful, however, we observed high response times at the edge. summary: Machines under r38798 had ghost rolls for reason '[256] Received Segment Violation...dying'
description:
There were machine suspensions and ghost rolls in TD0 region 38798 at May 21, 09:50 to 10:00 GMT.
These suspensions led to requests taking the failover route towards the Origin which in turn led to high requests towards the Origin.

Akatec raised a NOCC ticket (B-W-1H0F8P5) https://issues.deploy.akamai.com/cgi-bin/view.cgi?issue_id=B-W-1H0F8P5 to know the reason for suspensions. However, NOCC asked to reach out to ERE for more information on these suspensions.

Updated https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11365964 with cache.logs, suspension/ ghost roll details and coredump
executive_summary: On May 21st, multiple edge servers in Region 38798 experienced sudden process crashes due to Ghost rolls with exit code 256. This drop in server capacity forced active live-streaming requests to take a backup failover route. Because a cache-bypass setting was enabled for failovers in the customer configuration, the diverted traffic bypassed the edge cache and went straight to the origin server, causing a massive traffic spike and performance degradation.
resolution_description: The active testing traffic was immediately stopped after being traced back to a single internal Akamai test IP out of the Bangalore office. We coordinated with the account Technical Project Manager to scale down the testing frequency and ensure the immediate stability of the region.
root_cause: The incident was triggered by an internal Akamai team running load and error-handling tests for FIFA event readiness using a specific property. Their test requests included a custom debug header that matched a production configuration rule, which unexpectedly instructed Ghost to inject a fake read error into production traffic. When Ghost version 22.5.1 processed this simulation request, it entered a test-only code path that tried to access a socket stream object. Because the request was still in the early stages of reading HTTP headers, this object was entirely null. The code lacked a null check and blindly dereferenced the empty pointer, causing an immediate segmentation fault that crashed the process.
creator: Senthilkumar Rajendiran
mitigation_plan: We are actively coordinating with the IAT  to review and restrict the use of raw error-simulation tags on the production network. Internal teams must halt these production tests or implement strict security and scoping guidelines to ensure test headers do not impact production servers or adjacent customer traffic.
longterm_mitigation: On the engineering side, the ERE team is tracking a software fix to add a defensive null guard to the socket stream variable within the HTTP stream class, preventing any future simulation path triggers from causing a process crash.

summary: Customer reported 5030 player errors because of midgress 503 spikes associated with Flit spike.
description:
Log analysis during the anomaly window (May 23, 14:07–14:20 UTC) showed a high volume of 503 responses alongside ERR_FWD_SSL_HANDSHAKE errors (err_conn_strict_cert:ssl0:5:104). The ERR_FWD_SSL_HANDSHAKE errors were prominently served by edge nodes in Region 37658. Most affected requests were eventually recovered via fail action.

NOCC analyzed the cache logs on 23.199.69.182 and captured resource constraints.

1. Flit Utilization spiked repeatedly between 95% and 109%, forcing Ghost to suspend prefetching/icp behavior.
2. High average manager cycle times were recorded, escalating sharply from ~94ms up to 611ms during peak degradation.

Due to the severe Flit utilization, edge nodes automatically triggered machine suspensions, as captured by gSuspendFlag: 2048 logs at consecutive intervals (e.g., 14:12, 14:16, 14:17, and 14:49 UTC).

Concurrently, edge nodes within this shared region experienced an intense request surge (peaking over 2,300+ requests/sec per log sample line) directed entirely at the domain p16-common-sign.tiktokcdn.com.

https://lg.netarch.akamai.com/cgi-bin/loadgraphs?period=start1779537240end1779552360&region=37658&network=A&maprule=&display=maprule&ymax=&utcoffset=5

mr96 flit spike - ByteDance non-US image edge map



Analysis: https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11373435

Need ERE's assistance in handling this flit spike as IPL qualifiers are starting from tomorrow.

summary: [F-CS-11345567]-Timeouts on client side due to high response time
description:
Issue: Customer has reported timeouts on their service starting 18:00 UTC, May 11th.

 

Environment: Customer has a service that makes several thousand POST requests to path [https://fms.viacomcbs.digital/lookup] . These POST requests are cacheable.

For these service calls to succeed, the 99% percentile latency of requests should be under 450 ms; otherwise, it starts timing out. Starting May 11th, they noticed an increase in the timeouts. Screenshot shared by customer: 

!Screenshot 2026-05-22 at 4.19.25 PM.png|width=377,height=114!

Hostname: fms.viacomcbs.digital

Product: ION Standard

Timeframe: 18:00 UTC, May 11th

 

We did a comparison of cpcode logs for May 10th (baseline) and May 13th (during incident) to establish the deviation in performance.  - [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/ER-269259] line 32

Analysis of client CIDRs indicates no significant difference. Top client IPs belong to AWS CIDRs, and the incoming request traffic is sourced from the same location. - [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/ER-269259] line 51

Tracing a specific sample high-latency request shows the bottleneck occurs primarily on the edge-to-mch leg. - [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/ER-269259] line 65

Identifying top child edges with latency exceeding 400ms. Few child regions standout. The forward request distribution towards the MCH layer does not show any commonality. - [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/ER-269259] line 104

Looking at logs for 10th May, a similar set of IPs was there. Though the impact/count of such slow requests was less and would have not triggered the customer's monitoring thresholds. [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/ER-269259] line 127

These regions are consistent in the 10 May and 13 May logs that show greater than 400 ms:
52523, 48991, 43842, 47618

Out of these, r52523 stands out with the highest count and also looks under pressure. The other regions look good in comparison. 

[https://lg.netarch.akamai.com/cgi-bin/loadgraphs?period=5w&region=52523&network=A&maprule=&display=region&ymax=&utcoffset=-6]

[https://lg.netarch.akamai.com/cgi-bin/loadgraphs?period=5w&region=47618&network=A&maprule=&display=region&ymax=&utcoffset=-6]

[https://lg.netarch.akamai.com/cgi-bin/loadgraphs?period=5w&region=48991&network=A&maprule=&display=region&ymax=&utcoffset=-6]

[https://lg.netarch.akamai.com/cgi-bin/loadgraphs?period=5w&region=43842&network=A&maprule=&display=region&ymax=&utcoffset=-6]

Checking region 52523 further, we see that this region logged some unassigned load around 18 GMT on 11th May, that aligns with the customer's graph. 

!Screenshot 2026-05-26 at 01.11.03.jpg|width=317,height=302!
[https://lg.netarch.akamai.com/cgi-bin/loadgraphs?period=start1778503800end1778539380&region=52523&network=W&maprule=&display=maprule&ymax=&utcoffset=5]

Similarly in DNSP we see serial 1457 spiking around same time around 18:00 GMT
[https://mapper.akamai.com/short/CUc0ng9X91]

 

May 10th for comparison: [https://mapper.akamai.com/short/jbT4vtkqMK]


According to grafana the 1457 serial load is for cpcode 1896000 belonging to Airbnb.
[https://grafana-hats2-epremo.akamai.com/d/d398c61b-4cb5-4498-ada8-dc08c4962553/region-dnsp-serial-spikes-and-cpcode-traffic?orgId=1&var-service=W&var-dnsp_serial=1457&var-region=52523&var-hats_serial=-&var-account_regex=.&var-cpcodes=-&var-top_n=10&var-flit_util_thres=90&from=1778457600000&to=1778543999000]

 

Could you please help review the data and validate if the load on 52523 and 47618 is contributing to slowness reported by the customer? Is there any recommendation that can help improve overall performance for this property and bring it in line with customers' expectations?
root_cause: Starting May 11th, IAD regions r52523 and r47618 experienced increased unassigned flit load. Investigation identified that prewarm.muscache.com (Airbnb, serial 6141) had switched to FF with a custom behavior overriding maprule reporting from r map to a map, causing its traffic to appear as unassigned flit. Concentrated AWS client IPs from Airbnb hitting IAD drove these regions above capacity, causing high turnaround times on the edge-to-mch leg and client-side timeouts for Paramount (fms.viacomcbs.digital) which shares the same edge regions.
creator: Sameer Gupta
mitigation_plan: FOM was reduced to 70% on r52523 and r47618 (ref: B-W-1HM9IY5) as immediate mitigation. FOM was further reduced to 60% on the top 2 edge regions. IAT was asked to fix Airbnb's maprule reporting for Freeflow; the fix was applied on 06/03 16:54 GMT, after which unassigned load dropped and regions stabilized.
longterm_mitigation: platform-mapping

resolution_description: A permanent software fix is currently being engineered by the Ghost Core HTTP/2 team under tracking tickets GREL-5726 and GHOST-7972. The patch refactors the proxy engine to ensure that an empty DATA frame containing an END_STREAM flag accurately computes to an object size of 0 bytes, properly translating the response to a standard Content-Length: 0 header. This fix is slated to go through the standard QA validation cycle and completely roll out across the global production network within approximately one month (estimated early July 2026).
root_cause: The ERR_CHUNK_INCOMPLETE error is caused by a protocol translation bug within the Akamai Ghost H2G2O (HTTP/2 Gateway to Origin) layer during empty response handling. When a customer backend responds over HTTP/2 with a HEADERS frame followed by an empty DATA frame (0 bytes) carrying the END_STREAM flag, the H2G2O parsing layer misinterprets the empty container and incorrectly calculates the object size as 1 byte. Because Ghost expects a 1-byte body but immediately receives a clean HTTP/1.1 chunked termination sequence, the translation engine throws a ChunkedEofBeforeFirstHexDigitException, forcing the edge to output a faulty Content-Length: 1 header and drop the client connection prematurely.
creator: Javier Padilla
mitigation_plan: To immediately resolve the client-facing errors while the code fix is in development, the customer must temporarily disable H2G2O in their property configuration (or revert Staging to version 279). Turning off HTTP/2 to the origin forces Ghost to fall back to a standard HTTP/1.1 forwarding path, which successfully processes and passes the origin's empty chunked responses without triggering the parsing exception.
longterm_mitigation: The long-term strategy requires monitoring the engineering release cycle for the global deployment of GREL-5726. Once active, the team will coordinate with the customer to safely re-enable H2G2O and run regression testing against the /healthcheck endpoint. Additionally, Akamai will integrate this specific HTTP/2 framing edge-case (HEADERS without END_STREAM followed by an empty DATA frame) into the core Ghost automated test suites to prevent future protocol translation regression bugs.

summary: {F-CS-11311722} Intermittent Server Hello slowness over 3 seconds causes API endpoint connection timeout
description:
h2. +*Environment:*+

Product:   API-X (FF)
Property Hostname:  api.accounts.nintendo.com
Handout Cnames by GTM:   a2047.api[1-9].akamai.net
Slot: 45736, Standard TLS (SNI), CN=*.accounts.nintendo.com
Maprule ID:  15211-15219
CPcode: 1650949
h2. +*Issue:*+

When some clients attempt to request the aforementioned domains, a delay occurs in the "Server Hello" response from the Edge server. This delay exceeds the client-side connection timeout (3 seconds), resulting in a Net::OpenTimeout error. Based on our tcpdump analysis, we have observed several cases where the TLS handshake takes approximately 3 to 4 seconds to complete.

For other types of errors other than TLS handshake slowness at the customer’s monitoring stats, there are no obvious degradation observed;
 * *TCP Connection Errors* - While the frequency is low compared to TLS handshake delays, the customer has confirmed some occurrences of this error.
 ** Error Message: Failed to open TCP connection to (api.accounts.nintendo.com or accounts.nintendo.com):443 (execution expired)
 * *ECONNREFUSED (Connection Refused)* - Customer have not confirmed any instances of this error at this time.
 * *ECONNRESET (RST Packet)* - The frequency is low compared to TLS handshake delays, but we have confirmed some occurrences.
 ** Error Message: Connection reset by peer - SSL_connect

In the customer’s monitoring system the alert is fired when over 300 errors are detected in a two minutes window, and it has happened 4 or 5 times per month. +The error rate is 0.1% at most per day.+ 

Here is the part of customer’s report regarding the tendency of occurence;

Our assessment is that the occurrence of this error does not correlate with total traffic volume and is likely random.
 * *Monthly Traffic Analysis* - Error counts have increased since February; however, total user requests to the game server have remained stable from January to April. Since traffic to the specific domain should follow this same trend, we have ruled out monthly traffic growth as the root cause.
 * *Hourly Traffic Analysis* - No correlation was found between traffic volume and error frequency by time of day. For example, on April 16th, the error peak occurred at 13:00 (UTC), while the traffic peak was at 06:00 (UTC). This significant offset suggests the two are unrelated.
 * *Server Load Analysis* - We cross-referenced the error timestamps with backend server CPU utilization (load per instance), but no regularity was identified. Given these findings, we conclude this is not a timeout issue caused by origin resource saturation or congestion. We suspect intermittent, random latency is occurring mid-path (e.g., during handshake processes on Akamai edge servers). 

*Background History:*
For the objective domain the customer had been away from Akamai over two years, and decided to return from AWS to Akamai on January 22nd, 2026. It was a phased approach, starting from 1% on Jan 22, 10% on Feb 2nd, 25% on Feb 9th, 50% on Feb 16th, 100% on Feb 24th.

*Current Business Impact:*
Under the current specifications, the customer’s system is designed so that the client application automatically executes internal retries when a communication error occurs. Therefore, an error message is not immediately displayed to the end-user. However, these retry attempts may cause the screen to load longer, potentially leading to temporary performance delays. An error message will only be displayed to the end-user if the connection is not restored even after these retry attempts. While this has not resulted in a critical failure, it may be degrading the user experience, and we would like to improve this. Furthermore, from a different perspective, the operational workload required to handle these alerts cannot be ignored. The customer hopes to identify the root cause as soon as possible.

executive_summary:
4th June
It's not intended use-case for customer but the customer checked for the behavior in the exceptional case, and found it's not working. 
When the client sends X-Akamai-Edgescape: foo, Ghost sets has_edgescape = 1, With the flag set, the lookup is skipped and asip->asi_info->edgescape stays null. The outgoing origin request is built from ASI info  so if asip->asi_info->edgescape is null, no X-Akamai-Edgescape header is added to the origin request at all.
I believe this does not show any urgency to resolve this behavior, I will discuss this internally,

23rd June
I discussed this issue internally, as I mentioned it is working as per the design code and intentional behavior, this sounds like a non issue,

creator: Yasuhiro Oyabu
mitigation_plan: NA, Expected Behavior as per code design
longterm_mitigation: NA, Expected Behavior as per code design

resolution_description: Engineering is fixing this under ORS-16518 by updating the backend code to accept the new API fields with null-safety, running a SQL script to update the database template variables, and aligning with the Metadata team to prevent origin authentication breakages.
root_cause: A recent Property Manager API update (PM-26.4) removed the useCustomSignString field, replacing it with an encrypted storage model. The Cloud Wrapper backend (Behavior.java) still expected this field, causing it to deserialize as null and throw a NullPointerException. This only breaks MCDN activations because standard activations bypass the affected FreeMarker template.
creator: Cesar Roque Quiros
mitigation_plan: Temporarily disable MCDN if urgent configuration deployments are needed, as standard activations will bypass the bug and deploy successfully.
longterm_mitigation: Deploy the permanent fix under ORS-16518, update runbooks with pre-activation validation checks, and expand automated regression testing to catch upstream API contract changes before they hit production.

summary: Loss across TATA clusters in India posing a risk to IPL's final match broadcast [SI-00023813]
description: Starting from 05:57 UTC May 31, 2026, TATA clusters across India experienced losses. Akamai responded by suspending the impacted clusters and the issue subsided at 08:59 UTC. The issue reappeared at 10:13 UTC but initial investigation shows loss only in IN-MAA (Chennai). There was a Risk that the outage could impact [Jiostar's stream of the IPL final match|https://collaborate.akamai.com/confluence/spaces/IRAPT/pages/1371806652/Jiostar+India+-+Indian+Premier+League+2026+-+28+Mar-31+May?] but there were no customer reports of impact during the broadcast. As the IPL's final match broadcast has{color:#000000} concluded,{color}with no issues the incident will move to phase 2. The incident response team has concluded that the suspended regions will remain suspended until TATA provides the cause of the issue and confirms the absence of further issues.
resolution_description: Re-applied DENY_ALL to TCL_DOM links at TATA-MAA
root_cause:
Across India MLEs, TCL_DOM contract is used as an outbound route, and as expected, TCL was not accepting any of our prefixes. 
A DENY-ALL policy is applied towards TCL_DOM to prevent any accidental advertisements so that TATA doesn't prefer this path for routing inbound traffic. 

On 31st May, at around 05:57 UTC, Akamai accidentally started advertising our routes over TCL_DOM port at r01.maa01.ien, and these advertised prefixes from the TCL_DOM port were being selected as best paths, resulting in packet loss.
creator: Sandeep Jain
mitigation_plan: Ecor suspension to avoid impact during IPL event.
longterm_mitigation: Better router config change safety process and proactive detection.

summary: Performanace degradation for Saudi Telecommunications Company STC
description:
h3. *1. Business Impact & Background*
 * *Customer:* Sony Interactive Entertainment Inc. (Japan)

 * *Target Resolution Date:* *End of August (Critical)*

 * *Business Justification:* Sony uses a Multi-CDN strategy for PlayStation 5 data delivery, distributing traffic strictly based on price and performance. The customer reported that Akamai’s performance in Saudi Arabia was solid until last December but has significantly degraded since January.

 * 
 ** *Risk:* The next contract renewal is in {*}September{*}. If we do not improve performance in Saudi Arabia by the end of August, we are at high risk of losing traffic share to our competitors.

 * *Customer Evidence:* [Sony Customer Claim Data (Google Drive)|https://drive.google.com/file/d/1cD2jA0CL1t4vDE2MHhHQ5EDDQPnEAxJ1/view?usp=drive_link&authuser=3]

h3. *2. Problem Statement*

Sony PS5 traffic originating from Saudi Arabia is experiencing poor performance primarily due to highly suboptimal mapping and capacity issues, specifically regarding the *Saudi Telecommunications Company (STC)* network.
h3. *3. Investigation Findings*

_Full investigation details can be found on Etherpad: [F-CS-11364928|https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11364928]_

*Finding 1: Suboptimal Out-of-Country Mapping (Etherpad line 74-114)*

Performance drops significantly when SA clients are mapped to out-of-country edge servers. Instead of being mapped to geographically adjacent regions, a massive portion of traffic (~37%) is being routed across the ocean to Italy (IT).
|*Edge Country*|*Avg Mbps*|*Samples*|*% Samples*|
|GR|57.21|2|0.04 %|
|ES|43.10|167|2.98 %|
|*SA*|*32.13*|*3111*|*55.48 %*|
|FR|29.83|13|0.23 %|
|US|29.01|7|0.12 %|
|NL|27.52|1|0.02 %|
|*IT*|*23.85*|*2072*|*36.95 %*|
|DE|22.62|232|4.14 %|
|TW|16.83|2|0.04 %|

*Finding 2: Extremely Poor In-Country Mapping for STC (Etherpad line 117-123)*

Average in-country mapping for STC is hovering around {*}40%{*}, frequently dropping to a minimum of {*}0%{*}.
 * [Grafana Dashboard: STC In-country mapping|https://grafana-dmz.akam.ai/org1506/dashboard/db/maprule-qos-v-4-2?from=now-30d&to=now&var-business_unit_owner=Media&var-service=W&var-map_type=edge&var-ip_version=v4Only&var-map_group=All&var-map=W.w25&var-continent=AS&var-geo_name=Saudi%20Arabia&var-provider_name=SAUDI_TELECOMMUNICATIONS_COMPANY_STC&var-case=All]

*Finding 3: STC Regions Reaching {{ra_overflow}} (Etherpad line 125-134)*

Multiple STC regions are reaching {{ra_overflow}} for flits, causing traffic to be spilled over.
 * [Loadgraphs: STC Overflow Data|https://lg.netarch.akamai.com/cgi-bin/loadgraphs?period=2w&region=29348%2C29353%2C33282%2C33696%2C41022%2C41023%2C42214%2C%2C42759%2C50581&network=A&maprule=&display=maprule&ymax=&utcoffset=9]

*Finding 4: Priority Conflict with ByteDance Traffic*

ByteDance non-US image traffic is consuming a high amount of flits on the same regions. While MapRule 96 (ByteDance) holds a higher priority, it should not justify Sony's in-country ratio collapsing to 0-40%.
{code:java}
[yiguchi@lsg-gss16 ~]$ sql2 -q mapper2aggs.dev.akamai.com 'select * from MCM_MapRules where mapRuleId = 96'
mapRuleId name service ghostOnly priority type status mode description
--------- ---------------- ------- --------- -------- ------- ------------------- ---- -------------------------------
96 a;mm2.akamai.net W 0 5 default customer_supporting full ByteDance non-US image edge map {code}
 * [Loadgraphs: ByteDance Traffic MapRule 96|https://lg.netarch.akamai.com/cgi-bin/loadgraphs?period=2w&region=29348%2C29353%2C33282%2C33696%2C41022%2C41023%2C42214%2C%2C42759%2C50581&network=A&maprule=96&display=maprule&ymax=&utcoffset=9]

*Finding 5: Timeline Correlation*

Our internal data confirms that the drop in STC In-Geo mapping started in January, which perfectly aligns with the timeline of the customer's claims.
 * [Grafana Dashboard: 1-Year Trend|https://grafana-dmz.akam.ai/org1506/dashboard/db/maprule-qos-v-4-2?from=now-1y&to=now&var-business_unit_owner=Media&var-service=W&var-map_type=edge&var-ip_version=v4Only&var-map_group=All&var-map=W.w25&var-continent=AS&var-geo_name=Saudi%20Arabia&var-provider_name=SAUDI_TELECOMMUNICATIONS_COMPANY_STC&var-case=All]

h3. *4. Requested Actions (Ask)*
 # *Capacity & Mapping Strategy:* Please advise immediate guidance and make adjustments to improve Sony's performance for Saudi Telecommunications Company (STC) clients.
 # *Map Priority Review:* Investigate if we can balance the flits utilization between ByteDance (mr 96) and Sony to ensure Sony does not suffer from 0-40% in-country drop-offs.
root_cause: A shortage of in-country capacity resulted in degraded performance.
creator: Dimitris Kim
mitigation_plan: NA.
longterm_mitigation: Capacity should be restored and built.

summary: {F-CS-11403308} TIAA saw behaviour change with last ghost release for mTLS
description:
Starting May 22 TIAA started noticing that ssl session reuse no longer sent the client cert information to the customer origin.  This leads to them 403 ing and reauthing leading to extra sessions at the origin. Unfortunately we have finished the last release and it was just escalated today.

Do we have a way to restore the old behavior of always sending the client cert down? Do we know what would have caused the change in the last release more specifically than the openssl 3.0->3.5 upgrade 

* To be clear c2g does a resumption without the client cert, the forward header information is not filled out.
creator: Billy Tiemann

description:
Flipkart team has reached out to us for the API domain onboarding.
 
Here is the stats shared by Flipkart team on the expected API traffic:
|*Origin IP* *Address*|*Timeline*|*Inbound traffic*|*Outbound traffic*|*QPS*|
|*MAX*|*AVG*|*MAX*|*AVG*|*MAX*|*AVG*|
|103.243.33.5|Last 30 Days|948 MB/s|400 MB/s|1.67 GB/s|520 MB/s|204984 rd/s|103360 rd/s|
|During BBD|1.70 GB/s|338 MB/s|5.50 GB/s|995 MB/s|653185 rd/s|86426 rd/s|
|163.53.76.64|Last 30 Days|933 MB/s|391 MB/s|1.64 GB/s|507 MB/s|201462 rd/s|99904 rd/s|
|During BBD|1.59 GB/s|314 MB/s|5.51 GB/s|936 MB/s|628067 rd/s|82727rd/s|
 
We also engaged the EA team to help with the optimization recommendations and are working on it. 
 
However, we wanted to check on the below query:
As per this document: [+https://collaborate.akamai.com/confluence/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=709398033&spaceKey=MDE&title=Metadata%2BComponent%2BDesign%2BOrigin%2BIP%2BACLs%2Bfor%2BEdge%2BDelivery%2BPhase%2BGA#+]
 
If we just use OIPACL —> the maps will be *api-e6827.akasrg.akamai.com and* [*+ch42.akamaiedge.net+*|http://ch42.akamaiedge.net/] ** (Fallback)
If we use OIPACL +  "AKA_PM_OIPACL_RA_ONLY=1"" —> the maps will be [+ch42.akamaiedge.net+|http://ch42.akamaiedge.net/] and [+ch43.akamaiedge.net+|http://ch43.akamaiedge.net/] (Fallback)
 
We want to use OIPACL with "AKA_PM_OIPACL_RA_ONLY=1" to use ch42 and ch43. Can you confirm if it's the right approach and also about the capacity on the same?
 
Also, given the above traffic estimations - {*}+we don't have any f2b data points yet+{*}. To start with - customer will initially put 5% of API traffic and later gradually scale up.
Could you please check and let us know if there are any concerns from the network side?
root_cause: Customer requested mapper and capacity guidance for onboarding Flipkart API traffic to APIx. No custom map exists for APIx; API maps are clones of each other and ESSL in IN is a mix of MLE + AANP regions. No flit data points available to assess pre-spread need.
creator: Thilaga Raju
mitigation_plan: Provided guidance on using default RA maps (ch42/ch43) or sharded GTM maps (dscapi1-dscapi10), with recommendation to distribute traffic equally across all 10 shards. Recommended engaging EA for config review. Pre-spread to be evaluated once f2b data is available post-onboarding.
longterm_mitigation: Not Applicable

resolution_description: It is required to validate the AK_LOCATION_BASE_STR' variable for the Manifest ARL(s) and make sure those are distinct enough to spread the content across multiple serials.
root_cause:
Concentration of requests on a single serial at MCH leading to specific machine overloads in a region.
A single serial is getting derived in hashing using 'AK_LOCATION_BASE_STR' for the high traffic Manifest ARL. This leads to cascading issue within machines and regions.
creator: Pratik Salunke
mitigation_plan: It is required to validate the AK_LOCATION_BASE_STR' variable for the Manifest ARL(s) and make sure those are distinct enough to spread the content across multiple serials.a

summary: {F-CS-11355385} Latency on r45659 (SDN-TYO3)
description:
h2. Environment:

Product:   Dynamic Site Accelerator

Property Hostname:  api.bs.minna-no-ginko.com

Slot: 100339, Enhanced TLS (SNI)

Maprule ID:  1327

CPcode: 1294256
h2. Issue:

The customer claims that their service performance (turnaround time in Akamai) has been intermittently degraded. Latency typically remains under 500ms, but spikes exceeding 1 second have been observed during the incidents.

+*The specific timeline:*+

2026-05-22 17:50-18:00 UTC

2026-05-23 17:00-17:10 UTC

2026-05-24 18:20-18:30 UTC
h2. Investigation:

[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11355385#L9] 
 * Confirmed OOC mapping is NOT happening in this case.
 * The cause of slowness is overload in r45659 (SDN-TYO3) and this is one of SS regions, thus the traffic delays in G2G and G2O.
 ** [https://deltron.akamai.com/job-details/5041424e-896c-4ada-bd49-458e918e11bb] (For May 22nd)
 ** G2G: >500ms (14.57%), >1s (6.68%) 
 *** !image-2026-06-08-13-02-07-941.png|width=442,height=163!
 ** G2O: >500ms (6.04%)
 *** !image-2026-06-08-13-06-43-988.png|width=442,height=136!
 ** The same pattern was observed on subsequent dates (more pronounced on May 23rd).
 * Confirmed that r45659 is unstable frequently due to the massive traffic of api.epsapi.cn (Expedia Inc, CP1291836, mr1346 (e;xs.akamaiedge.net IonPremier (SNI-ONLY child)).
 ** [Flits load|https://map.akamai.com/cgi-bin/FreeFlow/Analysis/HDB_Server.pl?startmonth=5&startday=22&startyear=2026&starthour=17&startmin=30&endmonth=5&endday=22&endyear=2026&endhour=18&endmin=30&param1=45659&dbname=production&param2=&param3=&param4=&display=graph&normalize=none&ptdisp=normal&yaxis=y-axis&size=large&scope=all&query_name=REGION_FLYTELOAD%2BOVERFLOW_MARK&customSql=] spike on May 22nd

 *** !image-2026-06-08-13-08-11-620.png|width=445,height=179!
 ** The most traffic are occupied by api.epsapi.cn - [Pliny|https://pliny-aps.akamai.com/logmon/b3721436-cd89-434c-b9d9-9292d7435838] for May 22nd

 *** !image-2026-06-08-13-10-43-437.png|width=370,height=216!
 *** In these 30 days it is not that the traffic volume surged.
 **** !image-2026-06-08-13-11-26-017.png|width=394,height=232!
 ** Mitigation Implemented:  MR1346 has been suspended on r45659 as a temporary measure in B-W-1J8CGV9. 

h2. Ask:

Given that Fukuoka Financial Group’s traffic is highly time-sensitive and prone to interference from Expedia’s traffic on shared resource r45659, I would like to request advice on further mitigation strategies or long-term load distribution measures.
root_cause:
Expedia’s migration from ChinaCDN to Tencent and Akamai is acting as an origin cache for Expedia. Tencent's pull is higher than usual for this month.
The problem is primarily tracked under ERE-3356.
creator: Yasuhiro Oyabu
mitigation_plan: The affected region was mrsuspended.
longterm_mitigation: Under ERE-3356, the prespread and loadreporting fix

description:
h2. Environment:

Product:   Dynamic Site Accelerator

Property Hostname:  api.bs.minna-no-ginko.com

Slot: 100339, Enhanced TLS (SNI)

Maprule ID:  1327

CPcode: 1294256

 

API Client IPs:  35.200.7.92, 35.200.127.71 (TOKYO, Google_LLC, AS396982)

NS for API Clients:  172.253.236.24, 172.253.6.212 (TOKYO, Google_LLC, AS15169)
h2. Issue:

Out-of-Country (OOC) mapping began occurring on 2026-05-19 for this domain, resulting in partial performance degradation of the customer’s API traffic for durations of 1–3 hours.

+*The specific timeline:*+

2026-05-18 18:20-19:10 UTC

2026-05-26 16:40-19:00 UTC

2026-06-02 14:00-15:30 UTC
h2. Investigation:

During the 2026-05-26 16:40–19:00 UTC incident, OOC mapping was confirmed to be in effect.

 [Pliny|https://deltron.akamai.com/job-details/7a3c550f-b14c-42da-9fcf-f247dd102058] - C2G Response Time

!image-2026-06-08-16-59-56-379.png|width=575,height=200!

It is still a ‘PN’ (Ping based, non-local but allowed for MPG) score result with lower ranks. [link|https://mapper.akamai.com/ip/#from%3D1779809404717%26to%3D1779825653243%26treeType%3DA%26mrule%3D153%26viperSlot%3D100339%26cidr%3D172.253.236.24%26resolver%3Dip%26useGMTTime%3Dtrue%26timeRange%3D%7B%22min%22%3A1779809404717%2C%22max%22%3A1779825653243%7D%26]

!image-2026-06-08-17-02-07-152.png|width=605,height=202!

The mapping change is attributed to intermittent ping loss observed on two of the three assigned PPs (172.253.72.141, 172.253.72.140) for MPG 29522. [link|https://mapper.akamai.com/ppl/#useGMTTime%3Dtrue%26dataFrom%3D1780419329565%26startTime%3D1780204440000%26endTime%3D1780636440000%26timeRange%3D%7B%22min%22%3A1780204440000%2C%22max%22%3A1780636440000%7D%26mainTab%3DPingFromRegionView%26regionId%3D51218%26pingPoints%3D%5B%22172.253.72.141%22%2C%22172.253.72.140%22%2C%22172.253.73.43%22%5D%26regionLookup%3Dtrue%26]

!image-2026-06-08-17-03-35-708.png|width=498,height=280!

This pattern is consistent across all three reported cases. The packet loss for these PPs occurs sporadically - approximately once per week for a few hours. We understand that this frequency does not meet the threshold to be flagged as having a 'Bad' status.
h2. Ask:

While it appears that the mapping system assigned these OOC regions based on the defined logic when the PPs experienced connectivity loss, it is unclear why the system selected the current OOC region rather than a more optimal one, especially given that mr1327 includes numerous regions within Japan. OOC mapping is expected to negatively impact client performance.
 * Could you please elaborate on the technical validity of the mapping system's behavior in this instance?
 * Are there better solutions to manage these intermittent PP packet loss events while maintaining optimal performance by keeping traffic within the country?
root_cause: Bad PP (lossy) caused out of country mapping impacting the performance .
creator: Yasuhiro Oyabu
mitigation_plan: Intermittent loss on the PP so no action.
longterm_mitigation: Better capability to mark a pingpoint bad when the loss % is high over few sec. AFAIK today until a PP is showing 100% loss to all ecors it isn't marked bad.

summary: H2 errors on Apple TV hostname vod-ak-aoc.tv.apple.com
description:
+*Problem Description*+

Apple is experiecing H2 errors on vod-ak-aoc.tv.apple.com
Akamai Edge is sending RST_STREAM(PROTOCOL_ERROR) + GOAWAY, and it's surfacing to the client as ECONNRESET.

 

*Sample Client Side Logs H2 Errors shared by Apple customer showing failure impact i.e RST_STREAM(PROTOCOL_ERROR) + GOAWAY*
{code:java}
================================================================================
PDT time | UTC time | source | event
--------------+--------------+---------+--------------------------------------------
11:26:30 | 18:26:30 | PROXY | conn #1837326283 stream 199 finished (preceding stream OK)
11:26:30 | 18:26:30 | PROXY | conn #1837326283 stream 201 device->Charles HEADERS END
full URL of failed request:
GET https://urldefense.com/v3/__https://vod-ak-aoc.tv.apple.com/itunes-assets/HLSAppleVideo221/v4/75/d9/64/75d964e1-4c88-2b93-a25e-c35f2f478d3d/P1237968130_A1487885571_audio_en_gr2768_mp4a-A6-59.m4s?accessKey=1779323143_3139691109741872657_*2Fitunes-assets*2FHLSAppleVideo221*2Fv4*2F75*2Fd9*2F64*2F75d964e1-4c88-2b93-a25e-c35f2f478d3d*2F_9Ri*2FHa79NW3pulXT4IMcNh9tFsF*2Fo*2FUwL*2BhsrERQXQCECHWRtJxI6L44L8jUbCGEcGbyV*2F7yogYdxKm0jpEXUArdm8bp2iuz*2FKvZXTR1voIBJ99Zb*2B4WNtfxLA2VAn*2FFxZxIk0thZZ58w5JJp*2Ba4Ug*3D*3D__;JSUlJSUlJSUlJSUlJSUlJSUlJQ!!GjvTz_vk!T-DAupgPcQisv8gIXd2USNps5fZ8j4aTZTS6-uS8EbtJASeFfyA0iyZR_z-27ENCGXpAYHeYXsGcVr0$
11:26:30 | 18:26:30 | PROXY | conn #1837326283 stream 201 Charles->edge HEADERS
11:26:30 | 18:26:30 | PROXY | conn #1837326283 stream 201 Charles->edge DATA size 0 END_STREAM
11:26:30 | 18:26:30 | PROXY | conn #1837326283 stream 201 edge->Charles *** RST_STREAM error_code=PROTOCOL_ERROR (0x1) ***
11:26:30 | 18:26:30 | PROXY | conn #1837326283 stream 201 edge->Charles *** GOAWAY last_stream_id=201, error_code=PROTOCOL_ERROR (0x1) ***
11:26:30 | 18:26:30 | PROXY | conn #1837326283 stream 201 Charles->device RST_STREAM forwarded
11:26:30 | 18:26:30 | PROXY | conn #1837326283 stream 201 Charles->device GOAWAY forwarded (last_stream_id=201, PROTOCOL_ERROR)
11:26:30 | 18:26:30 | PROXY | conn #1837326283 stream 201 finished
11:26:30 | 18:26:30 | PROXY | conn #1837326283 stream 203 device->Charles HEADERS END (race; arrived after server GOAWAY)
{code}
 

+*Review*+
For the Instances customer has shared so far, what we observe from corresponding ghost logs is *ERR_HTTP2_ERROR|connection:protocol_error*
The RST_STREAM in client side logs happens on stream 201 as shown in customer side logs, which typically corresponds to ghost log r line that has request number field ~ 100 on the same h2 connection.
Customer shared a python script, which mimics their Apple client side behavior (attached to JIRA  and in google drive link) that consistently reproduces the H2 issue. 
It appears this RST happens around this 100 request number on ghost logs likely due to this H2 setting number of 100---> [SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS(0x03):100]. 
The verification of this hypothesis of "SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS(0x03):100" was done on Staging of Apple delivery property where IAT/PS got approval to increase this setting to 200 i.e "SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS(0x03):200", and upon issue reproduction, the RST_STREAM error_code=PROTOCOL_ERROR (0x1)  happened on stream 401 i.e Request number 200 on ghost logs.

An important update from customer about their client side script behavior is  that when they change specific portions of client Python code, the H2 error no longer occurs.
In customers words, Please see below section of customers python code which reproduces the H2 error and the corresponding change on customer script which solves the H2 error
 
*" this is the part of script which reproduces the issue:*
 ** 
         *conn.send_headers(stream_id, headers, end_stream=False)*
         *conn.send_data(stream_id, b'', end_stream=True)*
 ** 
 ** 
*Instead of these two lines if you change it to below then problem will not happen*
*conn.send_headers(stream_id, headers, end_stream=True)*
 ** 
*since HEADER frame itself will have END_STREAM flag instead of an additional frame for END_STREAM"*
 
In response to Customer we have highlighted to them that the client behavior exhibited in their Script is atypical and unconventional for GET requests as GET requests should not contain a body, so the client behavior should be changed to not send a data frame (even if empty/zero size data frame) after sending headers. 
Below is an extract from RFC doc we shared with with Apple to show an example of what the RFC doc(RFC 9113 and  RFC 7450) illustrates for a H2 GET request semantics
*You can refer to section 8.8 of RFC 9113 doc*
[https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc9113/]
 
HTTP2 RFC example in RFC 9113  shows for GET no Data frame is sent as a HTTP GET request includes request header fields and no payload body.
You can compare that to the example of the POST request which has a Data frame as expected in same doc.

RFC description
   An HTTP GET request includes control data and a request header with
   no message content and is therefore transmitted as a single HEADERS
   frame, followed by zero or more CONTINUATION frames containing the
   serialized block of request header fields.  *The HEADERS frame in the*
   {*}following has both the END_HEADERS and END_STREAM flags set{*}; no
   CONTINUATION frames are sent.
{code:java}
     GET /resource HTTP/1.1           HEADERS
     Host: example.org          ==>     + END_STREAM
     Accept: image/jpeg                 + END_HEADERS
                                          :method = GET
                                          :scheme = https
                                          :authority = example.org
                                          :path = /resource
                                          host = example.org
                                          accept = image/jpeg
{code}
 
*We have asked customer to remove the data frame from their GET requests since this resolves the H2 protocol error, however, customer has pushed back indicating RFC does not explicitly prohibit Data Frame to be sent in GET requests and other CDN's accept their client behavior and don't return the H2 protocol error and Reset like Akamai.*
Additionally Apple customer indicated that they use a http proxy and it adds this additional data frame with END_STREAM. They mentioned, It’s beyond their(Apple) control on how this proxy handles HTTP2 frames.
And since it's RFC compliant, they won’t be able to request the proxy vendor to make a change for this especially since other CDN's allow this.
 
+*Testings/Issue Reproduction*+
I used Customers Python script as is(just modified the customer script abit to target to specific ghost IP) and  as was able to reprouce H2 errors and Reset in a PCAP file named ""ghostip-23.50.51.46_eth0-1780084094.pcap"
Please see below google drive  containing the SSL Key file and PCAP , that captured the H2 error, RST_STREAM(PROTOCOL_ERROR) + GOAWAY
[https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ztnVkSboU-gDeymCoK1PlefgHp2QQFzs?usp=sharingwe]
 
{*}Output from running the customer python script  corresponding to time Packet cpature file named "{*}"ghostip-23.50.51.46_eth0-1780084094.pcap" was run

 Pls See ending portion for crucial datapoints
{code:java}

Connecting to vod-ak-aoc.tv.apple.com via forced edge IP 23.50.51.46:443
TLS key logging enabled: ./python_h2_sslkeys.log
ALPN: h2

*Additional unencrypted pCAP attempt done by AKatec engineer is captured in this 2nd google drive link. Customer python script copy is also in this google drive link*
pcap and the customer script > [https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/12yXq23ZcX2kM-eYww7TrRPw7HlMtyQSj?usp=sharing] (2nd google drive link

Corresponding ghost logs from Akatec CSE are tracked on etherpad lines 613-716 [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11356076#L613] with H2 error around 100 request number
[msilesva@lsg-gss3 ~]$ zcat CP892080-202606042045-23.211.12.32-610-1780611903.gz
I *also wanted to highlight* that the Akatec PCAP titled "shareable_output.pcapng" does not for some reason capature the RST_STREAM(PROTOCOL_ERROR) + GOAWAY. However the corresponding ghost logs on etherpad lines 613-716 [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11356076#L613] capture the H2 errors ERR_HTTP2_ERROR|connection:protocol_error.

Below are also have the python script output logs from Akatec CSE where the error happened in stream 201:
{code:java}
[93] 200 stream=185 576197B 10338ms (active=4)

[95] 200 stream=189 576197B 8620ms (active=4)

[94] 200 stream=187 576197B 9521ms (active=4)

[96] 200 stream=191 576197B 8431ms (active=4)

[101] RST_STREAM stream=201 error_code=1 125ms

 

GOAWAY last_stream=201 error_code=1 additional_data=None

 [97] stream=193 was in-flight for 3899ms

 [98] stream=195 was in-flight for 2408ms

 [99] stream=197 was in-flight for 2399ms

 [100] stream=199 was in-flight for 2188ms

 [102] stream=203 was in-flight for 0ms
{code}
*Nevertheless,* PCAP file named ""ghostip-23.50.51.46_eth0-1780084094.pcap" in first google drive link containing captured the H2 error, RST_STREAM(PROTOCOL_ERROR) + GOAWAY
[https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ztnVkSboU-gDeymCoK1PlefgHp2QQFzs?usp=sharing]

Customer was not able to provide us a PCAP from their Apple client/proxy end , so the two PCAP we have are from Customer Python script runs done Internally by Akamai employees.

*Asks*
Need ERE review to determine if/ how we can resolve this H2 Protocol error on the Akamai Edge Platform side. Specifically, can ghost edge server be modified to accommodate this atypical/unconventional client side behavior, i.e accept an an additional "empty data frame" with END_STREAM flag set after the HEADERS frame was sent for a GET request.

In customers own words from their apple client behavior/script they believe 'Since only one stream is ever open, that means the slot for each finished GET isn't being released. It's perfectly reasonable for the server to assume a GET carries no body - that's the common case. The only issue is that this leads it to leave the stream's slot open and eventually drop the whole connection, rather than just treating the stream as closed once END_STREAM arrives.

The same proxy sends this exact framing to other CDNs and they handle it fine, so it'd be great if the server could simply release the stream on END_STREAM (even when it comes on an empty DATA frame) instead of letting it pile up to a GOAWAY."
executive_summary:
Apple is experiecing H2 errors on vod-ak-aoc.tv.apple.com
Akamai Edge is sending RST_STREAM(PROTOCOL_ERROR) + GOAWAY, and it's surfacing to the client as ECONNRESET.

summary: Oppo EU traffic review for potential instabilities
description:
Oppo’s EU traffic profile on the hostname “mdp-appconf-euex.heytapdl.com" (CP1947435)” started creating instabilities in the EU. This is very similar to what was observed under ERE-3037

This Jira has been created to analyze the traffic and work with other teams (IAT, PS, Engg. etc.) to track the issue and find a resolution.
root_cause: Daily consolidated batch hits from Oppo (and other) devices ~22:00 UTC
creator: Ankit Tripathi
mitigation_plan: Oppo's EU serial was changed to 6140 with mg32, and maps changed to API-X shards (api1-10)
longterm_mitigation: The customer will focus on smoothing the spikes and divert some traffic away from Akamai if needed. The product will be changed to API-X in next contract (after a few months).

summary: Downloads stalls and Failures for Redhat  (prod.cdn01.quay.io)
description:
*Problem* +*Description-*+ Customer (Redhat) Downloads from prod.cdn01.quay.io are stalling or failing mid-transfer. Behavior Started around Mid-march based on customer telemetry (see timeseries graph from customer attached) 
Customer has indicated to us that this seems to only happen when the customer uploads a new asset and tries to download it. Once it is in cache, the issue won't happen, per customer comments in quotes: "The issue happens when we are pulling content not cached by the CDN. The moment the Akamai edge node has the content in its cache, you don't hit this anymore. Every URL you use to reproduce the issue is valid only one time. The moment it's used, your edge node has the content in the cache and the issue no longer occurs.
For this reason my reproducer flow is to get new content pushed to S3 and immediately after request it from cdn01.quay.io - that way I am sure Akamai edge node needs to pull it from S3 because it was never cached before."

+*Review*+ 
*Ran customers script (attached) which they use to consistently reproduce the issue (Please note the customer script has temporary credentials that enables the reproduction workflow run which will be deactivated in 7 days i.e approx June 16).*

*Observations from Request ID '3eca9d20' where partial bytes were served to client with error* 
1. We see edge served partial bytes to clent and read error client with error ERR_READ_ERROR
2. Edge went forward to MCH(Primary Td0) for byte range 0-2097151 and got got ERR_READ_TIMEOUT after waiting 120 seconds

*Suggestions we have provided to IAT so far*
1. We have suggested to IAT to review the existing timeout settings, FA/QR settings. For example as shown in the request ID '3eca9d20' above, edge went to TD0(MCH) for byte range 0-2097151 and got ERR_READ_TIMEOUT after waiting 120 seconds(2 minutes) before QR kicked in and failed over to backup TD0 ch2f, to get the range bytes, this is a long timeout wait for a 2MB chunk, we recommeded PS should review the config metadata timeout settings and optimize FA/QR and Timeouts to kick in sooner/a bit more aggressively .

2. Secondly, the the ghost logs from running the customers Script to reproduce download failures and stalls show very close similarity with Parallel POC 2 problems tracked in the ERE confluence link below, for whihc the solution recommedation is to use the tag
{code:java}
<cache:poc2.make-masters-public-early>{code}

[https://collaborate.akamai.com/confluence/spaces/EPRE/pages/590360938/Parallel+POC2+problems]
Specifically the "ERR_READ_ERROR" shows to be relatd to Ghost JIRA GHOST-303
[https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/GHOST-303]I see as recently as a month or two ago, this tag was used on a similar customer escalation ERE JIRA ERE-3234 and seems to have provided positive results as disussed in JIRA 
*So we have recommended IAT to use this Tag above .*

[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11336518] (Akatec case etherpad where CSE captured few other download trace failures from May and early June)

*Asks to ERE*
1. Can you please review this JIRA to help determine if these two suggestions above would help resolve the download failures /stalls Redhat customer is experiencing? If not what should we use? 

2. I was looking internally to see if there are any recent POC realated rollouts in March and came acorss this one that went world deploy end of March (poc-reduce-round-trips).{*}Can you please review is the uptick in download failures is related to this Rollout in March or another rollout?{*} This POC tag was released (POC-RRT) was release globally at the end of March 2026
[https://gripe.akamai.com/rollout/subnet.W.rollout-poc-reduce-round-trips-client-side]
Please let us know how we can effectively resolve this Downloads issue for customer in Prod. IAT is working o deploying the two suggestions above in a customer Dev config (pending testing), however, we would like ERE review on this JIRA before deploying this tag to Prod and also ERE review on what could be causing this Uptick in Download Failures starting in March based on customer time series
executive_summary:
Customer (Redhat) Downloads from prod.cdn01.quay.io are stalling or failing mid-transfer. Behavior Started around Mid-march based on customer telemetry (see timeseries graph from custoemr attached)

Blocker: Waiting for Akatech to confirm the modification of forward ARL where certain key characters (like namespace and akamai-signature) are getting stripped off, which triggered ERR_POC_FWD_NOT_206 in the 'S' line
resolution_description: Akatech suggested workarounds, reducing the read timeouts and adding MPE seem to have worked as per customer response. Regarding the other POC errors, Akatech would investigate and reach out if seen any further errors/issues with POC2.
root_cause:
Multiple issues to be investigated:
1. Forward ARL Characters getting stripped off resulted in AUTH TOKEN error.
2. Edge to MCH conenction results in timeout

summary: EU VOD Origin traffic rising after primetime peak around ~20:00 UTC, Jun 11
description:
Disney reported Sev1 issue that EU VOD Origin traffic rising after primetime peak, 2xx increased and Cache Hit Ratio decreased starting around ~20:00 UTC, Jun 11.

[https://grafana.akam.ai/org224/dashboard/db/customer-dashboard-lighthouse?var-breakdown=customer&var-myview=Disney%20Plus%20VOD%20EU%20West%202%20-%20HD&var-agg=5&var-percentile=50&from=1781157776745&to=1781243953861]

!image-2026-06-12-12-29-07-791.png|width=819,height=423!

When we checked ACC, we could see config changes around ~13:30 UTC, Jun 11 and change was to allow traffic from CYPRUS without getting blocked. This change increased 304s around ~13:30 UTC and 200s spiked at ~20:00 UTC, which may not be correlating to the config change.

!image-2026-06-12-12-29-53-937.png|width=814,height=235!

[https://grafana.akam.ai/org224/dashboard/db/customer-dashboard-lighthouse?refresh=1m&var-breakdown=customer&var-myview=Disney%20Plus%20VOD%20EU%20West%202%20-%20HD&var-agg=5&var-percentile=50&panelId=96&fullscreen&from=1781157776745&to=1781243953861]

!image-2026-06-12-12-31-25-830.png|width=804,height=397!

!image-2026-06-12-12-31-55-143.png|width=802,height=395!

We collected logs before and during the increase in 200s and compared f lines on forwards to the origin from before 19:00 UTC the uptick in hits/bytes and at the peak 21:00 UTC.

We are seeing that requests are only going forward to the origin once per unique forward ARL for the 21:00 timeframe.

summary: Post recent changes Velvet Rope lacks NOCC facing alerts and notifications
description:
[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11458700]

 

*Background:*

Customer reported high surge of 403's, it was identified custom, 2.5Tbps VR bucket was hit:

bucket name: dstv2026
[https://grafana.akam.ai/org524/dashboard/db/bucket_viewer?var-bucketname=dstv2026&from=1781164958395&to=1781228103126]

 

 

*Investigation:*

Looks like there were plenty changes ~VR recently (~2025) including alerting systems.
[https://collaborate.akamai.com/confluence/spaces/NETWORKS/pages/1345957580/VelvetRope+Buckets+Operations]

 

Checking all alerts ~ the time matching VelvetRope keyword it was identified most of the new alerts created & deployed ~2025 having NOCC procedures linked are email only!.

 

Example:

[https://alerts.akamai.com/adms/detail.jsp?definition_id=31539]

has linked [https://www.nocc.akamai.com/alertproc/view.cgi?id=10994]

 

When an alert is email-only obviously it won't create any NOCC Facing ticket.

 

*Ask:*

Is it expected or miss from Mapping Strategy Engineering Team responsible for VelvetRope none of the customer facing teams or internal were informed post Velvet Rope limit breach and denials?

Could we optimize the same if a miss?

[https://collaborate.akamai.com/confluence/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=91751098&spaceKey=MAPENG&title=VelvetRope]


Please redirect accordingly to the Jira project if this Jira project is not the proper place.
resolution_description:
stop new label machines to use the old reporting column. 
update alert to use or statement on both alertable or currently alertable = 1 

process will be looked into
root_cause:
VR version 2.36 caused a change in query table velvetrope_bucket_limit which changed "alertable" to "currently_alertable" - the alert uses alertable 

when VR lead machine started using new version (6/9) - the condition alertable=1 would never be in use. which is why when dstv2026 denied , we were blind from an alerting POV and customer experienced 403 VR denys when they hit their VR bucket limit.
creator: Maciej Maciaszek
mitigation_plan:
stop new label machines to use the old reporting column. 
update alert to use or statement on both alertable or currently alertable = 1
longterm_mitigation: process on updating tables will be looked into

description:
Hi team,

Zee has secured last-minute rights for FIFA streaming in India. Below is the preliminary setup information. Could you please review the setup and let us know if any changes are needed.

[https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1tvHj4dQJkiMGpgLDDGyxbA0t8-D04ykP7ireQJ3i1Lw/edit?usp=sharing]

 ++ 

 2. Account & Core Setup

Account name: ZEE Entertainment Enterprises Limited
 
Event history: Small scale events - ILT20, no major events hosted by Zee.

Traffic estimates: 

25 Tbps [Jio - 16.5 Tbps, Non-jio - 8.5 Tbps] - reserved capacity discussion ongoing

Traffic type: HTTPS

CDN vendor: Akamai primary CDN [Multi CDN - traffic sent to other CDNs if Akamai has issues via GTM]
h2. 3. Stream & Encoding Details

Encoder and location: AWS Medialive, Mumbai [Streams have preferred regions set with PNI links]

Number of feeds per match: 4 

Languages: English, Hindi, Bengali and Malayalam

Stream ingest format: 

AVC with HLS [Encryption at transcoder]

Segment duration: 4 seconds

Bitrate ladder: 

Connected devices:

1080p low - 4 Mbps 

720p - 3 Mbps 

420p -1.5 Mbps 

Mobile devices: 

720 - 3mbps

280 - 700 Kbps

Average bitrate: 3-3.5 Mbps 

DVR: No archive

 
h2. 4. Delivery Architecture & Workflow

Delivery products: MSL 4 + AMD

Delivery model: 

Primary delivery: 100% SSAI delivery with Google DAI, segments from MSL 4. SSAI: Cohort based [cohorting based on user location - State]

Pristine: DAI origin pulls from the AMD config same as delivery.  

MCDN origin: AMD + MSL used as the origin for other CDNs

 

Workflow information:
 
||Workflow||Traffic Type||Tiers (Path)||
|Primary Delivery|SSAI Manifest|Edge [dscw16] → TD0 [chc1/chb4] → DAI Origin|
|Non-SSAI|Manifest & Segment|Edge [dscw16] → TD0 [chapacp/chapacf] → MSL Origin [ch498/ch970]|
|Pristine Pull|Manifest|Edge [dscw16] → TD0 [chapacp/chapacf] → MSL Origin [ch498/ch970]|
|MCDN Origin|Non-SSAI Manifest/Segments|Edge [dscw16] → TD0 [chapacp/chapacf] → MSL Origin [ch498/ch970]|

 
h3. Resiliency Strategies

DR strategies:
 # Move from SSAI to non-SSAI streams in case of DAI issues

Configuration information:

Primary Delivery & pristine: 

Configuration name: falcon-akhls.zee5.com

Hostnames used: falcon-akhls.zee5.com

Manifest caching: 

SSAI master - 6 hours

SSAI child - 2 seconds

h2. 5. Origin Mapping & Streams

Each MSL stream has separate origin

Separate origin for English and Hindi 

For more than 1 match a day, we are tracking for double header with 2 separate origins [1 for Hindi and 1 for English]. 

Stream and Origin mapping information: 

[+https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1bcSGF04WXQJ7q3ikEXpxErZVZEN0J77CwJN_yA55h_A/edit?gid=50748699#gid=50748699+]  

 
h2. 6. Resiliency & Optimization
h3. Optimizations
 * Geo block [Allowed only in India]

 * EPD Deny [with RCC EPD exceptions]

 * Token auth [Manifest manipulation for HLS - cookieless auth]

 * Failover mechanisms (TD, OS failovers)

 * TD failover from edge to chapacf on backup stream 

 * OS failover from TD to ch498 on backup stream


 * Cascading timeouts

|Default - client -4s, FBT - 4s, Read - 4s, connect - 2s|
|Edge - client 3s, FBT 3s, Read 3s|
|Edge peer - client 2.7s, read 2.7s, FBT 2.7s, connect - 500ms|
|Parent - client 2s, FBT 2s, Read 2s|

|OS - client 2.6s, FBT 2.6s, Read 2.6s|

h3. Map Details

Backup- chb4.akamai.net

Non SSAI: 

Primary- chapacp.akamai.net

Backup- chapacf.akamai.net

Failover OS map: ch970.akamai.net

 

Edge maps: Currently configured to AMD default maps.

Plan is to segregate manifest and segment traffic on different Product Maps. 

APIX Edge Maps to be used for manifest traffic and Event maps for Segment delivery.

 

Has the pdg-cap team been engaged for approval, and to create a separate VR bucket:  In progress.

Has log spinning been enabled for the relevant CP codes: No

Does the event include Ads : No 

 

Please help review and share your recommendations on the following key areas:
 * Optimal Maps for each workflow and if 2047 serial required for edge map as manifest and segments are on same hostname.

Please feel free to reach out if you need any further details.

summary: Disney VPF Spikes on ASN 3292
description:
CPcode 927022
EU-NORTH-1 Performance Degradation | ASN 3292
[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11447405_ER|https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11447405_ERE]

Customer has been reporting VPF spikes over the past two weeks. The etherpad has detailed examples from the 9th, 10th, and 11th of what we are seeing on Akamai during our investigation. 

All three examples we are seeing clients connected to the same ASN 3292. All clients logging VPFs are connected to one region with low throughput <5000mbs (observable in Hats v3). 
In the etherpad we have confirmed that the client is connected to an edge server that rolls with roll *code 256* and "{*}FATAL: Received Segment Violation{*}" in the cache logs.
We aren't seeing any evidence of hight resource utilization or RHM spikes.


From June 9th Client logged a VPF when connected to Edge region 45985 (95.166.120.7) 
There were a gap in requests from this client between 2026/06/09-09:55:55 - 2026/06/09-09:59:52
The last request was to edge server 95.166.120.7 at 09:55:55 and the next request was to edge server 95.166.120.13 at 09:59:52. (~4 minute delta)
Between this time the player logs a VPF on the client side and doesn't log an error on Akamai. 
During this time there are no signs that the region is overloaded
[https://lg.netarch.akamai.com/cgi-bin/loadgraphs?period=start1780986840end1781002980&region=45985&network=A&maprule=&display=total&ymax=&utcoffset=-4]

We see there is low throughput on the region 
[https://grafana-hats2-epremo.akamai.com/d/e20b1f9b-85f2-4323-8590-ab10e9778885/hats-v3?orgId=1&var-load=yes&var-breakdown=srv_region&var-maprule=-&var-destination=-&var-cpcode=927022&var-cache_hit=-&var-service=W&var-region_country=DK&var-region_continent=-&var-region=-&var-client_country=DK&var-client_continent=-&var-child=-&var-client_asnum=3292&var-client_asname=-&var-client_asaccount=-&var-client_geo_id=-&var-proto=-&var-connection_type=-&var-ipv=-&var-tput=5000&var-rtt=50&var-size=500&var-topn=1-10&var-resolution=10min&var-hours=-&var-title=breakdown%3Dsrv_region%20%2F%20service%3DW%20%2F%20cpcode%3D927022%20%2F%20region_country%3DDK%20%2F%20client_asnum%3D3292%20%2F%20client_country%3DDK&var-title_no_breakdown=service%3DW%20%2F%20cpcode%3D927022%20%2F%20region_country%3DDK%20%2F%20client_asnum%3D3292%20%2F%20client_country%3DDK&from=1780963200000&to=1781049599000&viewPanel=37]
Session analysis for client request pattern- line 945 (in yellow) is the gap in hits and when the VPF occurs. 
[https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1vHqC2dTIXv2mwrmwZQbvnleeCRsJGbRuFMWv9_StjU8/edit?gid=1137132177#gid=1137132177]

From Mapper it looks like the traffic dropped immediately which could indicate clients may not be honoring the DNS TTLs. 

[https://mapper.akamai.com/dnsp/ghost-machine/#from%3D1781202300000%26to%3D1781288700000%26dataFrom%3D1781288698000%26useGMTTime%3Dtrue%26timeRange%3D%7B%22min%22%3A1781202300000%2C%22max%22%3A1781220287003.61%7D%26regionId%3D49255%26ghostIp%3D95.166.123.17%26service%3DW%26]

Ask for ERE:
Since this is all happening on one ASN we have also taken this up with the NOCC. However since we are seeing ghost rolls can ERE please review and provide insight on what could be the cause and why it is impacting the end clients in this way?
resolution_description: Long term fix will be pursued based on further discovery in GHOST-7943
root_cause:
Race condition. Ghostmon will not clear SFLAG 256 until isredirecting.W.txt is removed. On affected machines, isredirecting.W.txt was being created after ghostReady. 

This is the reverse of the expected sequence. Ideally, during a ghost roll, the redirect feature is triggered, resulting in the creation of isredirecting.W.txt and causing ghost to enter the draining state. Ghost then starts coming back up, at which point ghostReady is created. Once ghost is fully up , isredirecting.W.txt is deleted.
creator: Tyler Deary
mitigation_plan: Restart Ghost. Alert in place to identify machines with suspendflag 256 for extended period.
longterm_mitigation: Fix Ghost bug based on further discovery in GHOST-7943

Is it related to ERE-3336 but Jio is using Non MCH maps
resolution_description:
Having the same value for http.client-timeout, http.first-byte-timeout, and http.read can mask the actual failure condition, as client-timeout starts first and may be the timeout that is hit.
 
Consider configuring the g2g phase-specific timeouts lower than client-timeout.
http.client-timeout
http.first-byte-timeout
http.read
root_cause:
All the values for read/fbt/connect are the same. As the client-timeout timer starts first, this resulted in a client-timeout. When the client-timeout is triggered, the fail-action is taken and the forward connection is terminated without waiting for the response from the origin.

Working as expected. Successful response on FailAction; Negative caching amplified the impact.

mitigation_plan: To work with EA. Recommended to review the cascading timeout values.
longterm_mitigation: N/A

summary: Consistent Error Spikes in HTTP 5xx during UFC 250 for CBS
description:
The customer reported sporadic spikes in 5xx (503 and 504) http responses throughout the night. These spikes occurred consistently on Akamai and root cause did not point to a consistent region within the Akamai workflow as the cause of the issue. 

 

Drilling down on the spikes we could consistently see:
 * Edge failing to both the primary td0, the alt td0 (ch2f)
 * Corresponding smaller spikes to origin (largely AWS)

 

We drilled down on a spike early in the event. However, it was pretty consistent throughout the event time-line


!Screenshot 2026-06-15 at 9.23.03 PM.jpg|width=665,height=222!

*!09_05_24.jpg|width=665,height=324!*

*Sample trace:*

[https://crawly-aps.akamai.com/#!/?poll-id=7243f16f_23.62.38.30_1781486553.162_False_False] 

Etherpad: [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/ms_06_15_26]

 

The trace shows that the edge went forward to:
 # [mch-ff-lo.akasrg.akamai.com|http://mch-ff-lo.akasrg.akamai.com/] where it logged a 0xx CONNECT_TIMEOUT error triggering a retry
 # The retry attempt went forward to ch2f where it logged a ERR_FWD_SSL_HANDSHAKE|err_conn_strict_cert:ssl0 error
 # Edge then, as expected goes forward to [propebe5deb2-akamai.airspace-origin.cbsivideo.com|http://propebe5deb2-akamai.airspace-origin.cbsivideo.com/] which resolves AWS

Dissecting it further we can see that the mch server suffered a large spike in flitload that caused ghost to self suspend

summary: ERR_GZIP 11 error increase
description:
*Background:*

Customer suspects increase of ERR_GZIP|11 since last month is responsible for portion of the rebuffering.

 

*Investigation:*

[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11473645]

Looks like the known scenario of compression racing condition potentially suspected to be amplified by recent rollout.
 * Origin is serving the manifest in GZIP compressed form in chunks through CTE (Chunked Transfer Encoding) without content-length.
 * Edge is supposed to run manifest manipulation and needs to decompress the object for that purpose
 * Edge needs to compress the object again to satisfy the client Accept Encoding.

summary: High Latency Spike Investigation: abnormal flits load and unusual traffic patterns
description:
*1. Issue Summary*

Customer ‘Coupang Co.,Ltd.’ reported experiencing significant latency spikes between 2026.06.14 08:20 ~ 13:00 UTC. During this time frame, the transfer time of egress and child edge turnaround time increased across almost all regions. Additionally, a spike in 5xx errors was observed correlating with this timeframe.
!dashboard.png|width=556,height=292!

*2. Observed Symptoms & Log Analysis Findings*

Akatec has conducted an initial log analysis (focusing on the 5xx spike window: 10:55 ~ 11:05 UTC) and observed the following:

-. Abnormal flit load & traffic patterns:

Despite the regions' FOM levels not being significantly high, the flit load was higher than the flit soft cap (almost hitting the hard cap).

The traffic patterns for the apix map and the South Korean regions included in it appeared slightly different from previous historical patterns.

-. Parent region degradation:

A spike was observed in child region r51456, but all requests were forwarded to parent r30823. The parent r30823 responded with '0', and some servers in this parent region showed intermittent high flit and CPU usage.

[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11467896]    line 363~750.

description:
*Issue summarry:* 

Since May 11th, NTT Docomo (EW ID: 92040) has experienced an increase in EdgeWorkers Wall timeout errors (ERR_METADATA_APPLY_FAILURE) and client-side 500 errors, which correlate with an overall traffic increase and intermittent high turnaround times (>6s).

Issue has been escalated to EW EWDEVESC-329  and NOCC [B-W-1KEPK1P|https://issues.deploy.akamai.com/cgi-bin/view.cgi?issue_id=B-W-1KEPK1P]  but current investigation shows that there is no issue from EW nor in the region(45318)
{quote}Although traffic spikes appear to coincide with some of the events, our analysis does not suggest a regional capacity issue.

...

If it hasn't recurred and it's not reproducible, there's probably not much they can do to help at this point, but if further investigation is needed, you should involve ERE to determine why the redirect isn't going to the correct IP.
{quote}
