summary: {F-CS-11474920} DPM UI does not list some EHNs
description:
*ISSUE:*

KBC Group NV reported not being able to add EHNs to Delivery Policy as they are not showing up in the list.

Account: KBC Group NV
Delivery Policy: delivery-oi-EU
Contract: G-2M7PXR5

Following hosts can't be added to the delivery-oi-EU policy:

Edge Hostname ||| Property
-------------------------------------------------
[businessdashboard-a.cbc.be.edgekey.net|https://businessdashboard-a.cbc.be.edgekey.net/] ||| [businessdashboard-a.kbc.be|https://businessdashboard-a.kbc.be/]
[documentsigning.kbcbrussels.be.edgekey.net|https://documentsigning.kbcbrussels.be.edgekey.net/] ||| [documentsigning.kbc.be|https://documentsigning.kbc.be/]
[investments.kbc.be.edgekey.net|https://investments.kbc.be.edgekey.net/] ||| [investments.kbc.be|https://investments.kbc.be/]
[investments.kbcbrussels.be.edgekey.net|https://investments.kbcbrussels.be.edgekey.net/] ||| [investments.kbcbrussels.be|https://investments.kbcbrussels.be/]
[warrant.esop.kbc.be.edgekey.net|https://warrant.esop.kbc.be.edgekey.net/] ||| [warrant.esop.kbc.be|https://warrant.esop.kbc.be/]

 

 

*CHEKCS:*

I ran some checks for example EHN *businessdashboard-a.cbc.be.edgekey.net* : 

It does not show up on the list in DPM UI because the API did not return it in the response. I see the same when I call the OPEN endpoint of DPM API - this EHN is not returned:
{code:java}
$  http --auth-type edgegrid -a default: GET :'/delivery-policy-manager/v1/edge-hostnames?contractId=G-2M7PXR5&accountSwitchKey=AANA-4EEU2F:1-5G3LB' | jq -c ".edgeHostnames[]" | grep "businessdashboard-a.cbc.be" | wc -l
       0 {code}
 

All in all, DPM OPEN API only returns 1028 EHNs, but in the Contract tool we see there should be 1042 in total (see screenshot)
{code:java}
$  http --auth-type edgegrid -a default: GET :'/delivery-policy-manager/v1/edge-hostnames?contractId=G-2M7PXR5&accountSwitchKey=AANA-4EEU2F:1-5G3LB' | jq -c ".edgeHostnames[]" | wc -l    1028 {code}
 

As per docs, DMP API is supposed to [fetch the EHN data from HAPI.|https://collaborate.akamai.com/confluence/spaces/DPPE/pages/756268034/Policy+Manager+-+API+Design#PolicyManagerAPIDesign-EdgeHostnamesAPI] When I trace my DMP call in Portalsplunk, I do see it gets referred to HAPI. And logs say HAPI returned 1042 EHNs (see screenshot) - so why does DPM API only return 1028?

[https://portalsplunk.akamai.com/en-GB/app/Portal/search?sid=1781856252.2235094_9CD559D9-47CE-46AF-AC48-84E91004AECF]

 

When I check manually against HAPI, it does return this EHN.
So does the EHN endpoint of PAPI:
{code:java}
 $  http --auth-type edgegrid -a default: GET :'/hapi/v1/edge-hostnames?accountSwitchKey=AANA-4EEU2F:1-5G3LB' | jq -c ".edgeHostnames[]" | grep "businessdashboard-a.cbc.be" | jq "."{  "chinaCdn": {    "isChinaCdn": false  },  "comments": "Created by Property-Manager/PAPI on Wed Sep 09 10:05:49 GMT 2020",  "dnsZone": "edgekey.net",  "edgeHostnameId": 4654615,  "ipVersionBehavior": "IPV4",  "map": "e;b.akamaiedge.net",  "productId": "DSA",  "recordName": "businessdashboard-a.cbc.be",  "securityType": "ENHANCED-TLS",  "dnsSerial": 209347,  "slotNumber": 209347,  "ttl": 300,  "useDefaultMap": false,  "useDefaultTtl": false} {code}
 
{code:java}
$  http --auth-type edgegrid -a default: GET :'/papi/v1/hostnames?accountSwitchKey=AANA-4EEU2F:1-5G3LB' | jq -c ".hostnames.items[]" | grep "businessdashboard-a.cbc.be" | jq "."{  "cnameFrom": "businessdashboard-a.cbc.be",  "stagingEdgeHostnameId": "ehn_4654615",  "stagingCertType": "CPS_MANAGED",  "stagingCnameTo": "businessdashboard-a.cbc.be.edgekey.net",  "contractId": "ctr_G-2M7PXR5",  "groupId": "grp_172862",  "propertyId": "prp_623983",  "propertyName": "businessdashboard-a.kbc.be",  "propertyType": "TRADITIONAL",  "stagingProductId": "prd_Site_Accel",  "latestVersion": 27}{  "cnameFrom": "businessdashboard-a.cbc.be",  "productionEdgeHostnameId": "ehn_4654615",  "productionCertType": "CPS_MANAGED",  "productionCnameTo": "businessdashboard-a.cbc.be.edgekey.net",  "contractId": "ctr_G-2M7PXR5",  "groupId": "grp_172862",  "propertyId": "prp_623983",  "propertyName": "businessdashboard-a.kbc.be",  "propertyType": "TRADITIONAL",  "productionProductId": "prd_Site_Accel",  "latestVersion": 27} {code}
 

AkaTec and PS checked the missing EHNs and see no valid reason for them to be missing from DPM. Multiple other EHNs with the same setup (contract, group, product, slot, network, etc) _are_ visible in DPM and are assigned to policies.

Docs say that DSA is not supported by DPM, but that seems to be outdated info? Since we see multiple DSA EHNs listed by DMP, many of them having a policy assigned.

 

Etherpad with all the checks:

[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11474920]

 

*ASK:*

Please help us fix so that DPM UI lists all the expected EHNs and we can configure policy for them.

Escalating to ERE as this is our documented escalation path for everything DPM.
resolution_description: Customer can edits affected EHNs via Property Manager and explicitly changes map setting to 'Product Default Map', which updates useDefaultMap flag to true without altering actual traffic routing.
root_cause: EHNs with useDefaultMap: false are filtered by DPM API despite having valid map configurations. HAPI and PAPI return these EHNs correctly, but DPM applies additional validation that excludes EHNs where backend flag does not match default expectation for the product.
creator: Marta Siemczonek
mitigation_plan: Customer edits affected EHNs via Property Manager and explicitly changes map setting to 'Product Default Map', which updates useDefaultMap flag to true without altering actual traffic routing.
longterm_mitigation: The DPM and HAPI development teams have been looped in via email thread to track the permanent code-level fix for this validation edge case.

summary: Higher XFER latency in TW vs KR
description:
Hello GPO

Coupang reported that XFER latency for slow requests is way higher in TW  than latency in KR.

 

While the hit count is less than 1/3rd in TW and so are the flits hovering at 45%. (lines#1235/1250)

[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11460874] line#1201 onwards

The 99%tile value is 3.4sec XFER latency for TW - meaning that 1% of hits took longer than 3.5sec. (line 1265)

The 99%tile for KR is 1.13 sec (line#1272)

Obj sizes for TW and KR are similar (lines#1316/1356)

Content types for TW and KR are also similar (lines#1397/1415)

Both TW and KR exhibit high AS diversity for client IPs so it does not look like a localised ISP issue (line#1480)

No OOC mapping is seen for both countries (lines#1467)

Looks like a general issue with TW ISPs and we  understand that variations in ISP performance do exist and that it can be up or down in some regions - But you can dig deeper and find a suitable explanation that is not too generalized/vague and customer friendly, that would help.

 

Thanks

 

Thanks

summary: ZEE – Origin Shield 403 ACCESS_DENIED Errors During FIFA Event Due to Failover-Induced Origin Shield Saturation
description:
*Issue Overview*

During the FIFA event on {*}21 June at 20:12–20:13 UTC{*}, a spike in ingest errors on stream *2125516* triggered failover behavior associated with the ongoing XBC issue (SI-00023859)
[https://akamai.lightning.force.com/lightning/r/SC_SI_Service_Incident__c/aXea70000000Rg9CAE/view]

Immediately following the ingest error spike, a significant increase in *403 ACCESS_DENIED|vr* errors was observed originating from the Origin Shield.

*Findings :*
 * VR leader logs indicate requests were denied by Origin Shield bucket {*}OriginShield_mslo50Gbps{*}.

 * The affected traffic maps to {*}CP Code 2023003 (ZEE Origin Shield){*}.

 * Analysis shows that failover logic rewrote requests to backup stream URLs by appending the *"-b"* suffix.

 * Requests containing *2125511-b* surged from approximately 8K requests/minute to nearly {*}975K requests in a single minute{*}, overwhelming the Origin Shield VR.

 * Additional analysis shows the requests were initiated at the Edge and routed through *chapacf* via configured failover/path-rewrite logic.

 * The resulting traffic spike exceeded Origin Shield capacity, leading to *403 ACCESS_DENIED* responses.

*Key Questions*

1. Did MPE fail to collapse requests as expected during failover?

2. Should failover logic be adjusted to prevent large Origin Shield traffic spikes?

3. Can the CP be migrated to a larger Origin Shield VR to improve resilience during future failover events?

*Evidence*
 * 
 ** Request spike observed at 20:12 UTC:

 * 
 ** 
 *** 20:10 – 7,737 requests

 * 
 ** 
 *** 20:11 – 8,549 requests

 * 
 ** 
 *** 20:12 – 975,119 requests

 * 
 ** 
 *** 20:13 – 105,697 requests

 * 
 ** 
 *** 20:14 – 7,711 requests

 * 
 ** Approximately 701K requests were observed being routed via *rmap=chapacf* during the event.

Reference etherpad : [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/ms_06_21_26_vr]

+*Note :*+ 

While there is ongoing impact to BAU customers, the impact is expected to be high starting peak time in India (in approx 6 hours) with Women's T20 match scheduled at 6:30 pm IST (13:00 UTC) followed by FIFA match for the day.
resolution_description: Given the current metadata settings are triggering the FA irrespective of whether 404 is local cache hit or forward response, it is required to review and get it corrected as retrying on negative cache hit defies its purpose.
root_cause: Retrying back-up stream on Alternate path for a negative cache hit lead to higher number of FA requests when primary. stream fails - based on the current metadata design.
creator: Rashida Pathan
mitigation_plan: Given the current metadata settings are triggering the FA irrespective of whether 404 is local cache hit or forward response, it is required to review and get it corrected as retrying on negative cache hit defies its purpose.
longterm_mitigation: NA

summary: Reduce FOM on r25990
description:
Hello GPO

Customer reported 5xx errors for hostnames: login.mynt.xyz and login-ios.mynt.xyz. As the affected URL was the login endpoint, users were unable to access other services during the issue occurrence.

Error timeframe:
From 2026-06-19T08:55 to 2026-06-19T09:05

- The dip in Origin traffic was confirmed to be caused due Akamai Edge-Parent traffic issue.
- There were no issues observed in connectivity towards origin itself.
- We observed SSL handshake failures and timeouts *towards a parent region: 25990* {*}from various child regions{*}, resulting in 504 and 503 errors being served to end users.
- The cache logs for region confirm the flit to be reaching upwards of 100% flit utilisation

- There was a spike in traffic for maprule 7406 / serial 2050 , which overloaded all of the machines in the region and resulted in self suspensions. - No FOM reduction has been done on this region yet

Can we implement FOM on r25990 which was causing high flit usage as a mitigation?

summary: SBS || High number of 403s due to cloud-wrapper-summed-flits-au VR limit exceeding threshold
resolution_description: Since VR limit can't be increased without additional machines being deployed, it is required to make sure the CW demand doesn't exceed the limit for the event.
root_cause: IN AU, flit headroom of 60–64Gf available for event traffic in CW w.r.t the VR limit 109Gf. Since CW demand pushed more than the VR limit by SBS event, denials happened.
creator: Aparna Pathak

summary: Stale content served despite successful purge and prior new content delivery
description:
Customer reported an issue where stale content was served even after multiple purges were completed. ddc logs indicate that the ghost server (23.201.35.149) successfully served the new content, but paradoxically returned stale content to a client shortly afterward from the same ghost server.

!image-2026-06-29-14-00-38-271.png|width=575,height=380!
h3. *Investigation Findings*
 * *Purge History:* 8 purges were executed during the reported issue time.

 * *Content Details:* The JSON file has a 1-hour cache TTL.

 ** New content size: 47 bytes

 ** Stale content size: 42 bytes

 * *Log Analysis (Ghost Logs):*

 ** New content (47 bytes) was served by edge {{23.201.35.149}} at 06/18 00:41:57 UTC.

 ** Stale content (42 bytes) was served by the _same_ edge at 06/18 00:42:13 UTC.

 ** The issue appears isolated to client IP {{{}112.175.187.51{}}}.

 ** The problematic requests are associated with a global store entry: {{{}mtse=g|219754505{}}}.

 * *Server Health:* Checked edge {{23.201.35.149}} and found no abnormalities. Cache logs also showed no issues.

 * *Missing Logs:* Attempted to collect Ghost activity and jetsagent logs on 6/19, but they were no longer available for collection.

*Questions*

1. How is it possible for an edge server to return stale content after it has already cached and served the new content?

2. How does the global store entry (mtse=g|219754505) relate to this stale content behavior? 

[https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11487306] has more information on the issue.
creator: Dimitris Kim

summary: Pre-Spread request for r23481
description:
Hello GPO

The client, Coupang Co., Ltd., reported that 503 errors occurred on the [merchant-api.coupangeats.com|https://merchant-api.coupangeats.com/] service.
The root cause was that when requests were forwarded to the parent, some parent servers experienced high load, triggering a self-suspension.
Consequently, the parent failed to respond properly, resulting in 503 errors being returned to the client.
The high load on the parent occurred because traffic for [api.coupangeats.com|https://api.coupangeats.com/] and [delivery.coupangeats.com|https://delivery.coupangeats.com/]—which share the same slot 3999 as [merchant-api.coupangeats.com|https://merchant-api.coupangeats.com/]—surged into those specific servers.
Since this issue is recurring rather than a one-off event, is it possible to apply pre-spreading to slot 3999? Alternately, are there any other methods to distribute the load in order to prevent self-suspension?

As per NOCC#B-W-1KZRPBR
{noformat}
Flits are high, but no drop seen. FOM value is 65%.  dnsp mapper view shows many machines in suspended state, that's due to install. All suspended machines belong to IG9.
The issue was caused by overload. The parent IPs self-suspended due to high FLIT utilization. A large volume of requests to the hostname coupangeats.com overloaded the parent machines,which resulted in the observed impact.

Thanks

summary: WDR - Multiple rebuffering spikes during FIFA WC matches : Germany vs Ecuador and South Africa vs Canada games on Jun 28th, 2026
description:
WDR Westdeutscher Rundfunk reported multiple rebuffering spikes (refer to the screenshot attached to the case) from 20:40 to 23:00 CEST, 28th Jun during FIFA WC matches

*Spike Timeframes in CEST and GMT :*

20:40 CEST (18:40GMT)
21:10 CEST (19:10 GMT)
21:30 CEST (19:30 GMT)
21:50 CEST (19:50 GMT)
22:00 CEST (20:00 GMT)
22:20 CEST (20:20 GMT)
22:30 CEST (20:30 GMT)
23:00 CEST (21:00 GMT)

*CPCodes:*
1622042 — Das Erste DASH daserste-live.ard-mcdn.de
1622043 — Das Erste HLS daserste-live.ard-mcdn.de (1/3)

*Summary:*
 * Upon reviewing the logs, we observed a corresponding spike in HTTP error 0 with First Byte Timeout(FBT) errors and SSL timeouts on forward requests during the each rebuffering timeframe.
 * Spike in forward timeouts was matching with 200 (FBT and SSL timeouts) and high response times at the delivery.
 * The FBT errors were primarily observed on peer requests. Although there was a clear spike in FBT, the affected regions were widely distributed, and none of the top regions showed any significant health issues.
 * r52250:FABRIC-FRA43c, r51800:FABRIC-BERy, r42761:SDN-HAMg were among the top regions reporting FBT errors observed during multiple rebuffering spikes; however, the FBT issues were not isolated only to these regions and were observed across multiple other regions.
 * Further analysis of the FBT errors showed that the top region cache logs had “Detected DEAD Sibling” errors around the time of the issue.
 * The First byte analysis here showed that the majority of the failures occurred on ICP peer requests, with no indication of region or machine-level issues. No alerts were triggered that pointed to a specific region or server experiencing an issue.

 * For the SSL timeout errors, no single region stood out as a common source.
 * Upon checking the cache logs for SSL timeouts regions revealed high FLIT utilisation matching the issue timeframe.
 *  We created NOCC tix for regions r46387:DECIX-FRA1a (NOCC Case#[ B-W-1MF1FST)|https://issues.deploy.akamai.com/cgi-bin/view.cgi?issue_id=B-W-1MF1FST] and  [r37431:FABRIC-FRAh] (NOCC Case# [B-W-1MGX2Z7|https://issues.deploy.akamai.com/cgi-bin/view.cgi?issue_id=B-W-1MGX2Z7])  for the spikes of SSL Timeout errors noticed at ~21:50 CEST and ~22:00 CEST.
NOCC Responses:
B-W-1MF1FST - Loadgraph shows issues with flits in the region spike in traffic from MR22 & MR2907. From map.akamai, high flits are for MR22, and there is a spike for MR22 & MR2907 starting June 27th.
B-W-1MGX2Z7 - Traffic looks fine during the timeframe mentioned, Traffic almost reaching soft cap, but no dips seen in flits. 
(Here from cache logs we noticed high flits, we have followed up with NOCC again to investigate further)

*Further Analysis on FBT:* **

To investigate further, we traced MTSE-latched requests across multiple reported timeframes, with the following observations:
 * 18:40–18:45 UTC (~20:40 CEST): The traced MTSE-latched requests traversed multiple ICP peers before ultimately routing to region 52167 had logged status code 0 with high SSL overhead. This explains the multiple ICP peer requests observed in the logs. From load graph it clearly is a flit intensive region and has NO_SSL_KEYS errors
[https://lg.netarch.akamai.com/cgi-bin/loadgraphs?period=start1782669180end1782681480&region=52167&network=W&maprule=&display=maprule&ymax=&utcoffset=-6]
 * ~19:30 UTC (~21:30 CEST): Another set of traced MTSE-latched requests again routed to region 52167  had logged status code 0, matching the region previously identified during the SSL timeout analysis.
 * ~19:10 UTC (~21:10 CEST): The traced MTSE thread ultimately routed to region r37796:FABRIC-FRA2c  had logged status code 0, which also exhibited high flit utilization during the issue window and has NO_SSL_KEYS  errors.

 * ~19:30 UTC (~21:30 CEST): A separate traced MTSE thread ultimately routed to region r39109:FABRIC-FRA2l  had logged status code 0 , another FLIT-intensive region.
 * ~ 20:00 UTC (22:00 CEST) : MTSE thread showed SSL timeouts from region r37431:FABRIC-FRAh (Flagged to NOCC under B-W-1MGX2Z7)

All the MTSE traces are added here - [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11531875_FA_Traces]

So far, all the MTSE-latched requests we traced have ended up routing to flit-intensive regions. While the initial FBT analysis did not point to any specific region- or machine-level issue, the MTSE traces show a consistent pattern, with the affected requests routing to regions 52167, 37796, 39109 and 37431 all of which were experiencing high flit utilization during the reported timeframes.

Etherpad with overall logs: [https://etherpad.akam.ai/p/F-CS-11531875]

*Ask:* Since customer experienced multiple rebuffering spikes, we would like to understand what immediate mitigation measures should be implemented for the upcoming matches to minimize the impact.
creator: Aparna Pathak

summary: {F-CS-10868116} ERE-3374 – Follow-up on X-Akamai-Edgescape Header Handling
description:
Here is the continuation of the discussion from https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/ERE-3374. The IAT explained our position on the reported issue to the customer, but the customer disagreed with our stance and insisted on changing the behavior.

Can you please review the following arguments from both the customer and the IAT and let us know your thoughts?
{quote}This is to follow up on ERE-3374 for our gaming customer, Cygames. Right now, if a malicious user sends a fake X-Akamai-Edgescape header in a non-Tiered configuration, Akamai completely deletes the header instead of sending the correct one.

We need to emphasize that for a gaming company, this behavior is a critical risk because it directly causes game bugs for players. The origin game server reads the country code from this header to change game features. If the header is completely missing, the game code will experience unexpected behavior, which immediately breaks the game experience for users. In the worst-case scenario, this could lead to critical system failures or allow bad users to intentionally trigger bugs in the game application. Also, they save this country data with player logs into their database for business analysis, so missing headers ruin their data integrity.

Therefore, our first and highest priority is to ask the engineering team to fix this core bug. Even if this issue only happens with fake client headers, it triggers a critical application failure in production, so Akamai must always send the correct EdgeScape header to the origin to protect the game system.

If fixing the code is absolutely impossible because the priority is too low, please create guardrails for users. First, we need a UI warning message in Property Manager when Content Targeting is enabled without a Modify Incoming Request Header behavior to delete the incoming header. Second, we need a note in the official Techdocs to explain this behavior and share the workaround, so other customers will not face the same dangerous game bugs.

Please review this issue and let us know if we can fix the code first.
{quote}
creator: Yasuhiro Oyabu

summary: Intermittent 2MB Object Truncation on us.download.nvidia.com
description:
*Issue summary:* 

NVIDIA is experiencing intermittent download truncations of large objects at exactly 2 MiB, which directly correlates with the configured 2 MiB Partial Object Caching (POC) fragment size. Edge server cache logs reveal an internal exception (basic_string::_M_construct null not valid) triggered intermittently. Customer is not sure when the issue started to happen but there was no change from customer's side and there are several URLs impacted.

*Akatec observations:*

+ Akatec previously recommended issuing a purge. The customer performed the purge but continues to observe the issue for the URL: https://us.download.nvidia.com/Windows/581.15/581.15-desktop-win10-win11-64bit-international-dch-whql.exe.

+ Logs show a 200 response code for the above URL and the reported client IPs. The content length is listed as 895,581,672 bytes, but the actual content size delivered is 2,097,152 bytes. We observe range requests on the forward side with a 206 status code, but the Edge is logging truncated data with a 200 status code (starting at line 499).

+ Cache manager review for the instance with a 2,097,152-byte content size shows only one cached public fragment (line 519).

+ Not all cases but sometimes there is cache log something like "ConnStateData::process(): Exception caught - basic_string::_M_construct null not valid"

+ So far there is no specific error message in the ghost ddc logs and it happens intermittently even on the same ghost server.

summary: Disney HIVE clients experiencing VPFs potentially due to corrupt playlist.
description:
Account Name : Disney Streaming Services

CPCODE : 1638006

 

Disney reported a pair of spikes in VPFs as soon as traffic began to pick up during their F1 streams on Sunday 7/5/26 at 14:56 UTC and then again at 11:14 UTC. Per Disney the issues were isolated to their “Hive” player devices which have been an issue for Akamai. After these VPF spikes Disney removed the device’s traffic off Akamai for the remainder of the event. We drilled down on the spikes and observed no visible presence of edge errors that would help explain the issue. Furthermore, previous behaviors such as increased 111 and FIRST_BYTE_TIMEOUT responses from the midgress which have caused previous VPF issues for these same devices.

 

What we could see consistently in the client side logs is that the segments are requested out of order briefly before the client session stops.

 

Here the video segment numbers jump from timestamp 14:56:02 to 14:55:52, after which the client re-requests segment 
{code:java}
clt1/va02/disneyplus/event/2026/07/05/Formula_1_Carrera_GP_Gran_20260705_1783247413021/cmaf-cenc-ctr-7000K/186/14/56/02_914.mp4{code}
!Screenshot 2026-07-07 at 6.07.34 AM.jpg|width=665,height=229!

*For the same session we see similar behavior on the audio stream we see that the timestamps jump backward from 14:56:02 - 14:55:52, and re-request segment:* 
{code:java}
clt1/va02/disneyplus/event/2026/07/05/Formula_1_Carrera_GP_Gran_20260705_1783247413021/audio-1-128K/186/14/55/52_917.mp4a{code}
The rest line below notes where there is a gap of over 60 seconds between new requests followed by the client restarting the stream, which would have been the Video Playback Failure.

*!Screenshot 2026-07-07 at 6.09.15 AM.jpg|width=676,height=180!*

Our initial assumption here was that the playlist(s) had been corrupted or served incomplete, but we couldn’t find any evidence of that. Disney also reported no evidence of manifest irregularity at their origin, and that other CDNs were stable. Looking for aberrant behavior in the greater logs we can see that there was a spike in CLIENT_ABORT errors for a particular segment despite not having high transfer times. 

That segment was *disneyplus/event/2026/07/05/Formula_1_Carrera_GP_Gran_20260705_1783247413021/cmaf-cenc-ctr-7000K/186/14/56/02_914.mp4* which, looking at the video stream above, is the last segment requested before the out-of-sequence segments begin and the VPF occurs.

The theory: The playback error logged by Conviva is _*“PLAYBACK GEN_PLAYBACK_ERR 0000 "undefined: Fail to append buffer to video media source: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'traf')".*_ This would suggest that the player received a piece of corrupted media and was not able to assign it a track fragment to link audio and video. Talking to Disney directly they said it was possible that the Hive player, instead of aborting a segment it can’t decode, skips backward to a previously requested segment potentially as a failure mechanism trying to recover playback, but stalls and fails entirely. If this segment were somehow corrupted it would explain why the player failed.

 

If we trace the above request for that client/edge request ({*}70cfa4a7{*} - row 140 here: [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1oI1ZQ5xFTNOdA6ZVHm40p4-kZ4EcwbuFptOmiJEp6f8/edit?gid=1351354857#gid=1351354857])

summary: Intermittent curl: (52) Empty reply from server starting 3 July
description:
Customer reported there were intermittent curl: (52) Empty reply from server starting 3 July 07:30 UTC - 5 July. 
{code:java}
Curl test command:
curl "https://v16-kling-fdl.klingai.com/bs2/upload-ylab-stunt-sgp/muse/782702848764153904/VIDEO/20260703/1d36457dae8dafe3ff8364add1bfed72-6c1f6296-9680-4a6d-8a6b-53be356e76be.mp4?cacheKey=ChtzZWN1cml0eS5rbGluZy5tZXRhX2VuY3J5cHQSsAG3t5LBWW9-v8gRbqrClkrOmJSNeHoap_TU89EFWCkenMENz_uhfHUFbUfi79qijfU7CYcHKbDX90KTKz041w8RFewwXAVUQF2Ns60aSWS2oUZoDc63xSuNCCMzHf8r6pOTYSyxvXnVwEeAq3cvJWW5NZxW1NeSZwlAwq8IBBUrpOewnG5AYOLOUUvr49lLkmvhreJp1RYyWCHc3JjMp4_34bQJ1GbuV_vI8Q8j8Ab11hoSu4b9SEvlSFLKC9ylAQ2baCJIIiDjrY6lq48yY0sj4HvXZsl_jR-uA_3IdRPwz3j439CuRCgFMAE&x-kcdn-pid=112781&ksSecret=4f8ff7225f52e50b30dcbdca11f0a58e&ksTime=6a6efb2b" -o /dev/null -v {code}
*Current observation:*

1. Customer provided PCAP shows TCP 3-way handshake completes normally, followed by connection termination by Edge server via FIN, ACK (len=0) and RST flags. (PCAP file: s.pcap uploaded in SF case)
2. Checked ghost & cache logs across Edge IPs/CPCodes but unable to identify relevant log record, looks like the edge terminates the socket at the lower TLS/security layer prior to HTTP processing hence no standard access log entries found.
3. The issue was intermittent and not isolated to specific edge machine.
4. Upon testing, noticed request with auth parameters failed occasionally with curl error: (52) but when requests omit authentication parameters, the edge stably processes the request and returns 403 Forbidden.
5. Currently as of 6th July, the issue is not reproducible, customer requested for root cause identification

There was a SI opened for a recent release ([FF/releases/19008|https://release.akamai.com/ui/networks/FF/releases/19008]) and the issue doesn't happen since it's been rolled back.
 * Incident Viewer: [https://akamai.my.salesforce.com/apex/SC_SI_Viewer?sinumber=SI-00023902&source=salesforce]
 * SCM description : https://track.akamai.com/jira/browse/SCM-5189 
 * Rolled back feature [https://gripe.akamai.com/rollout/subnet.W.rollback-static-reference-id]

[RCA Document|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1q1_ESWmt3CfTEDMo_34rDGDWXri2Yq8m9uDAUis6VEk/edit?tab=t.0] for the SI doesn't look like it's related to this customer's issue but the issue timing matches with the SI.

Current log analysis doens't show any clue for the issue.

[https://docs.google.com/document/d/1CRV2NsBPD10PUNL0z282lUDlNJseVmsxjJ14VQS3ors/edit?tab=t.0] 

Customer provided pcap file but it's encrypted with limited information.
